full_judgment:
This is an application at the instance of the applicant petitioner for restoring states quo ante in the form of mandatory injunction against the opposite parties.
2. In the application, it has been stated inter alia, that on 11-7-1994, the RAJUK leased out a plot measuring 2.00 bighas of land appertaining to plot No. 69 under section 7, Uttara, Dhaka to the RAJUK Karmachari (Bohumukhi) Samabay Samiti in short 'the Samiti' for constructing a petrol pump by lease deed No. 7017 having received 'aka 1,98,387.10 for a period of 99 years. But the above mentioned Samiti found difficulty in installing a petrol pump at its own costs. Thereafter, the Samiti entered into a renewable sub-lease agreement with the petitioner on 8-9-1997 wherein it was provided that the petitioner would install petrol pump entirely at his own costs and peril having a life span of 25 years and accordingly, made over possession to the petitioner, and it is also stated that the period of lease period shall be counted from the commencement of the operation of the petrol pump and eventually, the petrol pump was started its operation on 9-3-2000 and the petitioner has been paying rent since 9-3-2000 while the petrol pump commenced its operation without any fail and the term of the lease agreement will be determined on 8-3-2028. After obtaining trade license for installation of petrol pump and observing all the formalities, the petitioner started operation of the petrol pump incurring huge investment. It is also contended that later on, the Samiti issued a notice to the petitioner for canceling the lease agreement and thus, the dispute between the petitioner and the Samiti has been crept. The lease agreement clearly depicted an arbitral clause to settle down the dispute through arbitration proceeding. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 119 of 2018 before the Court of learned Senior District Judge, Dhaka, Upon hearing, the learned Senior District Judge appointed two arbitrators and on the same date, he was pleased to direct the parties to maintain the status quo in respect of position and possession of the disputed premises. Despite the order of status quo, the Director (Administration), RAJUK issued a letter to the Police Commissioner on 13-10-2022 for deploying necessary police force on 16-10-2022 at 10-00 am in order to evict the instant petitioner from the Filing Station, M/s Cosmos Filing Station and Car Service Center. Thereafter, the petitioner was constrained to file a Writ Petition on 17-10- 2022 before this Court. Upon hearing, the Writ Court was pleased to issue Rule Nisi and stayed the operation of the letter for deploying the police force. Thereafter, RAJUK filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2916 of 2022 before the Appellate Division impugning the order of the High Court Division. Eventually, Hon’ble Chamber Judge was pleased to dismiss the CPLA as being not pressed and accordingly, the letter to the Police Commissioner for deploying the Police Force has lost its validity and, as such, the Rule has become infructuous. After that, on the application of the petitioner, the Rule was discharged as being infructuous.
3. Upon hearing, the parties and considering the backdrop of the case on 6-4-2023 this Court was pleased to direct the parties to the revisional application to maintain status quo in respect of dismantling the structure, position and possession of the disputed land as mentioned in the Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 119 of 2018 for a period of 2(two) months from date and also stated therein that the order no Further prayer of the extension shall be considered and with the consent of the parties this matter was fixed for hearing on 16- 5-20D at 2-00 pm on merit and the same has been duly intimated to Ms. Tanjina Sarwar, Director (Zone-3), RAJUK through e-mail, telephonic message and her contact No, 01713046932 and also by showing Lawyer Certificate as well. Moreover, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, Mr Asaduzzaman Monir being directed by this Court communicated to Ms. Tanjina Sarwar and Chairman, RAJUK for refraining from evicting the petitioner from disputed premises Being fully conversant as to the order of this Court, Ms. Tanjina Sarwar and Chairman, RAJUK did not pay heed to the solemn order of this Court and dismantled the structure of the disputed premises and dispossessed the petitioner from the disputed premises by creating a reign of terror with the assistance of the police force and after that, the disputed premises were totally sealed off and socked and, as such, the safety and security of the movable property and other assets amounting to crores of taka in the form of octane, diesel, other liquid incendiary mineral resources and other materials such as important financial records and daily receipts detailing the income and credit receipts and outstanding balances owed to different government bodies and other private parties and all these confidential business or financial records have remained locked and in an insecure state without supervision of the applicant inside the premises from 6-4-2023 and in the meantime, the applicant has suffered loss of Taka 10 crores and every day it incurs new damage.
4. In the above backdrop, finding no other alternative, the petitioner was constrained to file the aforesaid petition.
5. Mr Ajmalul Hossain QC, the learned Senior Counsel with Mr MK Rahman, Senior Advocate, Mr Mehedi Hasan Chowdhury, Senior Advocate and Mr ABM Siddiqur Rahman Khan, Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that being aware the order of this Court, the RAJUK officials did not pay heed to this and showing utter disregard to the order of this Court most illegally evicted the petitioner from the disputed premises and dismantled the structure and, as such, caused irreparable loss and injury to the petitioner and therefore, they are bound to restore the status quo ante otherwise, it will cause serious prejudice to the petitioner. Mr Hossain next submits that in a series of cases, it has been held that an order of status quo ante or mandatory injunction can be granted only to restore status quo and riot to establish a new set of things. Mr Hossain further submits that this Court may in its discretion grant an order of mandatory injunction to prevent the breach complained of, and also to compel performance of the requisite acts. Mr Hossain contends that, this Court has the jurisdiction to grant the order of mandatory injunction to preserve the status quo ante in order to rectify the gross tortuous wrongs committed by the opposite parties on 6-4-2023, which were committed in violation of the orders dated 13-12-2022 and 6-4-2023 passed by this Court in the instant Civil Revision.
6. Mr Hossain further submits that the opposite parties by their action has interfered with the order of this Court and flagrantly flouted the order Court of justice and, as such, presenting this Court with a fait accompli and therefore/ to cure the injustice admittedly caused, the Court may restore the .status quo ante by passing an order of mandatory injunction in ad interim form; otherwise, the image of the highest Court shall be disparaged in the estimation of the society. In support of his contentions Mr Hossain has referred to the cases reported in 45 DLR (AD) 762; 4 BLC (AD) 70; 35 DLR (AD) 42; 47 DLR (AD) 6; 7 DLR 606, 1994 BLD (AD) 195.
7. Per contra, Mr Md Sk, hid Morshed, the learned Senior Advocate along with Mrs Ayesha Morshed, the learned Advocate and Mr Niaz Morshed, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1-3 submits that the period of lease was terminated/determined on 08-9-1998 as per law, and, as such, the Clause-P of the sub-lease agreement lost its force. In support of his contention he has referred to the case reported in BCR (1987) (AD) 172. He further submits that Arbitration Miscellaneous Case is not maintainable in the eye of law; therefore, the order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka is liable to be set-aside. He next submits that eviction process was completed before at or before 10-30 pm and the order of the Court was communicated at 11-30 pm by the learned Deputy Attorney-General. Mr Morshed also submits that the Wirt Petition being No. 11894 of 2022 challenging the eviction proceeding was discharged earlier therefore, there is no bar to start eviction proceeding and since the eviction proceeding was completed before communication of the order of this Court, therefore, there is no apparent reason to pass any order of injunction in mandatory form. He finally submits that the Court cannot grant interim relief which is amounting to granting final report and, as such, he submits that the application is liable to be turned down in limine.
8. Heard the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates of both the parties. have meticulously and meaningfully read the relevant materials on record along with the applications, supplementary-affidavit to the application along with Annexures thereto and counter affidavit on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1-3 dated 4-4-2023 and also perused the convoluted question of law critically involved in this case in hand.
9. Admittedly, RAJUK leased out the disputed premises to RAJUK Karmochari Bohumukhi Samabaya Samity Limited on 13-7-1994. It is also admitted that the Samity sub-leased the premises by an unregistered deed authenticated by Notary Public on 8-9-1997 for a period of 25 years depicting the terms and conditions therein. By its letter dated 21-3-2020 President and Secretary of the Samity reiterated their commitment to the effect that the period of lease shall be determined upon the expiry of 25 years.
10. The learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 119 of 2018 was pleased to appoint two Arbitrators as per the arbitral clause as mentioned in the Clause-P to the sub-lease agreement. The petitioner challenged the aforesaid order solar it relates to appointment of two Arbitrators without giving the petitioner to nominate an Arbitrator of his choice but the Samity did not raise any question the validity of the order of the learned District Judge, The learned District Judge also passed an order of status quo in respect of disputed property till first sitting of the Arbitral Tribunal. This Court considering the backdrop of the case was pleased to pass the order of status quo in respect of dismantling the structure, possession and position of the disputed premises.
11. It appears from the record, the order of the Court has been communicated through telephonic conversation/electronic message/ showing result in the cause list/lawyer certificate. Moreover, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, Mr Md Asaduzzaman Monir tried his might and main to communicate the order by several attempts through official Telephone to Ms Tajina Samar, Director (Zone-3), RANK at 11-25 am but she did not pay heed to this Thereafter, the learned DAG communicates the order of this Court through telephonic and WhatsApp message but unfortunately, she did not care to carry out the order of this Court. Thereafter, at 12-30 am the learned DAG talked to the Chairman, RAJUK and who assured to carry out the order of this Court but eventually he did nothing positive.
12. In the instant revision Rule was issued upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 including Chairman, RAJUK and President of the aforesaid Samity. The RAJUK is well aware as to the effect that this Court is in sesin of the matter.
13. In the case of 35 DLR (Supra) it was held that mandatory injunction on interlocutory application may be granted to restore status quo and by invoking inherent power Court may issue mandatory injunction for demolition of structure. In 45 DLR (Supra) it was held that the mandatory injunction is available if dispossession had taken places during the pendency of the suit or during an order of ad interim injunction.
14. In 42 DLR (Supra) it was held that if a party to a suit does an act to bring about a change in the state of things existing at the date of the suit or just prior to that date, the Court may, in exercise of its inherent power, require the offending party, by issuing a temporary injunction in mandatory form to restore the status quo ante.
15. In 24 Halsbury's Laws of England (4th Edn.) pars 948, it is sated that a mandatory injunction can be granted on an interlocutory application as well as at the hearing, but, in the absence of special circumstances, it will not normally be granted. However, if the case is clear and one which the court thinks ought to be decided at once, or if the act done is a simple and summary one which can be easily remedied, or if the defendant attempts to steal a march on the plaintiff, such as where, on receipt of notice that an injunction is about to be applied for, the defendant hurries on the work in respect of which complaint is made so that when he receives notice of an interim injunction it is completed, a mandatory injunction will be granted on an interlocutory applications.
16. In the case of Dorab Cawasji Warden vs Coomi Sorab Warden at others reported in 1990(2) SCC 117, the Indian Supreme Court laid down the guidelines for granting Interlocutory Mandatory Injunctions. The relevant portion of the aforesaid judgment may read thus:
"The relief of interlocutory mandatory injunctions are thus granted generally to preserve or restore the status quo of the last non-contested status which preceded the pending controversy until the final hearing when full relief may be granted or to compel the undoing of those acts that have been illegally done or the restoration of that which was wrongfully taken from the party complaining. But since the granting of such an injunction to a party who fails or would fail to establish his right at the trial may cause great injustice or irreparable harm to the party against whom it was granted or alternatively not granting of it to a party who succeeds or would succeed may equally cause great injustice or irreparable harm, courts have evolved certain guidelines”
17. In the Case of Hammad Ahmed vs Abdul Majeed & others (Civil Appeal Nos. 3382-3383 of 2019, 9 July, 2019) the Indian Supreme Court while dealing with the issue whether art interim Mandatory Injunction can be granted in a suit, held to the effect:
"The balance of the case totally in favour of the applicant may persuade the court to grant an interim relief though it amounts to granting the final relief itself. Of course, such would be rare and exceptional cases. The court would grant such an interim relief only if satisfied that withholding of it would prick the conscience of the court and do violence to the sense of justice, resulting in injustice being perpetuated throughout the hearing, and at the end the court would not be able to vindicate the cause of justice. Obviously such would be rare cases accompanied by compelling circumstances, where the injury complained of is immediate and pressing and would cause extreme hardship. The conduct of the parties shall also have to be seen and the court may put the parties on such terms as may be prudent." The argument that under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of the Code, the Court has the jurisdiction to maintain the status of the parties on the date of filing of the suit or on the date of passing of the order but cannot direct the parties to do something which was not in existence at the time of filing of the suit, is not a general rule of universal application. The nature of the orders claimed by the Appellant are not passed ordinarily in a routine manner as the Plaintiff is required to have a case which should be of higher standard than mere prime facie case."
18. In the case of Babul Kanti Das vs Abul Hashem", reported in 47 DLR (AD) 6 it was observed—
"It does not appear from the facts and circumstances of the case that the matter is purely a concern between the private rights of two parties. The matter assumed a new character and it turned into a matter concerning public policy relating to administration of justice. This Court decided in the case of Abdul laid Munshi vs Abu Bakar Siddique, 35 DLR (AD) 42 at para 12 that If a party to a suit does an Act to bring about a change in the state of things existing at the date of the suit or just prior to that date, in Order to forestall a possible Order of the court, the Court may, in an appropriate case, in exercise of its inherent power, require the offending party, by issuing a temporary injunction in mandatory form to restore the status quo ante. "We held that this principle is in consonance with fair administration of justice and this power of making an Order of mandatory injunction on an interlocutory application may be exercised irrespective of the merits of the main case as it is one of the main concerns of a Court of Law to see that no one dares to interfere with the course of justice by presenting the Court with a fail accompli." In so holding we relied upon two English cases, namely, Daniel vs Ferguson (7891)2 Ch. 27 and Von feel vs Hornsey (1895) 2 Ch. 774 and also upon some decisions of the then Dhaka High Court. The present case falls squarely within the perimeter of the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42 and we find that the trial Court acted judiciously in passing the temporary and mandatory injunctions,"
19. In Subrata Roy Sahara vs Union of India, (2014) 8 SCC 470, para 185.2 it was held that-
"Disobedience of orders of a court strikes at the very root of the rule of law on which the judicial system rests. Judicial orders are bound to be obeyed at all costs. Howsoever grave the effect may be, is no answer for non-compliance of a judicial order. Judicial orders cannot be permitted to be circumvented. In exercise of the contempt jurisdiction, courts have the power to enforce compliance of judicial orders, and also, the power to punish for contempt.
20. In ET Sunup vs CA SS Employees Assn., (20)4) 8 SCC 683, para 16 it was held that-
"It has become a tendency with the government officers to somehow or the other circumvent the orders of court and try to take recourse to one justification or other. This shows complete lack of grace in accepting the orders of the Court. This tendency of undermining the Court's order cannot be countenanced. The Supreme Court time and again has emphasized that in a democracy the role of the court cannot be subservient to administrative fiat. The executive and legislature have to work within the constitutional framework and the judiciary has been given the role of watchdog to keep the legislature and executive within check".
<u>21. It appears that RAJUK officials are not respectful to the Court and they are completely oblivious as to their constitutional and legal obligation. We should not forget we are bound by law irrespective of our official post and position, subordinate to law and answerable to law whoever we may be. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that it is an appropriate case to grant interim relief otherwise, it would prick the conscience of the Court and do violence of justice and thereby injustice will be perpetuated and the delinquent officers will encourage to show thumbs up to the solemn order of the Court and it will further cause serious prejudice to the petitioner, In this respect whether petitioner is a year to year lessee or whether the disputed sub-lease creates any periodical lease or whether lease period has been expired these issues are immaterial in respect of disposing of this application. It cannot be denied that by exhausting due process the RAJUK or the Samiti may recover the possession of the disputed premises. So that as it may, if the Court's order is not obeyed by the responsible officers of the Government, it will surely disparage the position of the Court in the estimation of the people of the Country and thereby crying for establishing rule of law will be meaningless.</u>
<u>22. Obligation means every duty enforceable by law The opposite party flouted the order of Status quo as such to prevent breach of obligation existing in favour of the petitioner applicant mandatory injunction in interim form may be passed to do justice and undo injustice by invoking inherent power of the Court.</u>
23. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the exceptional circumstances especially the balance of the case in favour of the applicant petitioner persuades this Court to grant interim relief though it appears to granting final relief itself so that in future nobody dares to show disobedience to the Court's order.
24. Accordingly, the Chairman, RAJUK and Ms Tajina Sarwar. Director (Zone-3), RAJUK are hereby directed to hand over peaceful possession of the disputed premises to the petitioner after removing or demolishing the illegal and unauthorized construction i.e. tin-sheds walls, fences and boundaries and barriers so that ingress and outgress to the Filling Station becomes smooth and uninterrupted.
25. The concerned authority of DESCO and WASA is also directed to reconnect the electricity and water lines in the disputed premises of the applicant-petitioners and in this respect RAJUK Chairman shall take appropriate step to that end.
26. The Chairman and Director Ms Tajina Sarwar, Director (Zone-3) RAJUK are directed to comply with the order of this Court within 48 hours from the date of receipt of the copy of this order positively without any fail and accordingly, they will submit affidavit-of-compliance to that effect.
27. And thus, the application for status quo ante in the form of mandatory injunction is disposed of.
28. Let the application for drawing up violation proceeding against Chairman, RAJUK and others be kept with the record, it will come up in the cause list on 14-5-2023 for hearing. In order to dispose of the said application, the appearance of the Chairman and Ms. Tajina Sarwar, Director (Zone-3), RAJUK are sine qua non and therefore. They are directed to remain present in person before this Court on 14-5-2023 at 10-30 am positively.
Let a copy of the order be transmitted to the all concern at once for compliance of the direction of this Court through FAX, e-mail and as usual method of services.
End.

Tanjib-ul-Alam, with Mustafizur Rahman Khan with Abul Kalam Azad And with Karishma Jahan and Sumaiya Ifrit Binte Ahmed, Advocates---------For the Petitioners
 AM Aminuddin, Attorney General with Mohammad Bakiruddin Bhuiyan, Advocate----------For the Respondent No.1

full_judgment:
Md Khasruzzaman, J: On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, Rule Nisi has been issued in the following term:
"Let Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the office order bearing Memo No. 53.03.0000.036.01.034.21,145 dated 11-2-2021 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) stating that the Board of Directors of Delta Life Insurance Company Limited is suspended for a period of 4(four) months and as administrator appointed under section 95 of the Insurance Act, 2010 on the purported ground that the affairs of petitioner No.1 is being carried in a mariner likely to be prejudicial to the interest of the holders of its insurance policies, should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect."
2. At the time of issuance of the aforesaid Rule Nisi, this Court also directed the parties to maintain status-quo in respect of the operation of the impugned office order bearing Memo No.53.03.0000,036.01.034-21-145 dated 11-2-2021 (Annexure-A to the writ petition).
3. Facts, necessary for disposal of the Rule Nisi, in short, are as follows:
That Delta Lite Insurance Company Limited, hereinafter referred to as Delta Life, is a public limited company incorporated in 1986 under the Companies Act, 1913 and is engaged in the business of providing life insurance. It serves over 16 lac customers and is a major employer in Bangladesh with more than 20,000 field force and employees. Delta Life offers financial protection of the country through a mix of traditional and innovative products such as individual and group life insurance policies, health insurance and gono grameen bima. It is stated in the writ petition that Delta Life, under the guidance of its Board of Directors, always maintains strict corporate governance and transparency and its statutory auditors are always top tier audit firms of Bangladesh. For instances the company was audited by SF Ahmed & Co. MJ Abed in Hoda Vasi Chowdhury & Co. in respect of financial years of 2013 to 2015, 2016 to 2018 and 2019 respectively.
4. It also undertakes regular audits as prescribed by the respondent No.2 from time to time. As per section 29 of the insurance Act, 2010, respondent No.2 decided to audit the management expenses and related matters along with authentication/justification of business operation of all life insurers in Bangladesh. Accordingly, M/s Howladar Yunus & Co. was appointed as special auditors to perform the special audit for the years of 2015, 2016 & 2017 of the petitioner company on 12-2-2019 and the said audit firm after conclusion of the audit submitted a report to the respondent No.2 on 8-8-2019 (Annexures-B and B-1 respectively to the writ pennon). But, without exhausting steps to be taken under section 51 of the Insurance Act, 2010 following the aforesaid special audit, respondent No.2 being instigated by the incumbent Chairman (respondent No. 3), appointed another audit firm namely, M/s Fames & R vide letter bearing reference No.53.03.0000.71.27.019.19.154 dated 15-10-2019, to carry out investigation under section 48 of the Insurance Ad, 2010(Annexure-C to the writ petition) for the years of 2015 to 2018. As per section 48(3) of the Insurance Act, 2010 the Investigator is required to submit report on investigation within 7(seven) working days but M/s Fames and R submitted a vague report on 14-1-2021 after a prolonged period of one year and three months with some general observations out of terms of reference. It is stated that from the commencement of the tenure of the respondent No.3 as a Member of IDRA and after he was made as the Chairman of respondent No.2, Delta Life has been subjected to series of administrative and regulatory measures including delaying the grant of approval of extension of the tenure of the petitioner No..3 and subsequently rejecting the "renewal of appointment application of the petitioner No.3 as CEO of Delta Life and delaying the grant of approval of actuarial basis and eventually revising actuarial basis proposed by the Actuary appointed by Delta Life and imposing penalties for non-compliance of various sections of the Insurance Act, 2010 with the sole purpose of personal ratification.
5. All the above actions and inactions were challenged by Delta Life in various writ petitions and obtained Rules Nisi which have been annexed as Annexures-D to D-4 to the writ petition. Meanwhile, on 13-11-2020 and 14-11-2020, the respondent No.3 contacted an Officer of Delta Life and demanded illegal gratification threatening that if his demands are not met Delta Life will be subjected to further fines and drastic action in respect of appointment of an Administrator will be taken. It is stated that the illegal demands of the respondent No.3 was captured on tape record on 14-11-2020 by the Officer of Delta Life and a transcript thereof has been supplied to ACC for in and taking appropriate actions and further a complaint was lodged with the ACC. On the delay of ACC in commencing the investigation and in the face of continuous harassment by respondent No.3, Delta Life was constrained to file Writ Petition No. 1163 of 2021 and obtained Rule Nisi and direction upon the ACC to dispose of the application of Delta Life within a period of thirty days.
6. However, on the basis of the reports submitted by M/s Howladar Yunus Co and Arils Fames i.e. Co. on 18-1-2071 the respondent No.2 issued notice vide Memo No. 53.03. 0000.036.01.034.21.132 (Annexure-G to the writ petition) directing Delta Life to show cause within 7(Seven) days from the date of receipt of the letter as to why the Board of Directors of Delta Life should not be suspended for a period of 4(four) months and why an administrator shall not be appointed under section 95 of the Insurance Act, 2010. However, upon an application being filed by Delta Life for adjournments the hearing of the show cause notice was shifted to 11-30 am on 11-2-2021. It is stated that Delta Life challenging the show cause notice dated I R-1-2021(Annexure-G) had filed Writ Petition No. 1687 of 2021 and mentioned the same before the Court prior to commencement of the hearing on the show cause notice to appear on the next day for motion hearing and the Court was pleased to allow the prayer. Mr Tanjib-ul-Alam with Mr Mustafizur Rahman Khan and Ms. Karishma Jahan, learned Advocates being authorized by Delta Life to represent them in the hearing of the show cause notice subsequently entered the zoom link provided by respondent No.2 at about 11-30 am and they were allowed to join the meeting at about 11-37 am and right after logging in, Mr Tanjib-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate informed the respondent Nos. 3 and 5 i.e. the Chairman and Member( Law) who were present at the zoom meeting to attend the hearing under section 95 that Writ Petition No. 1687 of 2021 has been mentioned before Court No.35(A) and the same will appear on 14-2-2021 for motion hearing and accordingly, sought for adjournment of the hearing of the show cause notice till hearing the writ petition by the said Bench of the High Court Division. Mr Imtiaz Farooq, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.2 was also present as one of the participants in the zoom meeting. Respondent No.3 suddenly became agitated and started shouting stating that 'we will hear only the management of Delta Life and no lawyer should be allowed to speak'. However, before the learned lawyers for Delta Life could say anything on the matter of hearing under section 95, the respondent No3 disconnected the zoom link. Although the Board Members including the petitioner Nos. 2 and 5 and Mr Saif Khondoker were waiting to log in the meeting and even though petitioner No3 was present in the meeting but without providing any opportunity to the petitioner No.3, either to seek adjournment or to reply to the show cause notice, within approximately 5 minutes of commencement of the said meeting, respondent Nos. 2 and/or 3 abruptly ended the hearing at 11-44 am In the such circumstances, Delta Life served a hard copy of the reply to the show cause notice to the respondent Not and also submitted reply to show cause notice by e-mail dated 11-2-2021 at 1-34 pm (Annexure-H to the writ petition).
7. However, even before a reply was e-mailed and within less than an hour of disconnecting the zoom link, i.e. by 12-29 pm, online newspaper Insurance Bd. reported that an administrator will be appointed in Delta Life identifying the respondent No.6 as the administrator. Ultimately at 3-18 pm on 11-2-202] Delta Life was served with the impugned order dated 11-2-2021 vide Annexure-A to the writ petition.
8. Subsequently, on further probe by senior Reporter of Samakal with Moinul Islam, Member (Admin) of IDRA over phone it was discovered that Mr Moinul Islam was not aware of the issuance of the impugned order which was reported in Samakal on 12-2-2021. (Annexures-J and J-1 respectively to the writ petition) and, as such, the impugned decision passed by the respondent No.2 is coram non judice and, as such, without any lawful authority and of no legal effect.
9. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, challenging the impugned order dated 11-2-2021 the petitioners filed the present writ petition and obtained Rule Nisi and status-quo in the manner as stated above on 15-2-2021.
10. Subsequently, upon an application being filed by the petitioners for staying operation of the impugned order, this Court by order dated 23-2-2021 modified the status-quo order dated 15-2-2021 into an order of injunction restraining the respondent No.6 from taking any official decision other than to perform routine work and business assigned in Annexure-A to the writ petition.
11. Challenging the aforesaid order dated 23-2-2021, the respondent Nos. 2 and 6 filed Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 714 of 2021 and 715 of 2021 before the Appellate Division and the aforesaid two civil petitions for leave to appeal were dismissed on 18-3-2021 with a direction upon this Bench to hear and dispose of the Rule Nisi expeditiously. Accordingly, this Bench has posted the Rule Nisi in the list for hearing.
12. During the pendency of the hearing of the Rule Nisi, the respondent No.2 has issued three orders all dated 9-6-2021 vide Memo No.53.03.0000.036.01.034.21.182 ex tending the suspension of the Board of Directors of Delta Life for an indefinite period (Annexure-M to the application), vide Memo No. 53.03.0000, 036.01.034.21.183 removing the respondent No.6 as the Administrator of Delta Life (Annexure-M-1 to the application) and vide Memo No.53.03.0000.036.01.034.21.184 appointing Professor Md Rafiqul Islam, joint Secretary (Retd.) as the new Administrator of Delta Life (Annexure-M-2 to the application). As such, the petitioners filed an application for addition of party of Professor Md Rafiqul Islam, Joint Secretary (Retired) as respondent No. 7 and also prayed for issuance of supplementary Rule Nisi in the writ petition, whereupon this Court on 15-9-2021 allowed the application upon adding the applicant as respondent No. 1 and issued supplementary Rule Nisi in the following term:
"Let a supplementary Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo No.53,03.0000.036.01,03421,182 dated  9-6- 2021 issued by the respondent N0.2 (Annexure-M to the application) extending the suspension of the Board of Directors of Delta Life insurance Company Limited for an indefinite period and the Memo No33,03.0000.036.01.03421,184 dated 9-6-2021 (Annexure-M-2 to the application) appointing the added respondent No.7 as Administrator should not be declared to have been issued without any lawful authority and are of no legal effect"
13. But the writ petitioners are filing writ petitions one after another to frustrate the purpose of the respondents to protect the interest of the policy-holders from the illegal act of the writ petitioners company which is prejudicial to the interest of the policy-holders and, as such, he has prayed for discharging the Rule Nisi with cost.
41. Heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of their respective parties and on perusal of the writ petition, supplementary affidavits thereof, affidavits-in-opposition, supplementary affidavits-in-opposition filed by the learned Advocates on behalf of their respective parties and all annexures annexed thereto.
42. It appears from the impugned order that for the purpose of ascertaining as to whether the interests of the policy-holders is being protected by the writ petitioners company, on 12-2-2019 the respondent No.2 appointed an audit firm namely-M/s Hawlader Yunus & Co. to conduct special audit in respect of management expenses of Delta Life Insurance Company Limited, who after conclusion of audit, submitted its special audit report on 14-7-2019 raising some objections against Delta Life. Thereafter, on 6-10-2019 the respondent No.2 appointed another audit firm namely M/s Fames & R under section 48(1) of the IDRA Act, 2010 to investigate the audit of the writ petitioners company and this firm submitted its investigation report long after on 14-1-2021.
43. It further appears that on the basis of the said two reports the respondent No.2 issued show cause notice dated 18-1-2021 vide Annexure-G to the writ petition upon Delta Life requesting to submit reply within 7(seven) working days as to why the Board of Directors of Delta Life should not be suspended appointing an Administrator in Delta Life under section 95 of the Insurance Act, 2010. By the said show cause notice the writ petitioners were also requested to send reply to show cause by e-mail or by post within 31-1-2021 at 11-30 am or to give statement joining at the meeting using zoom link on the date and time as mentioned above or to appear in person before the office of the authority to give reply.
44. However, pursuant to the show cause notice Delta Life filed application seeking adjournment and, as such, the hearing of the show cause notice was shifted on 11-2-2021 at 11-30 am.
45. Ultimately, the respondent No.2 has passed the impugned order suspending the Board of Directors of Delta Life and appointing an Administrator of Delta Life to manage the affairs of the company in accordance with law vide Annexure-A to the writ petition.
46. The learned Advocates for the writ respondents in a body submit that to ascertain as to whether the company is protecting the interest of the policy-holders in carrying on their insurance business, the authority conducted audit by the audit firms as mentioned above and on the basis of the reports of the auditors, the authority has come to believe with apprehension that the petitioners are carrying their business against the interest of the policy-holders and, as such, upon exhausting all formalities the authority has passed the impugned order which is in full compliance of the provision of section 95 of the Insurance Act, 2010.
47. The petitioners stated in the writ petition that pursuant to the show cause notice dated 18-1-2021 the writ petitioners and the legal representatives of the petitioners attended at the zoom meeting on 11-2-2021 which commenced at 11-37 am but before they could say anything on the show cause notice the respondent No.3 disconnected the zoom link at 11-44 am and ultimately within a very short time the respondent No.2 passed the impugned order dated 11-2-2021 with undue haste.
48. From the facts and circumstances of the case and from the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocates on both the sides, it appears that the points as raised in this Rule Nisi to determine by this Bench are that whether the impugned order dated 11-2-2021 is in compliance of the provision of section 95 of the Insurance Act and whether the principle of natural justice as is required to be followed before passing any order under section 95 of the Insurance Act, 2010 or it has been violated and also whether the impugned order suffers from coram non judice and also whether the writ petitioners had the forum of review under section 32 of IDRA Act, 2010 and also whether the impugned decision is the result of malafide and malice in law.
49. In this respect, first of all we are to see the provision of section 95(1) of the Insurance Act, 2010, which reads as follows:
"95. Appointment of Administrator for management of insurance business. (1) If at any time the Authority has reason to believe that an insurer carrying on insurance business is acting in a manner likely to be prejudicial to the interest of holders of insurance policies or failing to fulfill the solvency margin requirements, in this case, it may after giving opportunity to the insurer to be heard, suspend the Board of Directors and appoint an Administrator to manage the affairs of the insurer under the direction and control of the Authority."
50. On reading the aforesaid provision of law, it appears that the provision of section 95 of the Insurance Act has two pre-conditions that before suspending the Board of Directors and appointing an Administrator to manage the affairs of the company, the authority has to hove reasons to believe that an insurer carrying on insurance business is acting in a manner likely to be prejudicial to the interest of policy-holders or failing to fulfill the margin requirements and if that be so, then the authority must give opportunity to the insurer to be heard.
51. In the instant case, on perusal of the impugned order it appears that the authority has stated four grounds in the impugned order to prove that it had apprehension that the writ petitioners were acting against the interests of the policy-holders and thereby tried to show that the interests of the policy-holders are not protected in the hands of the writ petitioners. But on perusal of the grounds of the impugned order and the facts and circumstances of the case we do not find any such reason or materials on the same to come to the believe that the writ petitioners are carrying on their insurance business in a manner likely to be prejudicial to the interest of the policy-holders.
52. It is to be mentioned that in respect of ground No.1 i.e. failure of the writ petitioners company to make payment of Tax payable at source, the learned Advocate for the writ petitioners submits that the authority i.e. IDRA has got no authority under the law to give direction or to take steps in respect of realization of the VAT and Tax rather if there is any failure on the same on the part of the writ petitioners then another authority is there under the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984. In respect of the power of the Authority on the point of VAT, Mr Tanjib-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate for the writ petitioners by producing a photocopy of the certified copy of the judgment and order dated 18-11-2021 passed in Writ Petition No. 6035 of 2021 submits that the High Court Division in the said judgment made the Rule Nisi absolute holding that Authority has got no such power to realize or direct the company to pay VAT payable at source and as such the learned Advocate submits that the Authority has no jurisdiction to take the aforesaid point into consideration as a ground for passing the impugned order and, as such, the impugned order is liable to be set-aside.
53. Moreover, on the perusal of the impugned order along with the show cause notice basing which the impugned order has been passed it appears that the impugned order contains four reasons, although the same do not attract the requirement of section 95, but the show cause notice following which the impugned order has been passed does not contain any of such reasons.
54. The learned Advocates for the writ petitioners submit that where a statute requires reason to be given and failure to give reason in the show cause notice will render the decision liable to be set-aside and fair justice demands procedural safeguards as enunciated in law. In the present case, section 95 of the Act requires opportunity of hearing is to be given before passing the impugned order but without giving that opportunity the respondent No.2 has passed the impugned order which is liable to be set-aside as submitted by the learned Advocates for the writ petitioners. In this respect, the settled principles for fair procedure are that before taking any action against a man the authority should give him notice of the case and afford him fair opportunity to answer the case against him and to put his own case. This view finds support in the case of Sk. Ali Ahmed vs Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, 40 DLR (AD) 170, wherein it has been held as follows:
"As to the question whether the appellant was entitled to a show cause notice/hearing before the decision to cancel his license was taken the High Court Division took the view that there is no such requirement under the Arms Act nor can such a requirement he imported into the statute because of the sensitive nature of the subject matter. This view seems to find support from some decisions in the Indian. Jurisdiction (vide AIR 1956 Calcutta 96, AIR 1954 Rajasthan 264). It must, however, be pointed out that there is a long line of decisions from the Pakistan Jurisdiction, (The University of Dacca vs Zakir Ahmed, PLD 1965 SC 90 = 16 DLR (SC) 722) which have consistently taken the view that in all proceedings by whomsoever held, whether judicial or administrative, the principles of natural justice have to be observed if the proceedings might result in consequences affecting "the person or property or other right of the parties concerned". This rule applies even though there may be no positive words in the statute or legal document whereby the power is vested to take such proceedings, for, in such cases this requirement is to be implied into it as the minimum requirement of fairness."
<u>55. It is also settled that the authority while issuing show cause notice must mention the grounds or part of the real grounds of the proposed action or mention one ground but action is taken on some other grounds in that case the notice suffers from vagueness. Again if one action is proposed in the notice and a different action is taken in the order, the principles of natural justice are violated. This view finds support in the case of Bangladesh Telecom Ltd vs BTTB, 48 DLR (AD) 20, wherein it has been held in paragraph No.31 as follows: "We have held earlier that although the impugned letter of cancellation is in respect of the Agreement, it is in effect a revocation of the licence. Mr TH Khan insistently argued that it was cancellation of a commercial contract for which no show cause notice was necessary. The licence was not revoked, but it was rendered ineffective as a consequence of cancellation of the Agreement, he argues. Under section 8 of</u>
<u>the Telegraph Act a licence can only be revoked, not made ineffective. The impugned letter of cancellation can only mean revocation of licence, nothing else. A licence is a privilege created in favour of the licensee and unless the statute excludes the operation of the principle of natural justice, a show cause notice is a must before revocation of the license."</u>
56. In the said decision it has further been held in paragraph No. 32 as follows:
"It is not enough to issue a show cause notice. In order to be valid it must be a meaningful one. The High Court Division failed to read the notice, although it is apparent that it does not fulfill the requirements of a meaningful and therefore valid show cause notice. When it is agreed on all hands that without the PSTN connection the cellular radio telephone system is not operational yet, it is idle to talk about violation of clause 17. BTUs transfer of its shares to Watership Ltd. is sub-judice and cannot be the basis of cancellation. Apart from these two allegations, no facts have been made out in the show cause notice to attract the violation of clauses 3, 6, 7, 9 and 23 of the Agreement. An attempt has been made by BTTB to furnish some facts in its affidavit-in-opposition and Mr TH Khan has also verbally submitted some facts, but we are unable to entertain them, as the facts which constitute the valid basis of cancellation have to be alleged in the show cause notice itself and cannot be supplemented by fresh facts in affidavit. As Krishna lyer, J. aptly put in the case of Mohinder Singh vs Chief Election Commissioner, AIR 1978 SC 851, orders are not like old wine getting better on being older".
<u>57. Further, procedural safeguards are essential elements of rule of law. The principles of natural justice are of two categories i.e. a man cannot be condemned unheard and a man cannot be the judge in his own cause.</u>
58. As we have already found from the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the writ petitioners that the writ petitioners stated in the writ petition that there so many allegations against the incumbent Chairman of Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority (IDRA) i.e. respondent No.3 is a former employee of Delta Life being employed between 8-12-1998 to 31-8-2001 and again from 26-3-2003 to 24-10-2005 and since his taking over of the office of respondent No.2 as Chairman, Delta Life has been facing difficulties and obstacles in the course of managements with IRDA on various scores with the sole purpose to extract personal gratification and settle personal score by the respondent No.3 and that complaints alleging corruption and demand for illegal gratification against respondent No.3 were filed with the Anti-Corruption Commission and accordingly, in the reply dated 10-2-2021 to the show cause notice (Annexure-H to the writ petition), the writ petitioners had sought that under the circumstances, Dr. M. Mosharraf Hossain FCA ought to have recused himself from the hearing to the show cause on the ground that the writ petitioners have so many allegations against the respondent No.3 who before taking over the office of the respondent No.2 was an employee of Delta Life being employed for the period mentioned above and also on the ground that no man should be a judge in their own cause which is one of the criterion of the principles of natural justice. But, without giving any heed to the same and rather being present in the hearing at the zoom meeting on 11-2-2021 or at the meeting to take decision to pass the impugned order as claimed by the petitioners, the respondent No.3 and the authority have violated the principles of natural justice which is nothing but malafide and malice in law.
59. The authority could have considered the prayer on the ground that no man should be a judge in his own cause but without considering the same, the respondent No.3 all along present in the zoom meeting to attend the hearing to the show cause notice. This is nothing but malafide and malice in law and also violation of the principle of natural justice.
<u>60. The settled principle is that no man should be judge in his own case. With a view to strengthening public confidence, it was developed into a jurisdictional principle that no one having any interest or bias in respect of any matter is competent to take part in the decision making relating to that matter. It was said that it is of fundamental importance that justice should not only be done, but should manifestly and undoubtedly be seen to be done.</u>
61. We have also found that the respondent No,3 has passed the impugned order with malafide intention along with ulterior motive to harass the writ petitioners because the authority at the time of passing the impugned order based on the four grounds although the same do not fulfill the requirements as required under section 95 of the insurance Act, but the show cause notice does not contain any of the grounds and, as such, without furnishing a copy of the show cause notice along with the grounds on which the impugned order has been passed and without affording opportunity of being heard on the said grounds, the same is violation of the principles of natural justice and, as such, the learned Advocate for the petitioners prays that the impugned order is liable to be set-aside as the same has been passed with malafide intention only to harass the writ petitioners and, as such, the same be hold that it is suffering from malice in law. In this regard, the learned Advocates for the writ petitioners relied on the decision in the case of Dr. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, 33 DLR (AD) 201.
62. It is also the settled principle that notice and hearing are to be given before the decision is taken. There may be several stages before the decision is taken. Fairness demands an opportunity of hearing. What is the effect of failure to give a fair hearing and will a decision in breach of audi alterarn partem be void or voidable? In this respect reliance can be made in the case of Ridge vs Baldwin, in (1964) AC 40 wherein the majority held that the failure of fair hearing rendered the dismissal of the Chief Constable void. In the case of Orissa vs Binapani, 1967 SC 1269 and Shreeram Durga Prasad vs Settlement Commission, (1989) 1 SCC 628, it has been observed that generally the Court held a decision in violation of audi alteram partem to be void and a nullity.
<u>63. We are of the view that audi alterarn partem is a part of the procedural due process guaranteed by Article 31 of the Constitution and in all cases violation of its renders the decision void under Article 31 of the Constitution.</u>
<u>64. On comparison of the show cause notice and the impugned order we do not find that the show cause notice contained any of such grounds basing upon which the impugned order has been passed. In this score also the principle of natural justice has been violated.</u>
65. Moreover, 'the allegations made in paragraph-18 of the writ petition against the respondent No.3 that respondent No.3 disconnected the zoom link provided to the petitioners and he did not give the opportunity to say anything on the show cause notice passed the impugned order within approximately 5 minutes of commencement of the meeting ended hearing' has not been denied by the respondent authority by affidavit-in opposition but subsequently it has been developed and, as such, it can easily be presumed that they have accepted the allegations made against respondent No. 2 and 3 which has been supported in the case of Naseem Bono 7.16 LIP, AIR 1993 SC 2592 wherein it has been held that the statements made in the writ petition and allegations made against the Respondent-authorities are deemed to have been admitted by the respondent authority and, as such, it can be said that principles of natural justice have been violated by the respondent authority which rendered the impugned decision void and a nullity
<u>66. Since the principles of natural justice as required under section 95 of the Insurance Act has been violated, we are of the view that the impugned order has been passed with malafide intention and the same is malice in law for which the impugned order is required to be interfered with.</u>
67. As such we are of the view that the authority did not comply with the requirement as prescribed in section 95 of the Insurance Act, 2010 before passing the impugned order.
68. In respect of whether the impugned decision suffers from coral?' non judice, we are of the view that since the respondent No.5 filed affidavit-in-opposition denying the claim of the writ petitioner that the respondent No. 5 was not present at the time of meeting and taking decision to pass the impugned order rather he stated that he was all along present in the zoom meeting and at the time of passing the impugned order and, as such, the same does not call for any discussion under the judicial review.
69. In respect of the question of maintain-ability of the writ petition as submitted by the learned Advocates for the respondents that the writ petitioners could at best file a review application under section 32 of the Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority Act, 2010, we need to go through the provision of section 32 of the said Act which reads as follows:
"32. Review.—(1) Any person or organization aggrieved by an order passed by the Chairman or any Member or any Officer under this Act may apply for review of that order within the time prescribed by regulation in prescribed form and subject to payment of prescribed fee, and the order of the Authority upon this review application shall be final."
<u>70. The law provides that review is to be filed against any order passed under the Insurance Development and Regulatory Authority Act, 2010 not the Insurance Act, 2010. In the present case, admittedly the impugned order has been passed by the Authority under section 95 of the Insurance Act, 2010 not under the IDRA Act, 2010 and, as such, question of filing review under section 32 of the IDRA Act does not arise at all. So the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the respondents on this score are not tenable in the eye of law.</u>
71. In view of the reasons and discussions made above, we find force in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the writ petitioners and, as such, the Rule Nisi along with the supplementary Rule Nisi is liable to be made absolute.
72. In the result, the Rule Nisi and the supplementary Rule Nisi are made absolute and the office order bearing Memo No.53. 03.0000.036.01.034.21.145 dated 11-2-2021 (Annexure-A to the writ petition) and the impugned Memo No.53.03.0000.036.01.034.21. 182 dated 9-6-2021 issued by the respondent No.2 (Annexure-M to the application) extending the suspension of the Board of Directors of Delta Life Insurance Company Limited for an indefinite period and the Memo No. 53.03.0000.036.01.03421.184 dated 9-6-2021 (Anrtexure-M-2 to the application) appointing the added respondent No.7 as Administrator are declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect.
73. The ad-intuit orders of status-quo and injunction granted earlier are hereby vacated.
There will be no order as to cost.
End.

None Appears ------------------ For the Opposite Parties.

full_judgment:
At the instance of the petitioners, the Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-4-1999 (decree being drawn on 10-5-1999) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 133 of 1997 allowing the appeal and decreeing the suit after reversing the judgment and decree dated 5-5- 1997 (decreeing being drawn on 25-5-1997) passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge the joint District Jude), 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 412 of 1990/67 of 1988 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are inter alma that the opposite party being plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 67 of 1988 before the Court of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge presently Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 412 of 1990 impleading the opposite parties as defendants for declaration of title in the suit land as mentioned in the schedule to the plaint contending inter alia, that the land measuring 1.58 acres in the plot Nos. 1859, 1782 and 1864 of CS Khatian No. 505 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 742 of Mouza Nandipara, Police Station-Demra (previous Tejgaon) Dhaka belonged to one Guru Dayal Mondol as the owner having recorded his name in CS Khatian and he was in possession of the suit land until his death. Guru Dayal Mondol died leaving behind his son, Surendra Mondol as his only heir to inherit his estate. Surendra Mondol inherited total 2.20 acres of land after mutual partition among his ancestors. Surendra Mondol died leaving behind his widow Makhani Bewa and also a minor daughter Robi Soria and a minor son Ratan Mondol alias Ratan. Under the Hindu Succession Law Makhani Bewa and Robi Sona were not entitled to inherit the properties as legal heirs but they had rights for enjoyment of the suit property.
3. For the necessity of repayment of loan, maintenance and purchasing land in other place, Makhani Bewa for herself and on behalf of the minor daughter, Robi Sona and Minor son, Ratan transferred their right, title and interest in 1.81 acres of land by 3 (three) separate deeds which were executed and registered on 6-2-1970 and 12-2-1970 to one Hasina Warcla Chowdhary, wife of Abul Kashem Md Enayatullah Chowdhury. Makhani Bewa was not competent to transfer the property on behalf of her minor son and daughter; therefore, the said transfer was absolutely illegal.
4. Robin Sona got married after attaining majority and she has been living with her husband for 5/7 years. Makhani Bewa died leaving behind Robi Sona and Ratan. After attaining majority, Ratan claimed ownership of the suit land while Ratan Mondol was in possession of the suit land, on 9-3-1987, he sold 1.58 acres of land in favour of the opposite party by executing and registering sale deed on 9-3-1987 ignoring the sale deeds executed and registered by Makhani Bewa (Ratan's mother) on 6-2-1970 and 12-2-1970. The plaintiff-opposite party filed a suit for declaration of title for the land measuring 1.58 acres by the sale deed dated 9-3-1987. By amending the plaint, the opposite party stated that he sold out 0.34 acres of land from plot No. 1782 and therefore, he had 1.24 acres of land.
5. The petitioner Nos. 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10 and 11 and the petitioner Nos. 2 and 7 jointly filed two separate written statements denying the material allegations as set out in the plaint contending, inter alga, that the suit is false and fraudulent and the plaintiff has got no cause of action. The plaintiff has got no title and possession in the suit land and the suit is not maintainable since, the suit is undervalued and unless ad valurem court fees on the market value of the suit land is paid. The suit should not be allowed to proceed further; hence, the suit is barred by the principle of waiver, estoppels and acquiescence and also barred by the limitation; therefore, the opposite party is not entitled to get any relief.
6. It has also been stated therein that the total 14.74 acres of land including the suit land was originally owned jointly by Tilab Matobbor 4 annas of total land, Slily Charan 4 annas, Hari Charan Mondol 4 annas, Guru Dayal Mondol 2 annas and Hari Dayal Mondol 2 annas of the total land. They may amicably partition of the suit land along with other lands and accordingly, they became the absolute owners and possessors of their respective shares in the land.
7. While the aforesaid Guru Doyal Mondol was an absolute owner of the suit land and he died leaving behind Surendra Mondol as his only heir. Surendra Mondol by mutual partition with his co-sharers got the suit land in previous Mouza No. 317 corresponding to present Mouza No. 123 at Nandipara, previous Khatian No. 505 present Khatian No. 2196, previous dag No. 1859 corresponding to present dag No. 3946 measuring 47 decimals of land, previous dag No. 1864 corresponding to the present dag No. 400 measuring 44 decimals of land; previous dag No 1782 corresponding to the present dag No. 3936 and 3932 measuring 67 decimals of land and other properties. While Surendra Mondol was an absolute owner and was in possession, he left this transitory world leaving behind his widow Makhani Bewa and his minor daughter, Robi Sona and a minor son, Ratan Mondol alias Ratan and after the death of Surendra Mondol, his widow Makhani Bewa's family was thrown into a serious financial difficulty. Therefore, being in urgent Legal necessity, Makhani Bewa for herself and on behalf of her minor children sold the suit land to Hasina Warda Chowdhury by the sale deed executed and registered or' 6-2-1970 and 26-2- 1970. Makhani had no other option but to sell the suit land because she urgently needed to repay the loans availed by her deceased husband Surendra Mondol and to incur their maintenance, in order to save the children from starvation and to have a home to live in along with the minor children. Thereafter, Makhani Bewa left Bangladesh, the then East Pakistan, for India for ever to live there along with her minor children Ratan Mondol and Robi Sona. Makhani, Ratan and Robi Sona never came back to Bangladesh and their names never appeared in the voter-list of Bangladesh as they neither lived in Bangladesh nor they were the citizens of Bangladesh. They are the Citizens of India. Ratan had no title and possession in the suit land, therefore, the impugned deed is illegal, rnalafide and fabricated.
8. Having purchased the suit land from Makhani Bewa, Hasina Warda Chowdhury owned and possessed the suit land since 1970 for more than 12 years without any interruption or intervention from any quarter. Her name was mutated in the Tahshil Office and she had been paying taxes to the Government regularly. Nobody raised any question about her entitlement at any time. While, the said Hasina Warda Chowdhury was an absolute owner and possessor of the suit land, she transferred her right, title and interest in the suit land for valuable consideration to the petitioner Nos. 1 to 8 by virtue of those registered documents and also made over possession to the petitioner Nos. 1 to 8 and 3.
9. Having purchased the suit land, the petitioner Nos. 1 to 8 and 3 other purchasers became the absolute owners of the suit land and they are in uninterrupted and continuous possession of the suit land since 1987 by mutating and recording their respective names in the Tahshil Office and in RS Khatian respectively. The petitioners are regularly paying rents, taxes to the Government and municipality. Therefore, the opposite party's claim of the purchase of the suit land from or exchange of the suit land with Ratan Mondol is completely false, malafide, fabricated and therefore, the same deed has got no value in the eye of law and the transaction made on 9-3- 1987 by the opposite party is only a paper transaction created by fictitious person in the name of Ratan Mondol of in order to defraud the legal system of the country.
10. The mutation in the name of the opposite party was cancelled by an order of the learned Assistant Commissioner (Land) dated 24-12-1987 in Miscellaneous Case No. 319 of 1987. The names of the petitioners were duly mutated in respect of the suit land.
11. On the pleadings, the trial Court framed the following issues:
(1) Is the suit maintainable in its present form?
(2) Has there any cause of action to institution the suit?
(3) Whether the suit is barred by limitation?
(4) Whether the suit is bad for defect of parties?
(5) Whether the Court fees have sufficiently been paid?
(6) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get the decree as prayed for?
(7) What other reliefs, if arty, the plaintiff is entitled?
12. The trial Court dismissed the suit. The Appellate Court set-aside the judgment and decree of the Trial Court. Challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the instant petitioners moved this Court and obtained the Rule.
13. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate with Mr Md Rashidul Karim for the petitioners submits that the learned Senior Assistant Judge after considering the evidence on record was pleased to dismiss the suit holding the view that the plaintiff has hopelessly failed to prove title and possession in the suit land. But the Appellate Court without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and without any independent assessment of evidence on record and being failed to appreciate the legal points intricately involved in this case allowed the appeal by gratuitous finding and, as such, decreed the original suit which is ex-facie illegal, therefore, the same is liable to be knocked down to secure the ends of justice, otherwise, it will entail serious loss and injury to the petitioner. He next submits that unlike the Mohamadan Law, hindu mother has got no legal status. She can be a manager of the estate left by her husband for herself as well as for her minor children till the children attaining majority and she was competent to transfer the property of minor son and daughter as their legal guardian for their legal necessity without taking prior permission of the court. In support of his contention, he has referred to the case reported in 12 DLR 433. He further submits that Makhani Bewa transferred 1.81 acres of land in the year of 1970 by two registered deeds to one Hasina Warda Chowdhury for herself and her minor son and daughter for legal necessity and thereafter, Hasina Warda Chowdhury transferred 1.24 acres of land in the year of 1987 by Exhibit-Ga series to the defendant Nos. 1-11 out of her 1.81 acres of land. He also submits that the suit of the plaintiff is barred by limitation as per Article 44 of the Limitation Act and moreover, the suit is hopelessly barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He neither sought consequential remedy nor challenged the impugned deeds created by her mother. He further submits that the plaintiff hopelessly failed to prove that the impugned deed of exchange have been executed by Ratan Mondol in his favour. He further submits that the Appellate Court hopelessly failed to appreciate the deeds executed by Makhani Bewa, mother of Ratan Mondol though the correctness of the recital of the deed shall presume to be correct.
14. None appears to oppose the Rule.
15. Heard the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates for the petitioners and perused the materials on record thoroughly and also considered the convoluted question of law involved in this Case. The learned Judge of the Trial Court disbelieved the exchange deed and came to the finding that for legal necessity, Makhani Bewa transferred the suit property and the Trial Court also came to the finding that the plaintiff hopelessly failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land. In this respect, the relevant portion of the judgment of the Trial Court may be reproduced for better appreciation:
“উপরোক্ত বিস্তারিত আলোচনার আলোকে বাদী নালিশী ভূমি রতন মণ্ডল হইতে এওয়াজ নামামূলে প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে মর্মে দাবী করিলেও বাদী তাহার বর্ণিত এওয়াজনামা হওয়ার বিষয় প্রমাণ করিতে সম্পূণরূপে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছেন। অপরপক্ষে, বিবাদী পক্ষের ১নং সাক্ষী নালিশী ভূমি মাখনী বেওয়া তাহার নাবালক পুত্র-কন্যাগণের পক্ষে নাবালকগণের হিতার্থে এবং বৈধ প্রয়োজনে হাসিনা ওয়ার্দার নিকট বিক্রয় করা এবং উক্ত হাসিনা ওয়ার্দার নালিশী ভূমি বিবাদীগণের নিকট বিক্রয় করার বিষয়ে সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করিয়াছেন যাহা বিবাদী পক্ষে ২, ৩ ও ৪ নং সাক্ষীগণ ১নং সাক্ষীর সাক্ষ্যকে সমর্থন করিয়াছে। এখানে বিশেষভাবে উল্লেখ করা প্রয়োজন বাদীপক্ষের বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলী মূলত দাবী করিয়াছেন যে, মাথনী বেওয়ার একার নালিশী সম্পত্তি বিক্রয়ের অধিকারী ছিল না বা তাহার বৈধ প্রয়োজন ছিল না এবং সেকারণেই মাখনি বেওয়া কর্তৃক হাসিনা ওয়ার্দা এবং তৎপরবর্তীতে হাসিনা ওয়ার্দা কর্তৃক দলিলগুলির আইনগত কোন ভিত্তি নাই। কিন্তু বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলী বাদী পক্ষে তাহার এই বক্তব্যের সর্মথনে কোন সাক্ষ্য প্রমাণ আইনের বিধান বা উচ্চতর আদালতের নজীর আদালতের সম্মুখে উপস্থাপন করেন নাই ।”
16. But the Appellate Court held:
"The defendant-respondents are the subsequent purchasers from Hasina Warda to whom Makhani sold the land of her minor son. The said sale is not found to have been made under any legal necessity. Hasina Warda sold 0.25 decimal land from plot No. 1882 while she purchased 0.09 acre from that plot. Moreover she sold the land of plot No. 1782 without having any saleable interest whatsoever in the said plot. However, the entire transaction between Hasina Warda and Makhani in absence of proof of legal necessity for selling out the land of minor Ratan having not been found valid transaction. The defendant-respondents are not in a position to claim title to the suit land as subsequent purchaser from Hasina Warda. Taking into consideration the entire gamut of evidence on record and the attending circumstances I find reasons to hold the view that the plaintiff has title to and possession over the suit land and having been so the suit for declaration of title was quite maintainable in its present form."
<u>17. If for the sake of argument, it is taken as granted that alleged transfer made by Makhani Bewa of minor Ratan Moridal in favour of Hasina Warda Chowdhury, the predecessor of the defendant is not a valid deed, nevertheless, the suit is barred by limitation as Ratan Mondal did not take any legal action challenging the legality of the deeds executed by her mother in 1970 within the stipulated time nor filed a suit for recovery of the khas possession from the defendants after attaining majority; therefore, the suit was barred by limitation. Shawkat Mahmud in his book titled 'The Limitation Act', 3rd Edition, page Nos. 460 & 461 rightly held to the effect:</u>
<u>"Void transfer. Where a transfer by a guardian is void rib initio, a suit by a minor to set it aside is not governed by this article. Thus where the sale deed of immovable property executed by the father of the minor is without consideration and legal necessity, the sale-deed is void lib initio and Article 44 is not applicable. Where the plaintiff filed a suit for a declaration that certain alienations effected by his mother were not binding on him as the same were not effected by her as his guardian, and in the plaint it was specifically stated that the plaintiff did not seek to set-aside the deeds in question as he was not a party either directly or constructively to those documents, and in substance the suit was one for possession on the basis of title. It was held that on the basis of the averments found in the plaint there was not room for the application of Article 44.</u>
<u>Possession under a void deed is adverse to the owner. Therefore in a case where transferee under a void deed has taken possession, the minor is entitled to bring a suit for recovery of possession within 12 years from the date when the possession of the transferee becomes adverse or within 3 years after attaining majority."</u>
18. In the case of Jalaluddin Shaikh vs Khirode Chandra Tikadar & others, reported in 12 DLR 433, it was held:
"Guardians and Wards Act does not interfere with the personal law of Hindus and Muslims. The Guardians and Wards Act does not alter or affect the rights of natural guardians under the Hindu Law and the powers of the natural guardians of a Hindu minor are larger than those of a guardian appointed under that Act. A natural guardian may alienate the minor's property even without the sanction of the Court, provided the alienation is one for necessity or for the benefit of the estate. Mother being the next natural guardian, in the absence of the father under the Hindu Law, possesses the power to transfer the properties of the minors for legal necessity and for the benefit of the minors."
19. From exhibit-Ka and Ka-1, the original registered deeds dated 6-2-1970; it appears that Makhani Bewa transferred the suit land for legal necessity of the minor. The plaintiff failed to rebut the presumption as to the contents of the aforesaid deeds by adducing cogent reliable evidence; therefore, it cannot be held that the transfer made by Makhani Bewa was illegal. But unfortunately, the learned Judge of the Appellate Court without considering the intricate question of law involved in this case most illegally decreed the suit by gratuitous findings; therefore, the same is liable to be struck down.
20. My penultimate conclusion is that-
(i) The suit is not maintainable in its present form.
(ii) The suit is also absolutely barred by limitation in view of Article 44 read with Article 144 of the Limitation Act.
(iii) The plaintiff hopelessly failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land;
(iv) The transfer made by the Makhani Bewa was lawful.
(v) The judgment of the Appellate Court is not proper judgment of reversal and the alleged exchange deed was not acted upon.
(vi) The impugned judgment and order of the Appellate Court is liable to be turned down to secure the ends of justice;
21. Having regarded the facts and circumstances of the case, I find substance in the Rule. Hence, the Rule deserves to be made absolute.
22. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without passing any order as to costs. The judgment and decree of the Appellate Court are set-aside and those of the trial Court are hereby restored.
23. The earlier order of stay granted by this Court thus stands recalled and vacated.
Let a copy of the judgment along with LCRs be transmitted to the Court below at once.
End.

parties:
Shib Lal Agorwala being dead his heirs: 1(a) Tara Debi Agorwala and others--------------------Appellants
vs
Panna Lal Agorwala being dead his heirs: 1(a) Pushpa. Rani Agorwala and others--------------Respondents
