full_judgment:
Md Iqbal Kabir, J: This Rule Nisi, under adjudication, was issued on 30-1-2018, in the following terms:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the Office Order issued by the Jagannath University authority on 10 August 2017 vide memo No. জবি/প্রশা-১(২৩৭)/২০১১/৩৭৬১ dismissing the petitioner from his post of Associate Professor in the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and as to why the respondent should not be directed to reinstate the petitioner in his service with due seniority and all arrear salaries and benefits and/or such order or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and gaper."
2. The short fact relevant for disposal of this Rule is that the petitioner joined in the service as an Assistant Professor of Jagannath University in the year 2011 and subsequently, he was promoted to the post of Associate Professor. From day one he was discharging his duties diligently and responsibly. However, all of a sudden petitioner along with two other female members of the faculty received an official order dated 11-4-2016, signed by the Registrar refraining them from participating in academic activities. It claims that one of the students of the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism filed a complaint against the petitioner before the Vice-Chancellor, such a situation, on 5-4-2016 Authority vide its memo dated 6-4-2016 formed a committee (in short committee No. 1), which found prima facie substance therein. Subsequently, on 19-4-2016, Petitioner appeared before the committee to meet up the queries as best as he could though he was not given any written copy of the purported allegation brought against him. Thereafter, the petitioner was informed by a memo dated 4-5-2016, that Syndicate of the University in its meeting dated 28-4-2016 considered the report and suspended the petitioner. On 8-5-2016, the petitioner was issued with another notice under the signature of a committee namely ‘যৌন নিপীড়ন প্রতিরোধ কল্পে গঠিত অভিযোগ কমিটি’ (in short committee No. 2) asking him to appear before them. Petitioner faced the committee on the given date and time and responded to the queries of the committee at his best. Following two separate inquiry reports of two individual committees, Authority issued two separate ‘অভিযোগবিবরণী’ (Charges), and ilzirrzurtlf4.40ti (description of charge) dated 17-8-2016 and 21-8-2016. The first one contains four, and the second one has six allegations, by the alleged memo petitioner was accused of misconduct and required the petitioner to show cause as to why he should not be dismissed from his service or any other appropriate penalty should not be imposed as per the Rules-1985, Petitioner by two separate letters dated 28-8-2016 asked for statements of allegations which ought to have been attached with the charges. Failing to get any elaborate statements of allegations, the petitioner based on the charges mentioned in the memo dated 17-8-2016 and 21-8-2016 denied the accusations brought against him except utterances of some rude/inappropriate words against the departmental head for which he apologized. In his reply has stated that he did not do anything which falls under the ambit of misconduct therefore, there is no scope for accusing him of such allegations.
3. Petitioner once again appeared before an inquiry committee on 23-11-2016 to response further to the queries. All most after four months i.e., on 14-3-2017, authority issued a memo titled second show-cause notice stating inter alia that by the memo dated 17-10-2016 following Rule 7 and 10 of the Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 an inquiry committee had been formed to take necessary steps in connection of the allegations brought against the petitioner under two charges dated 17-8-2016 and 21-8-2016 and issued the impugned memo. The letter titled second show-cause notice was served upon the petitioner without attaching a copy of the report prepared by the inquiry committee formed under Rules-1985. In such a situation, the petitioner before making his reply requested to provide him a copy of the report of the inquiry committee. However, the respondent did not post any response to the request. Thereafter, by a memo dated 10-8-2017 dismissed the petitioner from his service.
4. Against this backdrop, challenging the legality and propriety of the impugned memo, the petitioner has brought this case under judicial review.
5. Dr. Shahdeen Malik, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner took us through the impugned decision and annexed documents/papers available on record and submitted that the dismissal from the service is illegal, as the University authority did not provide the petitioner with a copy of the inquiry report thereby, violating the natural justice and mandatory provisions of Rules 7(5) of Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules-1985 issued by the impugned memo.
6. He further submits that petitioner is entitled to enjoy the protection of the law, and to be treated under the law, and only in accordance with law. In this particular case prolonging the disciplinary proceedings against the petitioner as well without following the mandatory provisions of law, the dismissal of the petitioner has violated article 31 and 40 of the Constitution.
7. Per contra, Mr Muhammad Yusuf Hussain Humayun, learned Senior Advocate along with Mr Nazmul Hassan Rakib, learned Advocate appears on behalf of respondent Nos. 2 and 3 entered an appearance, and contested the Rule Nisi by filing an affidavit-in-opposition.
8. However, it is noted that while the Rule Nisi was awaiting for substantive disposal, by filing an application Dr. Shahdeen Malik, learned Senior Advocate informed this Court that the petitioner had passed away leaving behind the applicants as his legal heirs and successors-in-interest, Therefore, the applicants prayed for substituting them in place of the deceased petitioner, in that regard, this Court allowed the application.
9. In this case, at the instance of this Court, Mr AM Amin Uddin, the learned Attorney-General appears to assist the Court. According to him, in the event of petitioner's death, the heirs if any, living at the time of succession open, shall per stripe receive the benefit as the case may be, if alive. In this case, the petitioner had died therefore, the petitioner's heirs will get the benefit, if the petitioner (Mir Mosharef Hossain) succeeds in the Rule.
10. Respondent in his submission claims that this writ is not maintainable. As the appeal against the order of dismissal has been filed by the petitioner before the Hon'ble Chancellor is very much pending. In reply to that contention, Dr. Shahdeen Malik brought to the notice of this Court that on 26-9-2017, the appeal has been filed, till date it has not been disposed of, according to him. Inordinate delay in considering the appeal was a good enough for the petitioner to be aggrieved and to bring this petition. On the alleged point, he relied upon a decision namely" Chairman and another vs Sakhawat Hossain and others, reported in 9 BLC (AD) 227. Mr Yusuf Hussain Humayun, learned Senior Advocate for the respondents argued that earlier petitioner filed an appeal before a wrong forum which was not placed before the authority as it was not made following the provision of law. Against the alleged argument, petitioner argued that failure to file an appeal won't in any way dent the right of the petitioner under the constitution to challenge his order of dismissal. In support of his contention, he relied upon a decision namely, Ayub Ali Chowdhury us Government of Bangladesh and others, reported in 57 DLR 578. According to him, the Registrar of the University was duty-bound to place the appeal before the appropriate authority, the wrong forum cannot debar the petitioner to adjudicate his legal right. It was argued by the petitioner that before taking any steps against the petitioner, the respondent ought to follow all applicable laws and rules, and only thereafter could take initiative. The petitioner claimed that the authority ought to have been issued with an elaborate copy of statements of allegations, which the authority despite several requests to supply such statements of allegations refused to provide thereby violated the mandatory provisions of applicable laws, In his reply dated 6-9-2016 against the memo dated 17-8-2016 and 21-8-2016, this petitioner categorically denied all the accusations brought against him. According to Or. Shahdeen Malik, there lies no scope for imposing any penalties under the Rules of 1985 upon him as he did not do anything which falls under the ambit of misconduct. The petitioner, however, again claims he has the right to be issued with an elaborate copy of statements of allegations which the university authority refused to provide on repeated requests and thereby, violated the mandatory provision of law.
11. It transpired from the record that following Rule 7 and 10 of the Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rules-1985 (in short, Rules-1985) an inquiry committee had been formed by the memo dated 17-10-2016. It had constituted to inquire the matter as regard the allegations made against the petitioner and to submit a report. Petitioner made his reply before the committee on 23-11-2016, as he was asked by the member of the committee. However, it appears that the second show-cause notice was served upon the petitioner vide its memo dated 14-3-2017, without attaching a report of the inquiry committee. The Registrar of the University in his notice dated 14-3-2017 claimed to rely upon the findings of the 'inquiry committee' asked to show cause as to why the petitioner should not be dismissed from his service. Against which Registrar of University was requested by the petitioner to provide him with a copy of the inquiry committee report and the minutes of the committee.
12. Dr. Shahdeen Malik, learned Senior Advocate pointed out that the inquiry by the committee formed under Rules-1985 was not properly conducted, it has claimed that no notification, and or petitioner was not informed about the committee. However, the petitioner was not furnished with a copy of the inquiry report along with a second show-cause notice to enable him to answer the charge properly. He took us to the provision of Rule 7 of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules-1985 (in short Rules-1985) which deals with inquiry procedure in cases calling for major penalties, Rule-7 (5) deals with the second show-cause notice.. According to him in the instant case, second show-cause notice had not been completed and or accompanied with a report under the provision of Rule 7(5) of the Rules-1985, such apparent facts demonstrate that natural justice along with the petitioner's fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution being the right to equality before the law and the right to be treated in accordance with the provision of law and profession or occupation have been denied and violated! Therefore, the impugned order of dismissal is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
13. At this juncture, the provision of the alleged sub-Rule 7(5) of the Rules-1985 may be quoted below verbatim for better appreciation:
"Rule 7(5): On receipt of the report of the findings of the Inquiry Officer or the Board of Inquiry, the authority shall consider the report and record its decision on the charge and communicate the same together with a copy of the report to the accused within ten working days from the date or receipt of the report."
14. From a reading of Rule 7(5), it is apparent that the second show-cause notice requires together with a copy of a report to be sent. That is precisely what has not been done in the instant case.
15. In response to the alleged submission, Mr Humayun, learned Senior Advocate claims that authority earlier conducted two separate inquiries and issued charge, thereafter, the committee formed under the Rules-1985 holding inquiry observing all formalities having found him guilty awarded the punishment which he deserved. According to him with regards to the service of the copy of the inquiry committee's report, he claims that non-service of the inquiry committees report has not in any, way caused prejudice to the petitioner and affected the inquiry which has been held duly and properly and in view of the matter, the petitioner is not entitled to get any relief.
16. At this juncture, it is pertinent to state that the second show-cause notice dated 14-a-2017 was served upon the petitioner wherein it has claimed the charges against the petitioner brought under memos dated 17-8-2016 and 21-8-2016 prepared by other committees have been proved. Therefore, in the dismissal order dated 10-8-2017, it was claimed that relevant documents, reports of the committee formed under Rules-1985, and replies of the petitioner were placed and accepted by the Syndicate on 9-7-2017, On scrutiny, it appears that the report prepared by the committee formed under the Rules-1985 did not come to light, nowhere the date of alleged report was mentioned, therefore, it is not visible how the said report could be considered. It was also best known to them for what reason did the committee formed under Rules-1985 relied upon the charge dated 17-8-2016 and 21-8-2016 which was brought before them instead of its findings brought in its report. Though, the petitioner to make his reply against the second show-cause notice requested for the report given by the committee formed under the Rules-1985 he also expressed his grave concern before making any reply to the previous committee, but that was not supplied.
17. As it was claimed by the petitioner that there were three committees and they have conducted inquiries violating the applicable Rules thereby question of the legality of the report has been raised. It appears that the inquiry proceedings in the instant case were started on 19-4-2016 alleging the allegation against the petitioner while a committee (in short 1st Committee) has been formed vide its letter dated 6-4-2016, The Syndicate of the University decided to suspend the petitioner temporarily while the report of the committee was placed before it. On 8-5-2016 petitioner was issued with another letter signed by the Convener of another committee namely,‘যৌন নিপীড়ন প্রতিরোধ কল্পে গঠিত অভিযোগ কমিটি’ (in short, 2nd Committee) stating inter alia ’..... আপনার বিরুদ্ধে আনীত অভিযোগ পর্যালোচনা করতে আপনার সাক্ষ্য গ্রহণ প্রযোজন.....’ Petitioner faced the second committee on 10-5-2016. However, by the memo dated 17-10-2016 another committee had formed under the Rules-1985 to conduct its inquiry against the petitioner, wherein the petitioner appeared on 23-11-2016 Thereafter, the committee formed under the Rules-1985 placed its report before the syndicate on 9-7- 2017, which altogether took 228 days to complete the same. Thus, it was alleged that the proceeding perjures the petitioner and he is entitled to exonerate from the proceedings.
18. In relation to the second show-cause not the learned Advocate for the petitioner placed reliance upon a case of Director, Telecommunication Region vs M Islam & another, reported in 1995 (3) BLT (AD) 90 wherein the Administrative Appellate Tribunal allowed the appeal on the ground that with the second show-cause notice that was served on respondent No. 1 a copy of the inquiry report was not annexed depriving respondent No. 1 of giving a reasonable opportunity to show cause against the proposed penalty the mandatory requirement of law having not been complied with, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal rightly set-aside the order of removal and reinstated respondent No. 1 to his service. Further, in the case of Golam Moatafa (Md) and others vs Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation and others, reported in 52 DLR 299, this Court observed that the supply of inquiry report along with a second show-cause notice is not an idle formality but the requirement of law which is also in consonance with the provision of the principle of natural justice. The petitioner under the rule is entitled to a copy of the inquiry report together with a second show-cause notice. Thus, it can be said that the impugned order of dismissal having been passed in violation of the Rules-1985 calls for interference.
19. It was claimed that the committee inquired about the allegation brought against the petitioner and prepared a report, wherefore finding came out that students were sexually harassed and the petitioner tried to take immoral advantage of the students and used abusive words against others. However, sexual harassment is not desirable and acceptable. It is one of the indicators to assess society. That harassment by a Teacher of an educational institution is undesirable and no one can ask for forgiveness. If it occurs, students of the institution, parents and family members of the students fall under depression and suffers irreparable loss and injury, therefore, everyone has to be careful and it should be prevented by any means. The alleged guilty person has to be brought under law and s/he cannot escape the Rules Against such allegations, the authority has to follow the applicable law and rules to prove the same. But, before being penalized authorities are duty-bound under the law to give the opportunity or defend the person against whom the allegation has been brought. In this case, an allegation has been brought against the petitioner and it was inquired by the inquiry committee. Before taking a final decision authority issued a second show-cause notice, but the second show-cause notice was not accompanied by the inquiry report. It was also admitted that after getting a second show-cause notice, the petitioner by a letter requested to provide a copy of the statements of the allegation and the respondent did not respond to it. According to him, the Rule of natural justice has become a part and parcel of the law, as well as procedure. It aims to ensure the delivery of justice to the parties and prevent arbitrariness. The rule of natural justice serves as a bridge against any blatant discrimination against the rights of individuals. Thereby, it has claimed rules of natural justice require a second show-cause notice along with an inquiry report and the mandate of law as aforesaid has not been done,
20. In this case, further reliance may be given upon the decision in an unreported case of Md Syedul Abrar vs Bangladesh and others (Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2844 of 2017) our Apex Court in a similar situation held that the authority would communicate along with the copy of inquiry report with their decision thereof. The court observed when disciplinary proceedings are not conducted following the rules of procedure and principle of natural justice the order of punishment passed therein is not sustainable in law. In the case of the Bangladesh and others vs Md Tariqul Islam, reported in 25 BLC (AD) 131 our Apex Court observed that non-supply of the inquiry report to the petitioner is a clear violation of the principle of natural justice and thereby, the petitioner-appellant has been seriously prejudiced from the right of self-defense as to the allegations brought against him. Admittedly, an inquiry report was not supplied and he was dismissed from service, which is a major penalty. Thus it was considered that before imposing a major penalty the cardinal principle of natural justice requires that a copy of the inquiry report has to be supplied to the concerned employee. Further in the case of Bangladesh and others vs Mr Abul Khair, reported in 9 MLR (AD) 221 =56 DLR (AD) 183 our Apex Court observed that the authority imposing any punishment upon a delinquent staff must see that he has been dealt with in accordance with law and following the principles of natural justice. to the instant case, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal on scrutiny found that the respondent has not been properly dealt with during the inquiry complying with the provision of law following the principles of natural justice, and as such, the impugned orders have been tainted with illegality making the same illegal and void and as such, the same are not sustainable in law.
<u>21.  By now proposition of law has been well settled that a second show-cause notice is, in fact, the accused employee's last opportunity to place his case before the authority who is to decide about the punishment to be awarded against the employee and accordingly, it has been held in the case of Md Torab Ali is Bangladesh Textile Millis Corporation and another, reported in 1989 BLD 383 = 41 DLR 138 that the accused employee has the burden and or the agony of disbursing the mind of the appointing authority from the impression created by the report of the inquiry officer. Further, it was observed that the second show-cause notice no doubt requires the delinquent to show because why the proposed punishment shall not be inflicted upon him, but upon perusal of his reply, the appointing authority may still take any view with regards to the proposed punishment to be awarded. In order to be meaningful, it has to be furnished along with the report of the Enquiry Officer.</u>
22. For a similar purpose, Dr. Shahdeen Malik, the learned Senior Advocate placed reliance on other cases i.e. Mostafa Miah vs Chairman, First Labor Court, reported in 46 DLR 373; Malik Afzal Hossain vs Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation and others, reported in 5 BLC 62 1998 BLD (HD) 686; Nazina Akhtar vs GM, Rural Electrification Board and others, reported in 10 BLC 667; Shafiqul Islam (Md) vs Intermediate & Secondary Education Board & others, reported in 15 MLR 345 and Chairman, Rural Electrification Board at present (Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board) Dhaka vs Maziruddin Ahmed Khan and others, reported in 70 DLR (AD) 151.
23. The legal position of the case in hand is identical to the case referred to above decisions. Therefore, the principle expressed in the case referred to above is fully applied to the case in hand. Moreover, the learned Counsel for the respondents could not make any case that could attract either of the principles as laid down in the aforesaid decisions and or find substance. Thus, we are unable to consider the submissions made by the Respondents.
<u>24. In this case, a dismissal order has been awarded, order of dismissal is major punishment under section 44(6) of the University Act, 2005 and Rule 4(3)D of the Rules-1985, before awarding such punishment authority may have the opportunity to scrutinize based on the reply made by the petitioner, without report of the committee petitioner may have failed to reply on it properly.</u>
25. Given the fact, and reason stated above, we find substance in the submissions made by the petitioner. The dismissal of the petitioner cannot be sustained as the impugned decision was taken violating the natural justice and provisions of applicable Rules.
26. Thus, we find merit in the Rule, for which the Rule is required to be made Absolute.
27. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The order of dismissal is set-aside.
28. However, the petitioner (Mir Mosharef Hossain) had died, thus, it is not possible to reinstate the petitioner to his service, but the petitioner who has been substituted in place of the petitioner (Mir Mosharef Hossain) would entitled to the monetary benefits as permissible under the law. Therefore, this Court directs the respondents to give financial benefit to the substituted petitioner, to which the petitioner was (Mir Mosharef Hossain) entitled during his lifetime.
No order as to cost.
Communicate the order.
End.

full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J: Defendant 10 has preferred this appeal challenging judgment and final decree dated 10-7-2019 passed by the Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka accepting the Commissioner's report pursuant to judgment and decree dated 28-6-2007 passed in Title Suit 177 of 2005 decreeing the suit in preliminary form and granting separate saham to defendant 10.
2. Respondent as plaintiff filed Title Suit 151 of 2000 before the Subordinate Judge, Court No. 4, Dhaka on 25-6-2000 and the suit was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka on 28-8-2005 and renumbered as Title Suit 177 of 2005. Suit was filed for declaration of title with respect to 'Kha' schedule land and a decree to the effect that the Heba-bil-Ewaz document 7027 dated 15-8-1990 executed by Alimunnessa in respect of 1:--ha' schedule land is fraudulent, illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff and also for a decree of partition with regard to schedule land by evicting defendant 10. A further prayer to the effect that the Heba-bil-Ewaz document dated 2-3-2002 is actually inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff was added by amendment dated 27-7-2002.
3. This suit was heard analogously with Title Suits 180 and 183 of 2005 which were filed by contesting defendants 3 and 4 respectively. Both the suits were filed for permanent injunction.
4. The case of the plaintiffs is that the 'Ka' schedule partible land measuring 0.74 acres of CS plots 4613 and 4614 belonged to CS tenants Lai Mia @ Miah Helu and Kalu Mia Kalu who are 3 (three) brothers. Kalu died leaving behind wife Karimunnessa and daughter Latifunnnessa who maintained possession amicably in plot 4613 with respect to 0.15 acres. They sold 0.14½ acres to the plaintiffs by 10 kabalas on 3-10-1989, 11-10-1989, 8-11-1989, 21-12-1989 and delivered possession. Plaintiffs paid rent upon mutation. Defendant 10 appellant claiming under a fraudulent document dated 15-8-1990 threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession for which plaintiff filed Title Suit 324 of 1992 for permanent injunction. The suit was withdrawn after subsequent dispossession on 12-124997. Then plaintiffs filed Title Suit 283 of 1998 for declaration of title and recovery of possession. Suit was dismissed on the finding that plaintiffs have title but their remedy lies in a suit for partition. Hence the suit was filed.
5. The case of defendant 3 is that Helu died leaving behind 3(three) sons and 1(one) daughter Alimunnessa. Alimunnessa got 0.20 acres by amicable partition. She sold 0.071/2 acres to defendant 3 Sohrab on 11-3-1984 and delivered possession. Defendants 4 and 10 threatened Sohrab with dispossession. Sohrab then filed Title Suit 357 of 2001 for permanent injunction which was renumbered as Title Suit 180 of 2005 and tagged with Title Suit 177 of 2005 for analogous hearing.
6. The case of defendant 4 is that the 4(four) sons and 1(one) daughter of Helu entered into an agreement with defendant 4 on 4-3-1982 in respect of 0.071/2 acres of land and since registration was refused Title Suit 44 of 1985 for Specific Performance of Contract was filed which was decreed on 25-4-1987. She got the document registered through Court on 26- 5-1997 and also got possession. Defendant 3 along with some others had been trying to dispossess defendant 4 for which she filed Title Suit 47 of 2002 for permanent injunction which was renumbered as Title Suit 183 of 2005 and heard analogously with Title Suit 177 of 2005.
7. The case of defendant 10 appellant is that KaIlk. Lalu and Helu were owners in possession in the 'Ka' schedule land including 0.35 acres of CS plot 272 of Delpara Mouja. Kalu died leaving behind wife Karimunnessa and daughter Latifunnessa who by amicable arrangement got the land of Delpara Mouja and accordingly a deed of relinquishment was executed by them on 28-4-1943 disowning partible land. Latifunnessa transferred the land of Delpara to Aslam and others by document dated 21-4-1949, Alimunnessa who is the daughter of Helu and mother of the appellant transferred 0.131/2 acres of land from plot 4613 to this defendant by Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 15-8- 1990 and delivered possession. The maternal uncles of defendant 10 named Shamsuddin, jamaluddin, and 2(two) sons and 2(two) daughters of deceased Alauddin executed a Heba-bil-Ewaz on 2-3-2002 with respect to 0.15 acres in favour of defendant 10. Thus defendant 10 acquired 0.281/2 acres. But since his mother had interest only in 0.0185 acres instead of 0,131/2 acres in plot 4613 he is entitled to 0.1785 acres in total and he prayed saham for such portion.
8. The trial Court framed 6(six) issues and decreed Title Suit 177 of 2005 in preliminary form and allotted saham to defendant 10 by judgment and decree dated 28-6-2007. The Court found that the acquisition of land of Delpara Mouja by Karimun and Latifun through amicable arrangement and the execution of nadabi document dated 28-4-1943 by them are absolutely false and Karimun and Latifun had interest in CS plots 4613 and 4614 and also found nobody claimed through Karimun and Latifun except plaintiffs through Exhibits 9-18 which conferred title. The Court also found that the vendor of defendants 3, 4 and 10 named Alimunnessa had interest only in 0.03 acres and the document of defendant 3 being earlier in point of time shall prevail over documents of defendants 4 and 10 and defendant 3 thus claiming under document dated 11-3-1984 got only 0.03 acres instead of 0.071/2 acres and defendant 4 acquired 0.011/2 acres from each of the sons of Helu which in total is 0.06 acres by document dated 26-6-1997 and since the heirs of Helu had remaining interest in 0.15 acres defendant 10 acquired title in the same by Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 2-3-2002. The Court further found that Title Suits 180 and 183 of 2005 filed by defendants 3 and 4 respectively failed due to want of exclusive possession and plaintiffs are entitled to declaration of joint title with the defendants and partition in the land under schedule 'Kha’ of the proceeding referring to order dated 23-1- and defendant 10 is entitled to separate saham 2010 passed in Civil Revision 1129 of 2010 of 0.15 acres of land.
9. None of the parties has preferred appeal against this preliminary decree.
10. Both plaintiffs and defendant 10 filed two separate applications for appointment of Advocate Commissioner on 15-8-2007 and those were allowed. Thereafter defendant 4 preferred Title Appeal 302 of 2007 against dismissal of Title Suit 183 of 2005 for which record was called for on 3-10-2007_ Appeal failed and record was received on 25-1-2010 by the lower Court. Plaintiffs paid the commission fee and accordingly Court appointed Mr Md Habibur Rahman as or on 25-1-2010 and fixed the next date on 14-3-2010 for submitting report, Meanwhile on 1-3-2010 which was an off date defendant 10 again filed another application under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and prayed for direction upon the Commissioner to grant saham in his favour in 0.15 acres from plot 4613 and the application was allowed, Learned Advocate Commissioner filed his report on 22-3.2010 and the next date was fixed on 7-4-2010 for filing objection. But defendant 10 on another off date on 24-3-2010 appeared in the Court to deposit chalan for commission fee and Court appointed Mr Md. Motiar Rahman as Commissioner who was ordered to complete commission according to the prayer made by defendant 10 on 1-3-2010. On 7-4-2010 defendant 10 filed written objection and Commissioner Mr Motiar also filed an application for time for submitting report. Court upon hearing rejected appointment of Mr Motiar and appointed Mr Habibur Rahrnan for holding commission and passed order upon him to deal with commission according to the meaning of the application filed by defendant 10 under Section 151 of the Code and the next date was fixed on 16-5-2010 for submitting report. On 21-4-2010 plaintiffs prayed for stay of the proceeding referring to order dated 23-1-10 and defendant is entitled to separate saham 2010 passed in Civil Revision 1129 of 2010.preferred by defendant 4 and on 16-5-2010 plaintiffs filed an application for status quo in the light of tine order dated 21-3-2010 passed in revision. The Court kept the application with the record and fixed on 27-6-2010 for filing report but Commissioner filed his second report on 24-6-2010. On 6-9-2010 High Court Division called for the record. On 9-4-2019 record was sent back. On 20-5-2019 Court passed order to issue Court notice upon defendants 3, 4, 10 and the left margin of the order shows that the same was issued on 17-6- 2019. On 19-6-2019 Court accepted the second report dated 24-6-2010. On 10-7-2019 plaintiffs filed an application for treating the first report dated 22-3-2010 as part of the decree and to make the preliminary decree final. The application was allowed. The final decree was signed on 24-7-2019.
11. It Defendant 10 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 10-7-2019 preferred this appeal.
12. Mr Taposh Kumar Dutta, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the learned Joint District Judge passed the impugned judgment and final decree without application of Judicial mind. The Court did not properly peruse the report of the Advocate Commissioner and accepted the same upon fanciful consideration. He submits that defendant 10 filed an objection on 7-4-2010 against the first report dated 22-3-2010 but the Court without perusing the order sheet and written objection mechanically passed the impugned order 120 dated 10-7-2019 without giving any opportunity to this defendant to cross examine the Advocate Commissioner. He then submits that after accepting the second report dated 24-6-2010 Court cannot pass decree upon first report dated 22-3-2010 and the impugned decree is liable to be set-aside. He strongly submits that there is a big gap of about 9 (nine) years between proceeding of commission and acceptance of report but Court notice was not served upon defendant 30 to challenge the report thereby natural justice has been violated and the date of service appears to be manipulated and such irregularity does not allow the impugned decree to stand. In support of his submission he referred the cases Jaherunnessa vs Safed Ali &pan and others, 1982 BUD 114 = 36 DLR 253: Hosna Banu and others Vs Azad Khan and others, 1983 BLD 140. He submits that the impugned judgment clearly violates the principles of partition which give preference to existing possession and the impugned decree is subject to interference being bad in law.
13. Mr Swapan Kumar Dutta, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents submits that the learned Joint District Judge correctly passed the decree and the report of the Commissioner is evidently clear and valid being made in accordance with the preliminary decree. The written objection dated 74-2010 is made beyond pleading and a new case has been made out which is untenable. He submits that defendant 10 has no allegation that the learned Commissioner did riot serve any notice arid has not gone to the suit land and the report is a mere table work. He then submits that the order 97 dated 15-8-2007 was made not for allotment of 0,15 acres to defendant 10 from plot 4613 but only for allowing the application for appointment of Commissioner. He further submits that the Court notice was duly served upon defendant 10 and in support of his submission he has referred the case of Abdur Rahman and others vs Sultan @ Sultan and others. 35 DLR (AD) 51, He finally submits that since the case of the plaintiffs is not specifically denied in the written statement of defendant 10 he has no reasonable and valid point to object the report and his case in appeal is barred under Order S Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in is support he refers the case of Divisional Estate Officer vs jashimuddin, 24 BLC (AD) 36,
14. We have heard the learned Advocates and gone through the materials on record and the cases cited,
15. Plaintiffs claim from the heirs of one of the CS tenants Kalu Mia who got 0.2466 acres in his share and he died leaving behind wife Karimunnessa and daughter Latifunn.essa and 2(two) brothers Help and Lalu. Accordingly Karimun, Latifun acquired 0.0308 and 0.1233 acres respectively. Plaintiffs purchased the suit land measuring 0.14112 acres from Karimun and Latifun by 10 kabalas Exhibits 9-18 in 1989 and nobody except plaintiffs claims under them in the suit. On the other hand defendant 10 claiming under Helu says that Karimun and Latifun disowned the suit land and got 0.35 acres of Delpara Mouja by amicable arrange-ment and executed a deed of relinquishment on 28-4-1943 Exhibit-B in favour of Helu Mia. Helu died leaving behind 4(four) sons Shamsuddin, Moniruddin, Jamal Uddin, Alauddin and 1(one) daughter Alimunnessa. Alimunnessa got 0.21 acres in plot 4613by amicable partition and executed Heba.-bil-Ewaz dated 15-8-1990 (Exhibit-D) to her son defendant 10 for 0.13½ acres. Subsequently Shamsuddin, Jamal Uddii and heirs of Alauddin executed another Heba-bii-Ewaz (Exhibit-F) on 2-3-2002 in favour of defendant 10 in respect of 0.15 acres. Thus, defendant 10 got 0.28½ acres but ultimately claims 0.1785 acres of land.
16. This is an appeal against final decree, None of the parties preferred any appeal against the preliminary decree. In this appeal parties are precluded from challenging the preliminary decree. But in the instant case there are some important aspects which should be looked into to decide whether the written objection dated 7-4-2010 filed by defendant 10 against Commissioner-'s report dated 22-3-2010 is reasonable and sustainable.
17. From reading of the judgment passed in Title Suit 283 of 1998 (Exhibit-E) it appears that the acquisition of land in Delpara Mouja by the vendors of plaintiffs and subsequent execution of nadabi deed (Exhibit-B) as claimed by defendant 10 are disbelieved with strong reasons as also is done in the present case. In Exhibit-E defendant 10 claimed 0.131/2 acres by Exhibit-D dated 15-8-1990 arid claimed possession. Now after about 12(twelve) years defendant 10 filed written statement on 24-3- 2002 after 22(twenty two) days of pendente lite execution of Exhibit-F dated 2-3-2002 and disclaimed the land of Exhibit -D except 0.0285 acres and claimed to be owner in possession in 0.1785 acres. It appears that the present suit is the outcome of Exhibit-E and defendant 10 approbates and reprobates according to their desire and convenience. Another important aspect of this case is paragraph 4 of the written objection dated 74-2010 in which defendant 10 made out a third case of sale of 0.24 1/3 acres from plot 4614 by as many as 10 documents from 1986 to 1989 by Monir Uddin who is one of the sons of Helu. Exhibit-8 and Exhibit-E show that although those documents were introduced in written statement and marked in evidence as Exhibit-Cha series in Title Suit 283 of 1998 but those facts are kept hidden in the instant suit because had those documents been introduced defendant 10 surely would have failed to have title by Exhibit-F. The sale of 0.21 acres of plot 4613 from the east side of the suit land by Lalu in favour of the predecessor of defendant 1 is admitted by defendant 10 as apparent from Exhibit-8 and E. Monir Uddin alone sold 0.24 1/3 acres to different persons in possession from plot 4614. Paragraph 160a) of Exhibit-8 shows that Helu's daughter Alimunnessa alone acquired 0.21 acres from plot 4613. She sold 0.07½ acres to defendant 3 Sohrab, Defendant 4 also claimed purchase of 0.07½ acres in execution of a decree from the heirs of Helu. Besides the sale in favour of the plaintiffs stands out. For such reason in the instant case defendant 10 threw out his earlier claim through Exhibit-I) and made out a new case on the strength of a pendente lite Heba-bil-Ewaz (Exhibit-F). We cannot strike the preliminary decree but nevertheless this Court is not unfettered to see and examine the available evidence adduced by the parties and to reach to a satisfactory conclusion and to put an end to the litigation once for all. Exhibit-F appears to have come out of the blue and the transaction seems colourable. It is also hard to believe that all maternal uncles and 4(four) maternal cousins out of love and affection have come forward together and execute a Heba-bil-Ewaz in favour of defendant 10 through Exhibit-F in 2002 during pendency of the suit.
18. Suit was decreed in respect of 0.14¼ acres specified by the boundary with the red coloured sketch map as detailed and depicted in the 'ha' schedule. The ordering portion of the judgment shows that preliminary decree of partition is passed in respect of 0.14¼ acres for declaration of title and joint possession of the plaintiffs and defendant 10 gets a separate saham of 0.15 acres of land. The red coloured portion of the sketch map shows the suit land is apparently within plot 4613. Defendant 10 did not prefer any appeal against such decree. There is no scope on part of defendant 10 to deny and challenge such specific portion given in favour of the plaintiffs by the decree passed in preliminary form. Order 103 dated 1-3-2010 shows that defendant 10 filed an application under Section 151 of the Code on the prayer for appointment of Commissioner for getting saham of 0.15 acres from plot 4613 and the application for appointment of Commissioner was allowed. Order 106 dated 24-3-2010 and 107 dated 74-2010 also show that the Court passed order upon the Commissioner to complete his commission work according to the meaning of the prayer made by defendant 10 in his application done under Section 151 of the Code. The Joint District Judge cannot pass such orders which directly go against the preliminary decree itself. Court can make directions in accordance with the principles of equity involved in a partition suit but cannot go behind or beyond the decree for making the same jeopardised and infructuous The above mentioned orders appear to be improper especially when the decree was passed with a clear specification and no appeal is preferred against such decree, Question which has been determined by preliminary decree should be delegated to the Commissioner.
19. Mr Taposh Dutta emphasized on service of Court notice and argues that the same having not been properly served upon defendant 10 the final decree suffers illegality specially when there is a huge gap of  9 (nine) years between proceeding of Commission and acceptance of report, Order 118 dated 20-5-2019 shows that Court passed order of issuance of Court notice and the left margin of the order also shows that on 17-6-2019 issue of notice was brought out to the peon and the same is also , apparent from notice itself. We have carefully perused the notice and it comes to our attention that the date is over written by "18" in place of "19" but this does not appear significant and it is a mere mistake of the peon and the return was duly received by the office of Nazir on 19-6-2019 and Court examined the same. Defendant 10 filed written objection on 7-4-2010 against first report dated 22-3-2010 and the second report dated 24.6-2010 was not confronted by any objection and on 6-9-2010 record was sent to High Court Division and retuned back on 94-2019. There is no specific provision of serving notice upon the parties or their respective lawyers after the Advocate Commissioner submits his report. Rut if considerable time has elapsed it is practice that the lawyers or parties are to be informed of recommencement of the Court's proceeding. In the case in hand from reading of order sheet and perusing service return it appears that notice was served. The parties were aware of the appointment of the Commissioner as well as the reports submitted by the Commissioner and appellant also filed written objection. Equity aids the vigilant and the same will not came to the aid of an indolent party who does not keep track of the proceeding. This case is regulated by procedural rules and there is no scope to invite a supposed rule of natural justice. The fact of the 1983 BLD case is different from the present one simply because defendant 10 filed objection in the instant case which is absent in the referred case. The 3982 RLD case has been reversed in Civil Appeal 157 of 1983 as reported in 2985 BLD (AD) 329. The raffia laid down in 35 DER case as referred by the respondents appears to be relevant in the present case and this 35 BILR case has also been referred to 1985 BLD case. We therefore hold that the submission made by Mr Taposh on point of notice does not have merit.
<u>20. We have also gone through two commission reports done by the same Advocate Commissioner on 22-3-2010 and 24-6-2010. The language of the two reports are completely same and in the second report it is explained away by the Commissioner that he has got nothing to do in effecting further partition because a report has been earlier filed giving specific saham to the plaintiffs and defendant 10 which is under judicial decision. In the report he clearly speaks that after getting writ he went to the locality on 20-2-2010 at about 10-30 am when plaintiffs were present but despite notice defendant 10 was absent. He also speaks that in effecting partition prior possession has preference for the sake of equitable justice and upon due compliance of judgment and decree along with formal procedures he has allotted 14.25 decimals to the plaintiffs from CS plot 4613 and defendant 10 from plot 4614 though defendant 10 prayed saham in plot 4613 overlapping the saham of the plaintiffs and in the process of effecting partition preliminary decree is complied with. There is no allegation made in the written objection of defendant 10 that the Commissioner did not go to the suit land or the report is a mere table work or he did not start from any fixed pillar or case map or field work is false, Rather defendant 10 says in his objection that he got the suit land by virtue of Exhibit-F dated 2-3-2002 which is 13 (thirteen) years later of plaintiffs' documents Exhibits 9-18 series Plaintiffs' vendors are admitted co-sharers and none of the parties in the suit claims under them. From reading of paragraph 11(Ga) of the written statement of defendants 5 and 6 it appears that the suit land is nal and page 7 of Exhibit-E shows that IRRI paddy is cultivated there, Thus the submission of Mr Dutta that equity has come undone in the instant case because there are buildings standing therein has no basis according to admission of defendant 10 as evident from Exhibit-E. Moreover in view to validate Exhibit-F defendant 10 in paragraphs 42(Ja), (Eno) of the written statement has made out a case of bigger quantum of land with share by implicating the land of Delpara mouja to show that the vendors of Exhibit-F had interest to execute the deed in 2002 during pendency of the suit. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, we are of the view that the Commissioner has correctly prepared the report in accordance with the preliminary decree passed in the original suit and he has not gone behind or beyond the decree where a clear picture of red coloured specification is shown and nobody was aggrieved by such decree. The new case of sale as described in paragraph 4 of the objection being beyond pleading cannot be accepted. The objection appears to be devoid of substance and it does not merit any consideration and hence it is rejected. The report of the Advocate Commissioner is sound and proper and since the same has not violated any established principle of partition and is made in accordance with the preliminary decree, we are not inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree.</u>
21. Accordingly the appeal fails. Thus the appeal is dismissed and the judgment and decree under challenge is upheld.
Communicate this judgment and send down the lower Court's record,
End.

lawyer:
Syeda Nasrin with AHM Rehanul Kabir and Bibek Chandra, Advocates—For the Petitioners. 
Md Asaduzzaman Monir, DAG—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Abdul Mahn (Md) and others Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners
Vs
People's Republic of Bangladesh and others----- Defendant-Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md Zakir Hossain, J: At the instance of the petitioners, this Court was pleased to issue Rule with the following terms: "Records need not be called for. Let a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 & 2 to show cause as to why the delay of 5549 days in filing this civil revision against the judgment and decree dated 9-7-2007 (decree being drawn on 16-7-2007) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 552 of 2003 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 24-2-2003 (decree being drawn on 3-3-2003) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 437 of 2000 decreeing the suit on contest should not be condoned and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper."
2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are inter alia that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No. 437 of 2000 before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and also for declaration that the suit property is not a vested property of the Government. The plaintiffs claimed that 54 acres land from the CS Plot No. 636 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 270 in Mouja Vakurta belonged to Mon Mohon Das and Shema Dashi and SA Khatian was duly prepared in their names. Mon Mohon Das died leaving a son, Behari Lal Das and Shema Dashi died leaving sisters, son Kishore Lal Das and some lands were recorded in the name of Keshob Lal Das. RS Khatian was prepared in the name of Keshob Lal Das. Thereafter Keshob Lal Das sold out 54 decimal lands to Md Moslem Uddin on 1-1-1980 who mutated his name and paid rent to the Government. After that Moslem Uddin sold all their lands to the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs being owner have been possessing the said lands peacefully.
3. The defendant Nos.1/2 entered appearance in the suit and contested the same by filing written statement denying the material allegations set out in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and moreover, the plaintiffs have no cause of action to file this suit.
4. The case of the defendant, in short, is that the suit land was treated as a vested property by virtue of the VP Case No. 70 of 1979. The Government is the custodian of the suit land. The Government leased out the suit land to different persons. The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest over the suit land, therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs.
5. After conclusion of the trial, the learned Joint District Judge delving into the evidence on records and considering the legal position involved in this case was pleased to decree the suit by assigning cogent reason. Being aggrieved by and highly dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendant-opposite parties preferred Title Appeal No. 552 of 2003 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka. After admitting the appeal, the learned District Judge, Dhaka transmitted the record of the appeal for speedy disposal to the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka without making the appeal ready for hearing. The learned Additional District Judge without waiting for service of summons upon the respondents and without giving notice of transfer to the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners heard the appeal in their absence and allowed the appeal ex-parte by his judgment dated 9-7-2007 and set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court without assigning any cogent reason with a stroke of a pen. The plaintiff-petitioners were not at all aware as to the ex-parte decree. It is also contended that the Tadbirkar of the plaintiff-petitioners left this transitory world after passing the decree by the trial Court and by lapse of time, some of the plaintiffs also passed away. The petitioners had no knowledge about the pendency of the appeal after transferring from the Court of the learned District Judge to the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka. It is further contended that the petitioners were not aware of the ex-parte judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court. It is further contended that the petitioners being in possession of the suit land got some threats of eviction from some miscreants on 5-6-2022 and 28-6-2022. The miscreants published that they got lease from the Government. Thereafter, the petitioners were aware as to the judgment of the Appellate Court from the office of the respondent Government. It is also mentioned that the petitioners with their might and main tried their level best to contact their appointed lawyer and they did not find his address to communicate. Thereafter, the petitioners engaged a new lawyer and after incurring huge time managed to obtain the certified copy of the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The respondents are powerful man in the locality and they are using political and monetary power to dispossess the petitioners. Finding no other alternative, the petitioners were constrained to prefer the aforesaid revisional application with a petition for condonation of delay. After hearing the same, the Court was pleased to issue the aforesaid Rule.
6. Ms Syeda Nasrin, learned Advocate for the petitioners reiterated the cause of delay as embodied in the petition for condonation of delay. She submits that the aforenoted appeal was heard ex-parte and the judgment was also passed ex-parte. She submits that the tadbirkar of the plaintiff-petitioners died after the judgment of the trial Court and in the meantime, some of the plaintiffs also passed away and the petitioners had no knowledge about the pendency of the appeal after its transfer from the Court of the learned District Judge to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge for hearing the appeal.
7. She further submits that the petitioners being in possession of the suit land got some threats of eviction from some miscreants on 5-6-2022 and 28-6-2022. The miscreants told that the Government leased out the suit land in their favour, thereafter, the petitioners went to the office of the respondents wherefrom the petitioners got to know about the judgment of the Appellate Court and subsequently, the petitioners tried a lot to contact their earlier lawyer but found no trace of him. Then the petitioners engaged a new lawyer who tried her level best to collect the certified copy of the relevant records but failed to trace the record for a couple of months. It took a lot only to find out the original record of the Court.
8. The learned Advocate further submits that against the decree, the defendant-appellant-opposite parties on 1-12-2003 filed appeal being Title Appeal No. 552 of 2003 causing delay of 242 days. The appellant submitted Court-fees on 18-2-2004. The order for serving notice upon the parties was passed on 1-4-2004. It appears from Order No. 12 dated 8-5-2004 that notice upon the respondents Nos. 1-3, 5-6 returns after service as per the report of the process server, the respondents No. 6 appeared with a power and filed hazira, notice upon the respondents Nos. 4, 7-10 had not been returned, after service. On 7-6-2004, the notice upon the respondents Nos. 8 and 10 returned after service notice upon them, the notice upon the respondents Nos. 7 and 9 returned unserved and only respondent Nos. 5-7 appeared by power and no one for the appellant appeared. In this order, there is no mention as to whether the notice upon the respondent No. 4 was served or not. However, from the Order No. 14 dated 24-7-2004, it appears that the notice upon the respondent No. 4 returned unserved, and respondent Nos. 1-2 and 8-10 appeared by power and filed hazira, and on the other hand, respondent Nos. 5 and 7 filed time petition for filing written statement and there was no step on the part of the appellant. She contends that very surprisingly on the following date i.e. on 7-9-2004, the Appellate Court mentioned that "respondent filed hazira, no step was taken by the appellant upon the respondent No. 4 to 6-10-2004 for taking steps." Therefore, it is clear that no notice was served upon the respondent No. 4 and the respondent No. 3 did not appear before the Court. On the next date i.e. on 6-10-2004, it appears from Order No. 16 that the respondent filed hazira and the appellant took no step but on the same date, the Appellate Court suo motu condoned the delay and admitted the appeal and also called for the LCR without any appearance or step of the defendant-appellants. Therefore, it appears from the order that though the appellant took no step but in absence of the appellant and in presence of the learned Advocate for the respondent, the appeal was admitted by condoning the delay of 242 days by which necessarily indicates vicious and malafide connivance between the appellant and the learned advocate of the respondents.
9. The learned Advocate further submits that the law does not allow an appeal to be admitted when there was none to place the appeal before the Court; specially an appeal filed out of time should not be registered and admitted without deciding whether the appellants are entitled to the condonation of delay. In absence of the appellants, the Appellate Court can only dismiss the appeal for default and there is no scope for the Appellate Court to condone delay at its own motion when there was none for the appellant to get the application for condonation of delay heard before the Appellate Court. The learned Advocate also made submission regarding the connivance of the earlier Advocates who acted against the interest of the petitioners. The learned Advocate further added that the present revision, if the Rule is issued upon condonation of delay as per the satisfaction of this Court, involves an important question of law which has already been settled by our Apex Court in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2310 of 2018 (Bangladesh vs Md Abdul Hye and others) that "this Division declared all actions, decisions regarding listing any property as vested property after 23-3-1974 as illegal." In the present case, the defendant-appellant-opposite party Government claimed over the suit land by way of a VP Case being No. 69 of 1978; therefore in view of the aforesaid provision of law, the claim of the Government is not tenable in eye of law.
10. This Rule was opposed by the learned DAG, but the Government did not file any counter affidavit adverting the causes of delay as spelt out within the bounds of the petition for condonation of delay.
11. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the materials on record with due care and attention and seriousness as it deserves and also meticulously considered the convoluted question of law critically involved in this Case.
12. An inordinate delay has been caused in filing the civil revision against judgment of reversal whereas the trial Court decreed the suit on contest with elaborate discussion and the Appellate Court reversed the same ex-parte in a slipshod and perfunctory manner. The order sheet of the Appellate Court is annexed with the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioners to their application for condonation of delay. It appears from the subsequent Order No. 18 dated 23-2-2005 that both parties filed hazira and LCR was received. On the same date the appeal was sent to the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for speedy disposal stating that- “দ্রুত নিষ্পত্তির জন্য অত্র মামলাটি বিজ্ঞ অতিঃ জেলা ও দায়রা জজ, ১ম আদালতের বদলি করা হইল।” Resultantly, the appeal was sent to the said Court of the learned Additional District
Judge who by order No. 19 dated 5-3-2005 received the same and fixed the next date on 18-5-2005 for hearing of appeal without being ready for hearing. In this junction, it is necessary to quote section 24A of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in short 'the CPC' which reads as follows—
"Appearance of parties on transfer of suit, etc.—(1) Where any suit is transferred under section 22, or any suit, appeal or other proceeding is transferred or with-drawn under sub-section (1) of section 24 on the application of a party, the Court ordering the transfer or withdrawal shall fix a date for the appearance of the parties before itself, if the suit, appeal or other proceeding is to be tried or disposed of by itself, or before the Court to which the case is so transferred.
(2) Where any suit, appeal or other proceeding is transferred from one Court to another, otherwise than on the application of a party, the parties thereto shall appear before the Court from which the suit, appeal or other proceedings is to he transferred, on the day already fixed for their appearance before that Court, and such Court shall then communicate the order of transfer to such parties and direct them to appear before the Court to which the suit, appeal or other proceeding is to be transferred, either on the same day, or on such earliest day as may be reasonable having regard to the distance at which the other Court is located."
13. Section 24A(2) requires the transferor Court to pass such order of transfer on the day already fixed for appearing before the Court and such Court shall then communicate the order of transfer to the party and direct them to appear before the Court to which the appeal is to be transferred either on the same date or on such earliest day as may be reasonable. The necessity of "communication" of the order of transfer is the heart of this section. The most essential requirement for giving effect to this "transfer" is the communication of the order of the Court. It is not the duty of the parties rather it is the duty of the Court itself to make sure of the communication of said order. But it appears from Order No. 18 dated 23-2-2005 and Order No. 19 dated 5-3-2005 that there was no such communication of order by the Court. It also appears that in the very transfer Order No. 18 dated 23-2-2005 there was no reflection of the Court's endeavor to communicate the transfer order upon the parties, neither the transferor Court nor the transferee Court served any notice or passed any order asking for communication of the said order of transfer.
14. It further appears from the Order No. 20 dated 18-5-2005 and Order No. 21 dated 2-8-2005 that no party appeared before the Court. Order No. 22 dated 26-10-2005 shows that the appellant was present but the respondent was not. From Order No. 23 dated 9-2-2006 it shows that only the appellant was not present though the respondents were present but from Order No. 19-23 it was not clear that whether notices upon the parties or upon the lawyers were served afresh, because as shown earlier from Order Nos. 1-14 that notices upon the respondent No. 3 had remain unserved and the respondent No. 4 did not appear. Moreover, whether the notice of transfer was served upon the lawyers of the respondents or upon the parties afresh is very important, because section 24A(2) requires service of notice upon the parties and therefore notice upon the lawyers is not enough. Notice should be given to the party and not to the counsel who has no authority to receive such notice. Non-receipt of notice is a good cause for non-appearance.
15. It further appears from order No. 24 dated 4-5-2006 and order No. 25 dated 3-8-2006 that no party appeared but order No. 26 dated 19-10-2006 showed that the appellant was not present but the respondent was present. But there was no specification that which respondent was present and whether they submitted any hazira or not. Thereafter, in Order No. 27 only the appellant was present but the respondent was not present and on that very day the Appellate Court took the same for ex-parte hearing on 18-4-2007 but it was held since the Court was busy with the hearing of another case. On 27-6-2007, the appeal was heard ex-parte and thereafter, the judgment was pronounced on 9-7-2007.
16. It transpires that from the beginning that the appeal was admitted in absence of the appellant and his lawyer, but in presence of the lawyer of some of the respondents which shows a connivance and concerted practice between the learned advocates of the respondents and the appellants. It also shows that after the transfer, the transferee Court was in a hurry to dispose of the appeal in favor of the appellant without giving any reasonable notices upon the plaintiff-respondents i.e. making the appeal ready for hearing. The learned Appellate Court ought to have considered that the plaintiffs obtained decree on contest and their right to property is involved in the suit land, but the appellant Court reversed the judgment of trial Court without adverting any specific finding and observation of the trial Court. The Appellate Court allowed the appeal only on the ground:
"1 have perused the record but I do not find any original deed of the plaintiff. On the perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiff sides have withdrawn all the deeds but they did not re-file. Plaintiff side could not prove their possession over the suit land. They also could not prove their title over the suit land by filing the original deed."
17. There is legal infirmity in the said finding; since the Appellate Court itself found that the plaintiffs had withdrawn their all deeds and they did not resubmit those deeds; therefore, the Appellate Court ought to have served notice upon the plaintiff-respondents to resubmit the same. But unfortunately, the Appellate Court hurriedly disposed of the Appeal without considering the admitted documents of the plaintiffs and thereby flouted and negated the provision of order 41 Rule 31 of the CPC.
18. The requirement of section 24A of the Code of Civil Procedure is that transferee Court has to give notice to the parties and on failure to do so the resulting ex-parte decision is liable to be set-aside. In this respect, the ratio of the case of Abdul Khaleque vs Abdul Barek, 3 BLC (AD) 174 may be read for better appreciation:
"The trial Court dismissed the suit at the first instance. On appeal the decision was set-aside and the case sent back on remand for fresh trial. After the arrival of the records while the suit was lying pending for disposal in the First Court of Assistant Judge, Barisal the learned District Judge, by an order dated 15 July 1992, transferred the suit from the said Court to the second Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Barisal for disposal. There was no appearance of the contesting defendant before the transferee Court. As a result the learned Assistant Judge, Second Additional Court heard the matter ex-parte but dismissed the suit on 30 August 1992. The plaintiff took an appeal; Title Appeal No. 195 of 1992 therefrom. The appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat who reversed the decision of the trial Court and decreed the suit on 8 November 1993. Being aggrieved defendant No. 1 preferred Civil Revision No. 221 of 1994. A Single Bench of the High Court Division set-aside the decree of the Appellate Court on the view that the defendant was not informed of the transfer of the suit from the First Court of Assistant Judge, Barisal to the Second Additional Court, Barisal as required under section 24A(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure for which he could not defend his cause in the case. Accordingly, the learned Judge sent back the case on remand to the trial Court for disposal by his judgment and order dated 24 February 1997."
19. The Court is required to pass order of transfer on a date fixed for the appearance of the parties and such Court shall communicate the order to such parties and direct them to appear before the Court to which the proceeding is transferred. In the case of Rezia Sultana vs Haroon Malik, 64 DLR 347, it was held that as per provision of section 24A(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, I do not find any fact from the order sheets transferee Court after receiving the record informed the parties to the case. So these orders passed by the Courts below are bad on this count.
20. There are many cases where inordinate delay was condoned by our Apex Court on reasonable grounds where the reason of delay is well explained and the chance of suffering prejudice by the party is greater if the delay is not condoned. In the case of Abdul Kader Mondal and others vs Shamsur Rahman Chowdhury alias Shamsur Rahman Saha reported in 51 DLR (AD) 253, the Appellate Division held that the High Court Division failed to observe that refusal to condone the delay can result a meritorious matter being thrown out without any hearing whatsoever and as against him, when the delay is condoned, the worst that can happen is that a case is decided on merit after hearing the parties, the opportunity that substantial justice shall take preponderance over technical consideration ought to have been kept in view by the High Court Division in deciding whether or not there was sufficient cause for the delay in filing the appeal. In view of this decision, the delay of 4578 days were condoned by our Apex Court in Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner Rangpur vs Hasrat Mohani and others, 3 ADC (2006) 237 = 14 BLT 2006 AD 123 = 2015 (23) BLT (AD) 121. In Md Shahid Farooqui vs The Director and Member (bind and Estate Management), National Housing Authority and others, 2016 BLD (HCD) 476 the delay of 13 years was condoned. In Md Golam Hossain vs Abdus Sukur Bhuiyan and others, 2008 (16) BLT (HCD) 293 = 13 BLC 817 delay of 4198 days was condoned by the High Court Division. In Dahyabhai Chhaganlal Mehta vs Padmaben Sanmukhlal Modi, MANU/GJ/0487/ 20211 delay of 7816 delay was condoned by the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad. In Oudekraal Estates (Pty) Ltd vs The City of Cape Town and others, (20104 1 SA 333 (SCA), (2009) ZASCA 85 the Supreme Court of Appeal of South Africa maintained the condonation of delay 47 years condoned by the lower Appellate Court. In Eklimur Reza Khan vs State, 59 DLR 7 = 10 MLR (HCD) 323 though criminal matter, delay of 4132 days was condoned.
<u>21. On perusal of the order sheets of the Appellate Court, it is as clear as day light that without servicing notice upon some respondents, the appeal was hastily heard ex-parte and without reversing the findings of the trial Court and without considering the evidence of the plaintiffs and without any independent assessment of evidence on record, the appeal was allowed ex-parte and thereby the long standing principle of disposal of the civil appeal has been flouted and, as such, the justice has been put in the ground. Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 has delineated to the effect that an appeal or application for a revision or a review of judgment or for leave to appeal or any other application to which this section may be made applicable by or under any enactment for the time being in force may be admitted after the period of limitation prescribed; therefore, when the appellant or applicant satisfies the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application with in such period. The expression of sufficient cause occurred in the provision has not been defined therein. Sufficient cause means the cause which is beyond the control of the person who wants to surmount the duty of proving the cause sufficiently to file appeal or revision or any other application. It may be man-made or an act of God. In the case of Md Golam Hossain vs Abdus Sukur Bhuiyan and others reported in 2008 (16) BLT (HCD) 293 = 13 BLC 817, it was held:</u>
<u>"The expression "sufficient cause" occurring in section 5 of The Limitation Act should, therefore, be considered with pragmatism in justice-oriented approach rather than the technical detention of sufficient cause for explaining every days's delay. It is pointed here that sometimes delay of shortest range may be uncondonable due to want of acceptable explanation; whereas in certain other cases delay of very long range can be condoned as the explanation thereof is very satisfactory. Once the Court accepts explanation as sufficient it is characterized as result of positive exercise of discretion. The Court is to decide the matters on merit unless the case is hopelessly without merit. Whether delay in presenting a proceeding before a Court of law is to be condoned or not is to be decided by its own facts and circumstances."</u>
22. In the case reported in, it PLD 2002 SC 84 was held: "Condonation of delay on ground of nullity of the order appealed against, can be allowed only if the order was without jurisdiction. The power of the appellate authority to decide the case on merits will not be hinged by any consideration of limitation, if the order appealed against is found to be a nullity. It means that where on merit the respondent has no case, then limitation would not be a hurdle in the way of appellant for getting justice."
23. My final conclusion is as under:
i. The Appeal No. 552 of 2003 was barred by limitation and the delay was condoned without hearing the respondents by the learned District Judge, Dhaka.
ii. The learned District Judge, Dhaka without making the appeal ready for hearing sent down the records of the appeal to the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka. It transpires from the order sheets of the Appeal that notice upon all the respondents were not duly served, nonetheless, the learned District judge transmitted the record to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge for speedy disposal. The learned Additional District Judge without making the appeal ready for hearing and without serving notice upon some respondents, most hurriedly allowed the appeal on ex-parte, thereby, set-aside the long cherished and hard earned decree of the plaintiff-petitioners with a stroke of a pen.
iii. The ex-parte judgment and decree of the Appellate Court appears to be repugnant to the existing law of the land.
iv. No notice was issued upon the respondents while the learned District Judge transferred the record of the Appeal to the Court of the learned Additional District Judge and thereby flouted the mandatory provision of section 24A(2) of the CPC.
v. The delay took place due to man-made cause.
vi. If the judgment and decree of the trial Court and the Appellate Court are considered in juxtaposition it appears that without reversing the finding of the trial Court, the Appellate Court indifferently allowed the Appeal ex-parte and thereby set-aside the judgment of the trial Court, therefore, the legality and chastity of the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court cannot be examined unless the aforesaid delay is condoned.
vii. If the delay is not condoned, meritorious case may be thrown to the street and the alleged lessees shall grasp the property without any valid title.
viii. The judgment of the Appellate Court is not well balanced but lopsided and therefore, it should be examined by the judicial authority.
ix. It is true that foreign judgments referred to by the learned Advocate are not binding to us, nevertheless, they have some persuasive value.
x. The Court should not be afraid of seeing the long delay in preferring appeal or revision but the concerned Court has to examine the facts and circumstances of the case keeping in mind, the dictum that no two cases are similar and significant facts and elements of the case may change the entire edifice of the case.
xi. If the delay is not condoned, I am of the view that a meritorious case be thrown to the street and consequently, it may cause serious prejudice to the petitioner who obtained the decree on contest.
xii. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the explanation given regarding the delay of 5,549 days in preferring this revisional application appears to be sufficient and reasonable. Accordingly, the Rule deserves to be made absolute.
24. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without passing any order as to costs. The delay of 5,549 days in filing the revisional application is hereby condoned.
The Office is directed to do the needful.
End.
