Uzzal Bhowinick Advocate —For she Petthones
Abu Mohammad Amin Uddin with Sudipta Arjun, Advocates—For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Sajjadul Karim Palash (Md) ...Defendant No.65-Petitioner
VS
Khairul Islam and others others. Defendant No. 21-22-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant (No. 65) petitioner Md Sajjadul Karim Palash calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-2 Khaind Islam and another to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 7-11-2021, passed by the learned District Judge, Sylhet in Civil Revision No. 30 of 2021 allowing the said revision filed against the order dated 14-3-2021, passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2018 cancelling the report of delivery of possession submitted by the nazir in the said execution case arising out of a final decree dated 14-6-2018 and preliminary decree dated 7-8-2016, passed in Title Suit No. 179 of 2020, should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may deem fit and proper.
2. Relevant facts for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party No. 3 Foyzunnessa Khanom as plaintiff instituted the suit No. 179 of 2010 praying for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the 2nd schedule land, for partition claiming saham over 2nd schedule of land, for declaration of title with confirmation of possession, that the decree passed in Title Suit No, 30 of 1998 is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff and for permanent injunction in respect of 2nd schedule land against the defendants.
3. The defendant Nos. 21-22 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material averments made in the plaint.
4. The suit was decreed on 31-7-2016 in preliminary form on contest against the defendant Nos. 21 and 22 and compromise against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in terms of solenama and ex-purse against the rest of the defendants including defendant No. 65.
5. On the basis of preliminary decree, the learned Advocate Biprodas Bhattacharjee was appointed as Advocate commissioner who submitted Advocate commission report on 29-3- 20 18, On the basis of that report, final decree was drawn up on 14-6-2018. Thereafter, the defendant Nos. 21 and 22 filed an Execution Case No. 2 of 2018 on 15-11-2018. Writ was issued to the nazir for delivery of possession. Accordingly, the nazir delivered the possession to the defendant Nos. 21-25 and submitted report on 19-2-2020. On 22-3-2020 the defendant No. 65 filed written objection claiming that the plaintiff sold out her 0.16 acre of land to defendant No. 64 vide registered kabala dated 9-2-2017 and delivered possession to the defendant No. 64, but the nazir illegally on the basis of erroneous Advocate commission report delivered possession to the defendant Nos. 21-25 demolishing wall situated in the 2nd schedule land. He also claimed that the commissioner report. chita, field book, sketch map prepared by the Advocate commissioner are erroneous which show a gulf of disparity and, as such, do not agree with the preliminary decree.
6. The trial court by the impugned order considered the written objection on 14-3-2001 and cancelled the report of delivery of possession submitted by the nazir. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order, the defendant Nos. 21-22 filed Civil Revision No. 30 of 2021 which was allowed by the learned District Judge, Sylhet on 7- 1 1-2021 by setting aside the order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge, the defendant No. 65 filed this revisional application and obtained the present Rule.
7. Mr Uzzal Bhowmick, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the Advocate commissioner's report was not prepared in conformity with the preliminary decree. He further submits that as per preliminary decree the plaintiff got 2nd schedule of land as saham measuring an area of 0.16 acre of land, the defendant Nos. 64-65 got 0.97 acre of land and the defendant Nos. 21-25 got 0_73 acre of land as their saham from the I st schedule of land. He adds that the advocate commissioner had to prepare the field book, chita, sketch-map showing the 2nd schedule of land measuring an area of 0.16 acre of land as saham of the plaintiff and allotting 0.73 acre of land as saham of the defendant Nos. 21-25 and 0.97 acre of land as saham of the defendant Nos. 64-65 from the 1st schedule of land as has been decreed in preliminary Form in the original suit. He also adds that the advocate commissioner erroneously has only allotted the saham in furtherance of the defendant Nos. 21-25 as it appears from the Advocate commission report and on the basis of that erroneous advocate commission report, the trial court erroneously passed the defective, incomplete and erroneous final decree and drawn up the same in the original suit which is an error of law and that should be amended by setting aside the final decree to secure the ends of justice. 8. In support of his contention, he cited the decisions passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Mosharrcif Hossain Chowdhury being dead his heirs 1(a) Najib Chowarury and other vs illoaz:ern Hossain Chowdhury and others reported in 2011 (19) BLT (HCD) 15 and Ismail Ullah and others vs Sulcumar Des reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 251 = 38 DLR (AD) 125.
9. On the other hand, Mr Sudipta Arjun, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1-2, submits that the advocate commissioner has not committed any mistake or error in preparing his commission report rather the report was prepared rightly and on the basis of that report final decree was duly drawn up by the Trial Court. Moreover, he submits that the petitioner had to file an appeal against the final decree and in absence of taking such measures; the petitioner had no option to challenge the report of the delivery of possession submitted by nazir. He further submits that as per writ issued by the executine court, the nazir delivered possession to the defendant Nos. 21-22 pursuant to their saham and he also adds that the defendant Nos. 64-65 illegally filed an objection for cancellation of nazir's report which was illegally considered and accepted by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet. Against that order the defendant Nos. 21-22 filed revision being No. 30 of 2021 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet which was allowed legally on 7-11-2021, reversing the order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet. The learned Advocate Mr Sudipta Arjun strongly contends that the final decree cannot be set-aside by this revisional court for amending the same since the proceeding has been started from execution case, not against the final decree. And therefore, there is no scope to reopen the matter again in this revision. He also contends that the defendant No. 65 did not disclose that defendant No.64 purchased the 2nd schedule land rather he suppressed it till drawing up of the final decree on 29-6-2018. He finally adds that the petitioner did not come to the court with clean hand and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.
10. In support of his contention, he cited the decisions passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Abdur Rabman and others vs Sultan (i Sultan and others reported in 35 DLR (AD) 51 and It Shahidur Rahman Ivlajunider and others vs Stthirunnessa and others reported in 1996 BLD (AD) 50 - 1 BLC (AD) 43.
11. 1 have heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and perused the materials on record meticulously.
12. In this revision important questions of law have been raised:
(i) Whether this revisional court has jurisdiction to set-aside a final decree drawn up not inconformity with the preliminary judgment and decree due to error apparent on the face of the record against which no amendment petition was filed or appeal was preferred and
(ii) Whether the final decree of the Partition Suit No. 179 of 2010 was passed as per definition contained in section 2(2) and final decree was drawn up in accordance with the provisions contained in Order 20 Rule 6 ( I) and 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
13. Section 2(2) defines: "decree" means the formal expression of an adjudication which, so far as regards the Court expressing it, conclusively determines the rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit and may be either preliminary or final. Explanation under section 2(2):
"A decree is preliminary when further proceedings have to be taken before the suit can be completely disposed of. It is final when such adjudication completely disposes of the suit. It may be partly preliminary and partly final."
Order 20 provides provisions as to the judgment and decree_ According to Order 20 Rule 6(1):"
The decree shall agree with the judgment; it shall contain the number of the suit, the names and descriptions of the parties, and particulars of the claim, and shall specify clearly the relief granted or other determination of the suit."
14. According to Order 20 Rule 7: "The decree shall bear date the day on which the judgment was pronounced, and, when the Judge has satisfied himself that the decree has been drawn up in accordance with the judgment, he shall sign the decree."
15. On perusal of the record it appears that preliminary decree clearly stated the saham of the plaintiff, defendant Nos. 21-25 and defendant Nos. 64165. But learned advocate commissioner, without showing the sahams of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 64-65, has allotted only the saham of defendant Nos. 21-25 in the report, chita, field book and sketch map. As a result, the commission report is defective, incomplete and erroneous. On the basis of that report, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet made the preliminary decree final and drawn up the same.
16. It also appears that on the basis of defective, incomplete and erroneous final decree, the defendant Nos. 21-22 filed an Execution Case No. 2 of 2018 wherein the trial court issued writ to the nazir for delivery of possession to the defendant Nos. 21-25. In the petition of execution case, it appears, schedule Nos. 1 and 2 were included in the execution case. As per preliminary decree, the defendant Nos. 21-25 were entitled to get their saham only from the 1st schedule of land. The defective, incomplete and erroneous final decree did not include the 2nd schedule of land, inspite of that it could not be understood why the defendant Nos. 21-22 prayed for execution including the 2nd schedule of the suit land which is a separate piece of land wherein the plaintiff got permanent injunction and which exclusively falls under the saham of the plaintiff as per judgment and preliminary decree. The 2nd schedule of land was subsequently purchased by the defendant No. 64 by a registered deed No. 430 dated 9-2-2017 before filing of the Execution Case No. 2 of 2018. The learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner contended that the defendant Nos, 21-22 intentionally and purposely included the 2nd schedule land in the execution case No.2 of 2018. I find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
17. From the order dated 14-3-2021, it appears that the learned Senior Assistant Judge cancelled the delivery of possession report submitted by the nazir on the grounds that the civil court commissioner CW-2 Mr Sanjib Dana did not peruse the judgment and decree of the original suit and it could not be understandable on what basis the civil court commissioner identified and measured the saham of the plaintiff, defendant Nos. 21-25 and defendant Nos. 64-65. In fact, it is found that the saham of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 64-65 were not shown in the Advocate commission report submitted by the Advocate commissioner Biprodas Bhaitacharjee. As a result, the final decree does not determine the saham of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 64-65.
18. As per definition of decree under section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, it shall conclusively determine the rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit, According to explanation contained in section 2(2) a decree is preliminary when further proceedings have to be done before disposal of the suit. Moreover, it is final when such adjudication completely disposed of the suit. The final decree passed in Title Suit No. 179 of 2010 did not determine the rights of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 64-65 conclusively and the suit was not disposed of with complete adjudication, inasmuch as, the final decree did not contain the saham of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 64-65,
19. In pursuant to the provision contained in rule 6(1) of order 20, the decree shall agree with the judgment. Moreover, it shall, inter cilia, specify clearly the relief granted or other determination of the suit. But the final decree drawn up in the Title Suit No. 179 of 2010 does not specify or determine the relief granted in favour of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 64-65 in conformity with the preliminary decree. As such the final decree passed in the Title Suit No. 179 of 2001 does not agree with the preliminary decree as per Wile 6(1) of Order 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
20. Under rule 7 of order 20, the judge shall sign the decree after being satisfied that the decree has been drawn up in accordance with the judgment. But it is apparent on the face of the record that the final decree was not signed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge after being satisfied that the final decree was prepared in accordance with the judgment passed in preliminary form in the suit No. 179 of 2010 which is also an error of law and violation of rule 7 of order 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
21. Section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides provisions as to amendment of judgments, decrees or orders which runs as follows:
"Clerical or arithmetical mistakes in judgment, decrees or orders or errors arising therein from any accidental slip or omission may at any time be corrected by the Court either of its own motion or on the application of any of the parties."
22. So, as per provision of section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure judgments, decrees or orders may be corrected or amended at any time due to mistake or error by the court either of its own motion or on the application of any of the parties. No party came forward to file any application to amend the final decree in the Title Suit No. 179 of 2010 and the question was not raised before the learned Senior Assistant Judge or learned District Judge and nor they raised the question themselves that the erroneous final decree should be amended. This question came to the notice of this court at the time of Rule hearing that the final decree passed in Title Suit No. 179 of 2010 was not drawn up in accordance with the preliminary decree which is an error of law.
23. In the case of RMKRM  Samasundaram Chetty vs MRMVL Subirmaniam Cherry reported in AIR 1926 PC 136 the Privy Council reiterated the principle as follows:
"The only cases in which the Court can interfere after the passing and entering of the judgment are (1) where there has been an accident or slip in the judgment as drawn up, in which case the Court has power to rectify it; and (2) where the Court itself finds the judgment as drawn up does not correctly state what the Court actually decided and intended."
Similar view was taken by the Calcutta High Court in the case of CR Mukhopadhya vs SAISB Debi reported in AIR 1924 Cal 895 and held that it is the duty of the court to amend the decree as it is brought to the notice that it does not agree with the judgment. Necessary amendments were made in that Case.
24. In the Title Suit No. 179 of 2010, the learned Senior Assistant Judge decided in the preliminary decree that the plaintiff would exclusively get 2nd schedule land measuring an area of 0.16 acre exclusively and from the 1st schedule of land, the defendant Nos. 21-25 would get 0.73 acre and the defendant Nos. 64-65 would get 0.97 acre of land as their saham. Under such circumstances, it was the legal duty of the Senior Assistant Judge to draw up the same as per their sahams. But erroneously plaintiff's saham and saham of the defendant Nos. 64 and 65 were not determined and included in the final decree.
25. It is pertinent to mention here that the different High Courts of India had taken uniform view that the Court can always amend the decree, if there is a mistake that had crept in, for bringing the decree in conformity with the judgment.
26. It appears from the facts of the case of Ullah being dead his heirs Baziullah and others vs Sukumar Das reported in 1986 BLD (AD) 251 = 38 DLR (RD) 115 that mistake was committed in the preliminary decree against which no appeal was filed. Thereafter, preliminary decree was drawn up. Subsequently, the question of mistake in the preliminary decree as well as final decree was raised. The Hon'ble lordships set-aside the judgments of the Courts below and directed to amend the decree so as to bring it in conformity with the judgment excluding first schedule land of the written statement of that case.
27. The learned Advocate for the petitioner also referred the case of Mosarraf Hossain Chowdhury being dead his heirs ..1(a) Najb Chowdhury and others vs Moazzern Hossain Chowdhury and others reported in 2011 (19) BLT (HCD) page 15. In that suit, the learned Joint District Judge decreed the suit in preliminary form and allotted Saharn of 3 acres of land to the plaintiffs and 6 acres of land to the defendant No. 1. Art advocate Commissioner was appointed for allotment of the Saharn. The report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner was accepted and final decree was drawn up. Thereafter, the petitioners filed an application under section 151/152 of the Code of Civil Procedure for correction of the final decree, without filing appeal against that final decree, on the grounds that the final decree was drawn up not in conformity with the preliminary decree and that the Advocate Commissioner performed the commission beyond their knowledge and allotted lands to the plaintiffs from the lands in possession of the defendant No.1 who has multi-storied building thereon. The learned Joint District Judge rejected the said application which was affirmed by the learned District Judge and against which Civil Revision No. 2414 of 2008 was filed and obtained the Rule which was made absolute by the Hon'ble Lordship. In that case Hon'ble Lordship held that the Courts below on superficial consideration of the Advocate Commissioner's report rejected the defendant's application for amendment of the final decree which has been apparently drawn up beyond the preliminary decree. Although the appeal was not filed by the defendants, the Hon'ble Lordship made the rule absolute and set-aside the impugned judgments including the final decree with a direction to draw
Up a final decree in accordance with the preliminary decree by appointing fresh Advocate Commissioner, if it is necessary.
<u>28. It has been held in the case of Pathan vs Poonrulli. A 19701 57 that even in the absence of any move by the parties the Court can stio-nrotu make the correction. It is confined only to the kind of mistakes, errors, slips of omissions mentioned therein. Where the decree is not in conformity with the judgment the Court can order correction even when the decree has been executed and fully satisfied. It is held in the case of Kudu vs Bhim. A 1950 P 183 that Commissioners' mistake in totaling area embodied in decree may be corrected. Decision has been passed in the case of Narayan Das vs Bishnu. A 1963 that a decree can be corrected, even when it is executed. In the light of the decision passed in the case of Adinarayana vs Kothanda, A 1940, the High Court can interfere with in special circumstances in revision. It is held in the case of Chandra vs Sudhangshu A 1924 C 895.28 CWN 873 that it is the duty of the Court to amend the decree when it is brought to its notice that it does not agree with the judgment and the power was held to be discretionary.</u>
<u>29. In the light of the above decisions held by the Hon'ble Apex Court and discussion made above, it is decided that the revisional Court has jurisdiction to set-aside a final decree drawn up not inconformity with the judgment and preliminary decree due to error apparent on the face of the record against which no application was filed or appeal was preferred. It is also decided that the final decree in Title Suit No. 179 of 2010 was not passed as per provision of section 2(2) of the CPC and was not drawn up in accordance with the provisions of order 20 rules 6(1) and 7 of the CPC.</u>
30. It is worthy to mention here that the cases referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite party are not applicable in the instant suit inasmuch as the facts and circumstances of the instant suit and facts and circumstances of the cases referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite party are not same.
<u>31. It comes to the notice of this Court that the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet without applying his judicial mind has drawn up the final decree on the basis of defective, incomplete and erroneous Advocate commissioner's report which was beyond the preliminary decree. As such the courts below committed errors of law resulting in errors in their decisions occasioning failure of justice.</u>
32. In the light of the discussions made above, the two questions related to law are decided in favour of the petitioner.
33. Considering all the corners I find merit in the Rule which should be made absolute.
34. Hence, it is
Ordered
That the rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.
The impugned judgment and orders including the final decree are hereby set-aside. The trial court is directed to draw up a fresh final decree in pursuant to the preliminary decree by appointing another Advocate commissioner having clear knowledge with regard to the matter concerned for allotment of the sahams inconformity with the preliminary judgment and decree.
The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.
Copy of this judgment be sent to the concerned court at once.
End.

lawyer:
Mrinal Kanti Biswas with Md Aktaruzzaman, Binoy Krishna Poddar, Abdullah-al-all-Afzal and Biroza Mala, Advocates—For the Appellants.

VS

full_judgment:
Md Ali Reza, J: These two appeals are taken up together for analogous hearing pursuant to order dated 25-11-2008 and accordingly are disposed of by this common judgment.
2. Sole defendant Bilquis Jahan has preferred First Appeal No. 299 of 2007. On the other hand plaintiffs Syed Abdul Hafiz and Mijanur Rahman have preferred First Appeal No. 309 of 2007. Those two appeals arose out of the judgment and decree dated 18-6-2007 passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 34 of 2005. Initially Title Suit No. 44 of 2002 was filed in the Court of Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka on 17-3-2002 and subsequently on transfer on 9-6-2005 it was registered as Title Suit No. 34 of 2005.
3. The suit was filed for declaration of title on the basis of purchase and adverse possession, confirmation of possession, alternatively for recovery of khas possession and also for permanent injunction. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land measuring 0.1093 acres appertaining to RS plot 8187 of RS Khatian 926 corresponding to SA plot 5329 of SA khatian 2132 originated from CS plot 143 of CS khatian 13021 of mouja Lalbagh belonged to Sheikh Nanna. CS plot 143 contains 0.2256 acres of land from which Sheikh Nanna transferred 0.1163 acres of land to the father of plaintiff 1 before SA operation. While Nanna was owner in possession in remaining 0.1093 acres died leaving behind 05(five) sons named Chand Miah, Chunnu Miah, Sona Miah, Bachchu Miah and Suruj Miah. Chand Miah died leaving behind 2(two) sons named Tara Miah, Pier Ali and 2(two) daughters named Dulari Begum and Kosturi Begum. Tara Miah died leaving behind 03(three) sons named Rahman Miah, Badal Miah and Iqbal Miah. Chunnu Miah died leaving behind 1(one) daughter Anarzadi Begum. Sona Miah died leaving behind 1(one) son Babul Miah and I (one) daughter Piyari Begum. Bachchu Miah died leaving behind 1(one) son Solaiman Miah and 1(one) daughter Nurjahan Begum. Suruj Miah died leaving behind wife Irani Begum, 03(three) sons named Tara Miah, Kalu Miah and Abdul Kader and 05(five) daughters named Jabeda Begum, Meherun Begum, Hasna Begum, Rashida Begum and Rehana Begum. All the descendants of late Nanna Miah executed an unregistered agreement for sale of the suit land on 25-6-1991 to the plaintiffs at a consideration of Taka 5,00,000 (five lac) from which Taka 1,00,000 (one lac) was paid as earnest money. Subsequently, the rest Taka 4,00,000 (four lac) was paid on 19-6-1993, 15-6-1995, 10-6-1997, 13-1-2000 and ultimately document in favour of the plaintiffs was executed and registered on 13-1-2000. On 15-1-2001 plaintiffs came to know from the settlement office that defendant mutated and separated her name in respect of the suit land. The vendors of the plaintiffs gave the photo copy of the SA record prepared in the name of Sheikh Nanna. Meanwhile, the city survey record was prepared in the name of Jahanara against which plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Case No. 651 of 2000 under Rule 30 of the State Acquisition Rules but plaintiffs failed in the case on 7-6-2000. Then they preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 13149 of 2000 which was also disallowed. Defendant threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession on 25-1-2001. Then plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 103 of 2001 for permanent injunction in the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka. The suit was withdrawn on 7-3-2002 with liberty to sue afresh. Now the present Title Suit No. 44 of 2002 was filed on 17-3-2002 and the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 34 of 2005 showing cause of action arose in the suit on 07-6-2000, 15-1-2001, 25-1-2001 and 7-3-2002.
4. Sole defendant appeared and contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Devendra and Surendra filed Mortgage Suit No. 9 of 1919 against Satyendra and Monosha in the Court of 4th Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and got decree. Decree-holders filed Decree Execution Case No. 154 of 1919 and auction was held on 3-6-1920 and Birendra alias Dhirendra purchased the same in the benami of Jogendra which was confirmed by the Court on 10-7-1920. There-after, Jogendra executed a deed of relinquish-ment on 20-3-1922 to Birendra who sold 6(six) kathas from the west side of CS plot No. 143 to Ram Gopal by kabala dated 29-8-1923 and delivered possession. Ram Gopal sold the suit land to Jahanara by kabala dated 29-9-1942 and delivered possession. SA khatian 2132 was correctly prepared in the name of Jahanara in respect of suit land measuring 0.1090 acres in SA plot 5329 with reference to holding number 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Dhaka. Then Jahanara died on 10-2-1965 leaving behind husband Abdul Majid, 3(three) sons named Tariqul, Reazul, Enamul and 3(three) daughters named Khurshid Jahan, Kamar Jahan and defendant Bilquis Jahan. Majid then died on 10-12-1976. Khurshid Jahan also died in 1987. Thereafter, defendant and Enamul filed Title Suit No. 235 of 1989 for partition in the 2nd Subordinate Judge Court, Dhaka against Tariqul, Reazul, Kamar Jahan which ended in compromise on 24-3-1991 and the suit land exclusively fell into the saham of the defendant. Subsequently, she mutated her name in separate khatian No. 2132 on 19-11-1991 by Separation Case No. 1992 of 1991-92 and has been maintaining title and possession upon payment of rent and other taxes. Subsequently in Certificate Case No. 17 of 1997-98 defendant paid Taka 10,222.45 on 13-6-1999 by rent receipt 496817. It is further stated that enhanced rate was realised from the defendant considering the suit land as commercial for which defendant filed Land Development Case No. 30 of 1999 to reduce the rent treating the suit land as residential and the case was allowed. During liberation war the original documents of Mortgage Suit, sale certificate, writ of delivery of possession, nadabi document, 1923 document, 1942 document, rent receipt, holding taxes were lost. The city survey DP khatian 5140 was prepared in the name of the defendant against which plaintiff filed Objection Case No. 651 of 2000 under Rule 30 which was rejected on 7-6-2000. Then plaintiffs filed Appeal Case No. 13149 of 2000 under Rule 31 which was also rejected on 24-1-2001. Plaintiffs admitted the address of defendant in 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Lalbag in the memorandum of Miscellaneous Appeal. The second schedule of plaint and decree of Mortgage Suit No. 9 of 1919 attracts the land covered by CS plot 143. Defendant and her predecessors have been maintaining title and possession in the suit land upon payment of taxes and all utility bills for more than 80(eighty) years within the knowledge of others. Plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land and the suit being false is liable to be dismissed with cost.
5. The trial Court framed as many as 06(six) issues as to maintainability, whether the suit is barred under Article 144 of the Limitation Act, whether the plaintiffs have title in the suit land, whether the plaintiffs have possession until dispossession, whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get the relief as prayed for.
6. During trial plaintiff examined 03 (three) witnesses and defendant examined 06(six) witnesses and both the parties adduced documentary evidence in order to prove their respective cases.
7. The trial Court dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 18-6-2007 on the finding that the certified copy of the SA khatian (Exhibit 2) was not issued by the proper authority but the certified copy of the SA khatian (Exhibit C) prepared in the name of Jahanara was duly issued and it supports possession of Jahanara and further found that admittedly the suit land is situated at 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Dhaka for which rent and taxes are paid by the defendant through series of exhibits and those are evidence of possession and collateral evidence of title which prevail over RS khatian (Exhibit 3). The Court found that plaintiffs failed to prove their or their predecessors' possession and RS record has no basis. The Court further found that the plaintiffs also failed to prove their dispossession from the suit land and the suit is not maintainable and also found that Exhibit 2 does not correspond to CS khatian 13021 (Exhibit 1) and again found that Exhibit 6 shows that execution was done on 16-1-2000 but the document was presented for registration on 13-1-2000 which is absurd and also found that defendant did not file the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession and the nadabi document does not confer title and since plaintiffs or their predecessors were not parties to Title Suit No. 235 of 1989, Jahanara Begum did not acquire any title and accordingly both the parties have failed to prove their title over the suit land.
8. As against the same defendant Bilquis Jahan preferred First Appeal No. 299 of 2007 and plaintiffs Syed Abdul Hafiz and Mijanur Rahman preferred First Appeal No. 309 of 2007.
9. Mr Mrinal Kanti Biswas, learned Advocate appearing with Advocates Mr Md Aktaruzzaman and Ms. Biroza Mala for the appellant (hereinafter be called as defendant) of First Appeal No. 299 of 2007 submits that the trial Court was wrong in finding that the defendant failed to prove her title to the suit land and such finding is apparently illegal and uncalled for and required to be reversed. The finding on the deed of relinquishment dated 10-12-1921 is a blunder and the Court misjudged the document which is not tenable in the eye of law. He further submits that the trial Court failed to appreciate that many documents including the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession were lost during liberation war and adverse finding upon such documents are misconceived when long possession of the defendant in the suit land is evidently found. He also submits that the observation along with the finding arrived at by the Joint District Judge in respect of title of defendant is against the evidence on record and the same being misconceived and illegal is liable to be reversed and set-aside. He lastly submits that there are good grounds in the appeal and the same might be allowed. In support of his submission he referred the cases of Golzar Ali Pramanik vs Saburjan Bewa, reported in 6 BLC (AD) 41; Moksed Ali Mondal vs Abdus Samad Mondal, reported in 9 BLC (AD) 220; Government of Bangladesh vs Md Sharif Uddin reported in 22 BLC (AD) 204; Shishir Kanti Pal vs Nur Muhammad reported in 55 DLR (AD) 39.
10. Learned Advocate Mr Mansur Habib, appearing on behalf of the appellants (hereinafter called as plaintiff) of First Appeal No. 309 of 2007 submits that the trial Court erred in law in dismissing the suit beyond the evidence and law. He submits that the trial Court ought to have decided that plaintiffs being purchaser from the successive heirs of CS tenant Sheikh Nanna hold good title and the finding on possession of the plaintiffs is wrong and beyond the evidence on record. The witnesses of plaintiffs prove the possession in accordance with the law and the finding that the suit is not maintainable for want of possession is wrong. He submits that the SA record submitted by the defendant has got no basis and defendant has no title and possession in the suit land. He finally submits that since there is merit in the appeal the same would be allowed.
11. We have heard the learned Advocates and perused the pleadings of the parties and the evidence on record and also gone through the grounds taken in the appeals as well as the judgment passed by the Court below.
12. Defendant's case starts with a suit for recovery of money of a mortgage of the year of 1917 filed by Devendra against Satyendra and others. That was Title Suit No. 180 of 1917 filed on 23-4-1917 before the CS record was finally published in the Calcutta Gazette for the concerned area on 26-6-1917. The suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 240 of 1917 and finally as Title Suit No. 9 of 1919 by Order No. 27 dated 9-1-1919. The identity of the present suit land with boundary is found in schedule 2 of the plaint and decree of that suit which are Exhibit B series wherein it is mentioned that the land within the boundary is "mudafate Gobinda Moisal" which in other words means "in the name of Gobinda Moisal". Title Suit No. 9 of 1919 was decreed on 15-1-1919 and final decree was passed on 21-8-1919 Exhibit B(iii). Decree-holder filed Execution Case No. 154 of 1919 and auction was held on 3-6-1920 and Birendra purchased the same in the benami of his cousin's son Jagendra which was confirmed by the Court on 17-7-1920. Jagendra acknowledging ownership of Birendra executed and registered a deed of relinquishment on 20-3-1922 (Exhibit T) in respect of all lands including the suit land covered by Exhibit B(iii). Jagendra then sold the suit land situated at the west side of CS plot 143 to Ram Gopal Roy by kabala dated 29-8-1923 (Exhibit U) and delivered possession. Ram Gopal subsequently transferred the same in favour of defendant's mother Jahanara by kabala dated 22-9-1942 (Exhibit V) and delivered possession. Accordingly SA record 2132 (Exhibit C) comprising plot No. 5329 was prepared in her name with reference to holding number 4 Hosseni Dalan Road, Dhaka. Jahanara died in 1965 leaving behind husband Majid and 03(three) sons namely Tariqul, Reazul, Enamul and 03(three) daughters Khurshid Jahan, Kamar Jahan and defendant Bilkis Jahan. Majid and Khurshid Jahan died later on. For the convenience of possession in the joint property defendant and brother Enamul filed Title Suit No. 235 of 1989 for partition against brothers Tariqul, Reazul and sister Kamar Jahan and according to item 4 of the decree (Exhibit D series) the suit land fell in the saham of this defendant. There was arrear of rent for the year 1398 BS to 1405 BS for which Certificate Case No. 70 of 1997-98 started and accordingly notice (Exhibit F) was served and arrear of Taka 10222.45 was paid on 12-3-1998 by receipt number 896902 and the case was disposed of as evident from Exhibit H. Subsequently defendant filed Land Development Tax Case No. 30 of 1999 for decrease the rent of the suit land and the Assistant Commissioner reassessed the rent which is Exhibit I. City Survey DP khatian 5140 with plot No. 2065 (Exhibit J) was also prepared in the name of the defendant. Plaintiffs filed Objection Case No. 651 of 2000 against Exhibit J but failed (Exhibit L). Plaintiff also failed in the following Appeal Case No. 13149 of 2000 (Exhibit N). Defendant filed rent, tax, utility bills (Exhibit G, 0 series, P series, Q series).
13. Plaintiffs claimed that they have entered into an agreement with the descendants of CS tenant Sheikh Nanna on 25-6-1991 wherein consideration was fixed at Taka 5,00,000 (five lac) and 1,00,000 (one lac) as earnest money was given on that day. Subsequently, on 19-6-1993, 15-6-1995, 10-6-1997 they paid Taka 3,00,000 (three lac) and on 13-1-2000 the rest Taka 1,00,000 (one lac) was paid and the kabala in respect of the suit land was executed and registered on that day.
14. On 15-1-2001 plaintiff went to the local settlement office and came to know that the suit land was mutated and separated in the name of the defendant. Later on when the city survey khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant they filed Objection Case No. 651 of 2000 in the settlement office but plaintiffs lost in the said case on 7-6-2000. As against the same plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 13149 of 2000 and the appeal was also disallowed. On 25-1-2001 defendant threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession for which Title Suit No. 103 of 2001 was filed for permanent injunction and due to formal defect the suit was withdrawn on 7-3-2002 with liberty to sue afresh and the present suit for declaration of title by purchase and adverse possession and for further declaration that the documents, judgment and decree of the defendant are illegal, fraudulent, collusive, inoperative, mere paper transaction and not binding upon the plaintiffs along with confirmation of possession and alternatively for recovery of khan possession and also for permanent injunction was filed on 17-3-2002.
<u>15. The title document of the plaintiffs dated 13-1-2000 is filed in original and the same is Exhibit 6. There are as many as 20(twenty) executants in the kabala who are the successive heirs of CS tenant Sheikh Nanna. There is a reference of an agreement dated 25-6-1991 in the kabala. Plaintiff did not offer any explanation for not filing the agreement in order to prove the passing of consideration money. From perusal of the kabala it comes into view that all the executants reside in different addresses other than the address of the suit land. Exhibit-6 was executed and presented for registration on 13-1-2000 and the document itself shows that the same was registered on 13-1-2000. But it appears that Pear Ali, Soleman Miah and Nurjahan Begum being executants 1, 10 and 11 respectively executed the document on 16-1-2000. The document is shown to be registered without some of the vendors. It is incredible that how the sub-registrar proceeded with the registration process with the endorsement seals and sign violating the registration rules. It is a fraud upon registration. This is not a document registered in accordance with the law and the same is a forged, fraudulent, collusive and void document.</u>
<u>16. The prayer portion of the plaint shows that the plaintiff made a simultaneous claim of declaration of title on the basis of purchase and adverse possession. It is the settled principle of law that declaration of title on the basis of a document and adverse possession cannot go together because such claim conflicts with each other. In paragraph 4 of the plaint it has been stated that all the heirs of Sheikh Nanna have been in possession in the suit land. In paragraph 7 it has been stated that defendant might dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land at any time. The last dates of cause of action are 25-1-2001 and 7-3-2002 and the suit was filed on 17-3-2002. PW 1 stated in examination-in-chief that the holding number of the suit land is 4 Hosseni Dalan Road. He further stated that after withdrawal of Title Suit No. 103 of 2001 defendant dispossessed him. He admitted in cross-examination that dispossession was done before filing of the suit. In order to get a decree for recovery of possession a definite case of possession followed by dispossession has got to be made out in the plaint and accordingly evidence has to be led. Plaintiff did not even amend the plaint to the effect that they had been dispossessed on such date and time by such person or persons in such manner. Plaintiffs have no case on possession followed by dispossession and question of decree on recovery of possession does not arise at all under Article 142 of the Limitation Act and their factum of actual position on possession is beyond pleading. From reading of the deposition of PW 2 and PW 3 it does not appear that plaintiffs or their predecessors had possession in the suit land. PW 2 expressed his ignorance about the possession of DW 6 in the suit land. From the oral evidence of both the parties along with the series of documentary evidence filed by the defendant it transpires that defendant's mother Jahanara had been maintaining title and possession in the suit land till her purchase in 1942 by Exhibit V and after her death defendant Bilkis maintains the same.</u>
<u>17. Defendant has stated in paragraph 23 (Jha) of the written statement that the original documents of foreclosure suit, sale certificate, writ of delivery of possession, deed of relinquishment, title documents, rent-receipts, khatian, receipts of holding taxes were lost during the war of independence. The trial Court found since no sale certificate, writ of delivery of possession were produced, the predecessor of defendant acquired no title. But the trial Court failed to appreciate that sale certificate is not a document of title and auction can be proved by other evidence independent of sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession. This proposition finds support from the case of Thanda Nessa Bibi and others vs Monowar Joarder and others reported in 5 BLC (AD) 189, Bazlur Rahman and others vs Sadu Mia and others reported in 45 DLR 391. In the present case the certified copies of most of the lost documents were produced and marked in evidence. The reason for not filing the previous original documents has been explained away by the defendant. From reading of all those documents it appears that the details of the fact are chronologically and very clearly presented in the recital of those documents in consonance with the statements made in the written statement. Trial court also found that Birendra did not acquire any title by the deed of relinquishment (Exhibit T) executed by Jogendra. Trial Court did not appreciate that this deed of relinquishment although is not a document of title but of admission and declaration about the benami nature and transaction. In the instant case Birendra is the real owner and Jogendra is the ostensible owner. The admission made by the ostensible owner is sufficient to prove that Birendra was the real owner and from reading of Exhibit T, it appears that Jogendra admitted that the auction was purchased by Birendra by his own money and for his own interest. This aspect of the case has been discussed in the case of Mst. Khaleda Razia and others vs Mahatub Uddin Chowdhwy reported in 30 DLR (SC) 27. Recently in a judgment passed on 26-2-2019 in Civil Appeal No. 535 of 2009 in the case of Lalmon Bibi and another vs Mohammad Del war Hossain and others our Appellate Division only relying upon a nadabi document dismissed the appeal. Exhibit-T is proved by calling the volume book from the concerned office. The trial Court failed to appreciate the preponderance of evidence and being driven by whim made adverse observations and findings against the title of the defendant which is absolutely unwanted because in the instant case plaintiffs failed at possession but even then if they could prove title to the suit land in that case title of defendant might be investigated but it is not wise to disbelieve defendant's title when plaintiffs holding a void document without possession summoned defendant to take a chance on her. Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case even if had the defendant failed to prove her title, her and her predecessor's possession for more than 12 (twelve) years would have given birth to her title although she did not specifically claim title by adverse possession and this aspect of the case has been decided in the case of Nurjahan Begum vs Nur Rahman, reported in 6 ADC 469 = 59 DLR 98. Exhibits-C, E series, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, 0 series, P series, Q series are good evidence in support of the case of the defendant and those documentary evidence also terminate the case of the plaintiff.</u>
18. The son of defendant holding a power of attorney Exhibit-A examined himself as DW 1 in support of defence case. DW 2 came from land office and proved SA khatian 2132 Exhibit C prepared in the name of defendant. DW 3 came from the record room with volume book and proved the deed of relinquishment (Exhibit T) dated 20-3-1922. He also proved the kabala dated 29-8-1923 executed by Birendra to Ram Gopal (Exhibit U). DW 3 also proved the kabala dated 22-9-1942 (Exhibit V) executed by Ram Gopal in favour of the mother of the defendant named Jahanara Begum and this document is described in Volume 46 of the year of 1942 at page numbers 27-31. The deposition of DW 3 remained undisturbed in cross. Defendant has successfully proved her title to the suit land. There are series of documents in support of her title and possession in the suit land. DW 4 deposed on possession. DW 5 is the full brother of defendant and he upheld the relevance of Exhibit D series and stated that defendant acquired the suit land. It is stated in paragraph (Kha) of written statement that Lal Miah and his family have been living in the suit land as care taker. Lal Miah as DW 6 deposed in the suit and in cross examination his position got stronger.
19. It is an age-old principle of law that plaintiff has got to prove his own case independent of defence weakness. In the instant case plaintiffs have utterly failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land. Exhibit-6 dated 13-1-2000 is a forged, fraudulent, collusive, void document. They did not even make out any case on possession followed by dispossession. Their prayer is vague and their simultaneous claim on title by purchase and adverse possession is not permitted under the law. Plaintiff with a view to grab the suit land filed this false suit.
<u>20. The title and possession of the defendant in the suit land is evidently proved. The adverse observations and findings arrived at by the trial Court with regard to the title of the defendant being apparently unwanted and misconceived are hereby set-aside and expunged. Accordingly, First Appeal 299 of 2007 is allowed. Since plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove their case First Appeal No. 309 of 2007 is dismissed. The judgment and decree of the trial Court is affirmed in the modified form by expunging the findings of title and possession against the defendant.</u>
21. There will be no order as to costs.
22. Communicate this judgment to the concerned Court.
Send down the lower Court's record.
End.

full_judgment:
Borhanuddin J. This civil appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 06.04.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5187 of 2004 making the Rule absolute.
2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal are that present Respondent Nos.1-11 as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.73 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Betagi, Barguna, impleading the present petitioners and others as defendants for partition of the suit land, contending inter-alia, that 7 acres of land of C.S. Khatian No.559 of Mouja-Talusi Baria, Thana and District Barguna originally belonged to Someruddin and Sher Ali in equal share; The arrear of rent of the aforesaid land was due as such Rent Suit No.229 of 1948 was instituted and the same was decreed; Execution Case No.226 of 1949 was filed and the land was put in auction on 12.07.1949; One Arshed Ali purchased the said land in auction who sold 6.88 acres of land to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder, Tajem Ali and Sekander Ali by a registered sale deed on 27.02.1951 and handed over possession thereto; Rest 12 decimals of land was in possession of Arshed Ali who died leaving one son Mohammad Ali and one daughter Dholai Bibi; Haji Hachaonuddin Talukder sold 86 decimals of land under R.S. Khatian No.54 by a registered sale deed to Samertoban Bibi on 27.03.1954; Mohabbat Ali Kha died leaving 3 sons and one daughter namely Joynal Kha, Plaintiff No.6 Salim Kha, Defendant No.41 Sohrab Kha and Piyara Begum; Said Piyara Begum died leaving husband Defendant No.3 Kanchon Ali Kha and son Defendant No.5 Belal; One Kashem Ali Kha took settlement of 65 decimals land from purchaser Haji Hachonuddin Talukder on 22.12.1952; Kashem Ali Kha sold the land on 05.11.1955 to Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali and Hochen Ali by a registered sale deed and they sold 38 decimals of land to Tajem Ali and Sekander Ali by a registered sale deed; Hatem Ali sold 49 decimals of land under S.A. Khatian No.955 on 29.09.1951 to Mominuddin Kha, Entajuddin Kha and Afezuddin Kha; Entajuddin Kha, Mofez Kha, Rahima Bibi, Ambia and Halima Khatun sold 49 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 to Zulmat Kha on 30.04.1975; Defendant No.41 Sohrab Kha sold 13 decimals of land to Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha who again sold the same to Defendant No.3 Kanchon Ali Kha on 12.05.1979; Haji Hachonuddin Talukder sold 6 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 to the predecessor of the plaintiff Mohabbat Ali Kha, Atahar Ali Kha, Amina Khatun and Samertaban Bibi on 27.03.1954; Haji macnonuaain Talukder died leaving two sons Defendant No.53 Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali and 5 daughters Poribanu, Kodbanu, Iful Bibi, Rupshon Bibi and Rizia Khatun and wife Defendant No.50 Joynab Bibi; Rupshon Bibi died leaving one son Mohammad Ali and one daughter Dholai Bibi; Mohammad Ali and Dholai Bibi jointly inherited 12 decimals of land from their father and 24 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 from mother and jointly sold the same i.e. 36 decimals of land to Plaintiff Nos.2/5/6 on 24.03.1985; Atahar Ali Kha died leaving Plaintiff Nos.8-10 as heirs; Plaintiff Nos.9 and 10 sold 31 decimals of land to the Plaintiff Nos.2 and 12; Samertoban Bibi sold her entire share to Plaintiff Nos.3 and 4; Son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder i.e. Yousuf Ali sold 1.19 acres of land to Defendant No.36 Yousuf Ali Munshi, Nurali and Abdur Razzak on 02.10.1963; Against the said transfer Mohabbat Ali Kha, Amina Khatun, Arabia Khatun and Atahar Ali Kha filed Preemption Case No.136/1964 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and obtained order of preemption on 19.11.1965 from the 1st Munsif Court of Patuakhali; Yousuf Ali died leaving mother Defendant No.50 Joynab Bibi, two wives Defendant Nos.] and 51 Maleka Begum and Kulsum Bibi respectively, one son Defendant No.49 Abdus Sobhan and one daughter Defendant No.52 Farida Begum; Hatem Ali son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder sold 65 decimals of land to Danesh Ali and Moslem Ali Kha on 08.11.1955; Against the said transfer father of Plaintiff No.6 Mohabbat Ali Kha, Atahar Ali Kha, Amina Khatun, Art bia Khatun and Samertoban Bibi filed Pre-emption Case No.164/1959 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and obtained order of pre-emption on 23.01.1960 in which Plaintiff Nos.6-8 jointly got 45 decimals of land; Purchaser Sekander Ali died leaving son Adorn Ali, two daughter Hajera Begun, Anowara Khatun Piyara and wife Ayshon Bibi; Purchaser Tajem Ali died leaving one daughter Minara Begum, wife Maleka Begum, consanguine brother's son Adorn Ali and consanguine sister Sorbanu; Said Adorn Ali, Sorbanu, Ayesha Bibi, Hajera Bibi, Anowara Khatun and Minara Khatun sold 38 decimals of land to Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha on 19.03.1973; Plaintiff No.2 Moslem Ali Kha transferred 10¾ of land to Defendant No.13 Shajahan; Plaintiff No.1 purchased 49½ decimals of land on 19.02.1982 and Plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 jointly purchased 80+22+42-144 decimals of land on 03.02.1985, 01.08.1987 and 02.03.1987 respectively; In this way plaintiffs' became owner and possessor of 4.41¼ of land of S.A. Khatian No.955 and 1.39 acres of land of S.A. Khatian No.954, in total 5.80¼ acres of land; Inspite of repeated requests of the plain-tiffs', the defendants refused to make amicable partition of the suit land which con-strained to file the suit for partition since there is no earlier partition by metes and bounds.
3. Defendant Nos. 3/5/14 and 19 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending interalia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, barred by the law of limitation and also for defect of parties; Their further case is that the suit land originally belonged to Someruddin and Sher Ali in equal share; Sher Ali died leaving two sons Osman Ali and Abdul Ali; Kashem Ali obtained 1.29 acres of land of Plot No.960 from Osman Ali and Abdul Ali on 05.05.1942 through pattan and Osman Ali received rent from Kashem Ali for the years 1349-1352 B.S. admitting Kashem Ali as an under rayat of Osman Ali who executed and registered dakhila on 16.04.1946; Sahed Ali pur-chased Marsha right from Osman Ali and Abdul Ali on 27.02.1946; Sahed Ali gave pattan through unregistered dakhila to Kashem Ali on 11.11.1946 and the said pattan was made during revisional survey and for that reason R.S. and S.A. Khatians were not published in the name of Kashem Ali; Though the land.was not recorded in S.A. Khatian in the name of Kashem Ali but he had been owning and possessing said land through pattan; Sahed Ali and Abdul Ali transferred 1.42 acres of land of Khatian No.955 on 05.11.1955 to Hatem Ali, Yousuf Ali, Hochen Ali and Kashem Ali; By virtue of the said deed Kashem Ali acquired 35½ of land; Kashem Ali being the owner of 1.64½ of land by way of pattan and kabala executed registered will infavour of his two sons and others i.e. Defendant Nos.3/14 Dholu Kha and Asmot Ali; Said Dholu Kha died leaving wife Nurjahan Begum, son Delowar Hossain and 3 daughters namely Rahima, Halima and Reba; Kashem Ali took pattan of 65 decimals of land trom Haji Hachonuddin Talukder on 22.12.1952 from C.S. Khatian No.410 and subsequently transferred the said land to Kobbat. Ali; Sobder, Sadar, Hachon Uddin and Hochon Uddin were owners and possessor of the land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.545 in equal share; Sobder Ali died leaving two sons and 3 daughters namely Arshed Ali, Kodom Ali, Borujan, Mayajan and Dwitiya Bibi where each son got 1.01 acres of land and each daughter got 50½ of land; Sadar Ali died leaving his mother Meherjan and two cousin Arshed Ali and Kodom Ali as heirs and they sold their 4 annas share to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder, Ketab Ali, Ahad Ali and Arena Bibi on 25.04.1941; Arshed Ali died leaving two sons Ketab Ali and Akkel Ali; Akkel Ali died leaving his full brother Ketab Ali as heirs; Ketab Ali (son of Arshed Ali) transferred his land to Ketab Ali (son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder) on 12.03.1940 through pattan and gave dakhila admitting him as under tenant and in the said pattan the share of Borujan and Mayajan was not included; Dwitiya Bibi transferred 50½ decimals of land to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder; Again Borujan Bibi transferred 50½ decimals of land to Haji Hachonuddin Talukder on 21.10.1953; In this way Haji Hachonuddin Talukder obtained 5.54 acres of land amongst which 4.58½ acres of land was his recorded land and he transferred 1.89½ acres of land to Azahar Ali and Paribanu; Said Paribanu sold her portion of land to the defendants on 19.07.1979; Rest land of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder was put in auction and Sirajuddin and others purchased 4.86 acres of land in that auction; Against the said auction Yousuf Ali filed Case No.38/1967 in the 1st Munsif Court of Patuakhali to set-aside the auction. In the said case the auction purchaser amicably released 90 decimals of land infavour of Yousuf Ali; On the death of Yousuf Ali this defendants inherited said 90 decimals of land; Ketab Ali son of Haji Hachonuddin Talukder acquired 1.90 acres of land by way of pattan and kabala and thereafter died leaving wife Borujan, one son Hochen and father Haji Hachonuddin Talukder as heirs; Said Hochen Ali died leaving wife Rejia and two consanguine paternal uncle Hatem Ali and Yousuf Ali; Rejia sold 23 decimals of land on 09.04.1979 to Defendant Nos.3/19 and Plaintiff No.1 jointly; Haji Hachonuddin Talukder being owner of four annas of land of C.S. Khatian No.545 died leaving wife Amina Bibi and one son Ahad Ali; Said Amina Bibi died leaving one son Ahad Ali; Said Ahad Ali being the owner of 5.32 acres of land died leaving two sons Sekander Ali and Tajem Ali; Said Tajem Ali sold 22 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No.954 to Abdul Khobir on 31.03.1964; In this way the defendants acquired 7.01½ of land of S.A. Khatian No.954 by way of inheritance and purchase and have been using and possessing their portion of land peacefully; Plaintiffs' filed this suit with false and baseless claim which is liable to be dismissed.
4. Defendant Nos.21/42-48/70/73/75/77, 36-39 and 87 filed separate written statements and thereafter prayed for saham of 6.69 acres of land, 2.50 acres of land and 22 decimals of land respectively from the suit land.
5. Plaintiffs in support of their case examined 2(two) witnesses and produced documentary evidences which are marked as exhibit-1(series)-15(series). On the other hand contesting Defendant Nos.3/5/14 and 19 examined only one witness and produced documentary evidences which are marked as exhibit Aa-Oi (series). Defendant Nos. 21/42-48/70/73/75 and 77 examined one witness in support of their contention and produced documentary evidences which are marked as exhibit-Ka(1)-Chha(1) (series). Defendant Nos. 36-39 examined one witness and also produced documentary evidences in support of their prayer for saham which are also marked as exhibit-Ka(2)(series)- Ga(2)(series). Again, Defendant No.87 examined one witness in support of his prayer for saham and produced documentary evidence marked as exhibit-Ka(3).
6. After hearing the parties and perusing the record, learned Senior Assistant Judge (In-Charge of Assistant Judge Court) decreed the suit in preliminary form and allowed the saham petitions of the respective saham petitioners by his judgment and decree dated 12.06.2001. Being dis-satisfied, the Defendant Nos.3/5/14/19 as appellants preferred Title Appeal No.99 of 2001 in the Court of learned District Judge, Barguna, which was transferred to the learned Additional District Judge, Barguna.
7. Upon hearing the parties and perusing the record, learned Additional District Judge, Barguna allowed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 15.082004 reversing the findings of the trial court.
8. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiff-respondents as petitioners preferred Civil Revision No.5187 of 2004 before the High Court Division under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Upon hearing the petitioners, a Single Bench of the High Court Division issued a Rule. The defendants as opposite parties contested the Rule.
9. After hearing both the parties, a Single Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court below vide judgment and order dated 06.04.2009.
10. Feeling aggrieved, the Defendant Nos.3/5/14/19 as petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1397 of 2009 and obtained leave granting order dated 09.06.2014 upon the following grounds:
I. Because, the High Court Division did not advert to the decision and findings of the learned appellate Court yet reversed the judgment of the learned appellate Court and thus committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.
II. Because, the appellate Court upon consideration of evidence found that the identity of C.S. and R.S. plots were not established and the suit was bad for hotchpot but the learned appellate Court did not advert to the same yet reversed the judgment and thus committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.
III. Because, the appellate Court found the exhibit-6 and 7 sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession covers the superior interest bearing Khabot 410 but the High Court Division without reversing the same found the subordinate tenancy was sold thus committed error of law occasioning failure of justice.
11. Consequently, present civil appeal arose.
12. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman Helal, learned Advocate for the appellants made his submissions in line with leave granting order.
13. On the other hand, Mr. Helal Uddin Mollah, learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent Nos.2(a)-2(e)/3(a)- 3(c) supports the impugned judgment and order.
14. Mr. Mohammad Ahasan, learned Advocate for the Respondent n support the contention of the appellants.
15. Heard learned Advocate for the respective parties Perused the papers/documents contained in the paper book.
16. We have gone through the judgment and order passed by the Trial Court,
Appellate Court below as well as Revisional Court. The Trial Court framed the following issues for determining the suit-
১। বাদীর মোকদ্দমাটি বর্তমান ভাবে আকারে ও প্রকাণ্ড চলিতে পারে কি?
২। বাদীর মোকদ্দমাটি পক্ষাভাব ও হসপট জনিত দোষে দুষ্ট কি?
৩। বাদীর মোকদ্দমাটি তামাদি বারিত কি?
৪। না: ভূমিতে বাদীর স্বত্ব দখলআছে কি?
৫। বাদী পক্ষ প্রার্থীত মতে অত্র মোকদ্দমায় ডিক্রী পাইতে পারে কি?
৬। ছাহাম প্রার্থী বিবাদীগণ প্রার্থীত মতে অত্র মোকদ্দমায় ছাহাম পাইতে পারে কি?
17. The appellate court below formulated the points for determination as under:
১। বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ১২/০৬/০১ইং তারিখের তর্কিত রায় ও ১৮/০৬/০১ইং তারিখের স্বাক্ষরিত ডিক্রী সঠিক ও আইন সংগত হইয়াছে কি?
২। অত্র দেওয়ানী আপীল মোকদ্দমাটি মঞ্জুর করা যায় কি?
18. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute concurring findings of the Trial court and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court below.
19. Admittedly, the suit land appertaining to C. Khatian No.559 belonged to Someruddin and Sher Ali in equal share. Plaintiffs/respondents claimed that their predecessor got the suit land by auction purchase and subsequently plaintiffs/ respondents got the same through some registered sale deeds. On the other hand, the contested defendants/appellants denied the alleged auction purchase of the plaintiffs and also claimed that the suit is barred b defect of parties and bad for hutch-pot. Again, they claimed that their predecessor got the suit land through settlement and later on they got the same by way of deed of will as well as some registered sale deeds.
20. The question is to be decided here whether the High Court Division is justified to set-aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court below without adverting the findings regarding defect of parties, hutch-pot as well as disputed auction sale.
21. Regarding defect of parties learned appellate court below thoroughly and meticulously discussed the issue appreciation, relevant portion from the Judgment or me appellate court below is reproduced below:
“বাদীপক্ষের উক্ত জেরা পর্যালোচনায় প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, ১৪নং বিবাদীর স্ত্রী মইফুল বা আয়ফুল বা তিন পুত্র মালেক, সুলতান, আলতাফ হোসেন এর এস.এ. ৯৫৪ নং খতিয়ানের শরীক তাহা বাদী/রেসপনডেন্ট মইফুল বিবি, আ: মালেক খা, সুলতান খা, আলতাফ হোসেন খাকে মূল মোকদ্দমায় পড়া না করায় মোকদ্দমাটি পক্ষদোষেও অচল ছিল।”
<u>22. By now it is settled that the suit for partition is incompetent if all the co-sharers are not included as parties to the suit, as no effective decree can be passed in the absence of any one of them. It is true that under Order-I, Rule-9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, no suit shall be defeated by reason of miss-joinder and non-joinder of parties but there can be no doubt that if the parties who are not joined are not only proper but also necessary parties to it the infirmity in the suit is bound to be fatal.</u>
<u>23. On perusal of the evidence on record it appears that P.W.-0 1 admitted in his cross-examination that the wife of Defendant No.14 i.e. Moiful Bibi and 3 sons namely Malek, Sultan and Altaf Hossain are in possession of the suit land. Thus, from such admission it is crystal clear that the fact of possessing a portion of suit land by the Moiful Babi, Malek, Sultan and Altaf Hossain is in the knowledge of the plaintiffs, as such it was the duty of the plaintiffs/ respondents to implead them as parties to avoid multiplicity of proceedings. But on perusal of plaint it appears that the above mentioned four persons are not made parties to the suit, Again, according to the plaint, the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 is subsequently recorded in R.S. Khatian Nos.54,55,607 and S.A. Khatian Nos.418,954,955,951/1, 911 respectively. But on scrutiny of the plaint it appears that the plaintiffs/ respondents did not give any description about the names of individuals in whose names R.S. and S.A. Khatians were recorded. So, in the absence of such description it is not possible to ascertain whether all the R.S. and S.A. tenants are made parties to the suit.</u>
<u>24. This Division in the case of Mobinnessa and Ors. vs. Khalilur Rahman and Ors., reported in (1986) 6 BLD (AD) 109, held:</u>
<u>"In a partition suit, the established principle of law is that all co-sharer shall be impleaded and that failure to implead any-sharer shall render the suit liable or dismissal on the ground of maintainability."</u>
25. Thus, an the question of defect of parties our answer is that the suit is miserably barred by defect of parties.
<u>26. Regarding hutch-pot the fundamental Rule is that a partition suit should embrace all the joint properties of the parties concerned in that suit. Violation of that rule will result in the multiplicity of litigation which all the parties and court must avoid and discourage.</u>
<u>27. On perusal of record it appears that P. -01 admitted in his cross-examination that he doesn't know how much land there is in the former (sabek) plots and how much lands of the former (sabek) plots has been recorded in current (hal) plots. Again, the appellate court below on perusal of exhibit-2 and 2 (lea) arrived at a finding that the former (sabek) plot numbers of the current (hal) Plot Nos.2282 and 2285 are 96 and 909 respectively. The appellate court below also arrived at a finding that in the said exhibited docu-ment no former (sabek) plot number of current Plot No. 2284/2935 is mentioned. On perusal of plaint 2935 and exhibit-01 i.e. C.S. Khatian No.559 it appears that former Plot Nos.96 and 909 are not included in the schedule of the plaint as well as in the C.S. Khatian No.559. In this context appellate court below upon evidences on record arrived at a conclusive finding that the suit is barred by hutch-pot for non-inclusion of the land of former (sabek) Plot Nos.96 and 909 in the schedule of the plaint. Inspite of such finding of the appellate court below, the High Court Division did not utter a single word to controvert such finding of the appellate court below.</u>
<u>28. Our Apex Court in the case of Nurul Afsar vs. Rafiqul Ahmed, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 155, held:</u>
<u>"The general Rule that a partition suit should embrace all the joint properties of the parties concerned is indeed a Rule of convenience. If properties are left out in a partition suit it brooks further litigation. It is true that this Rule is relaxable. But there are specific situations calling for relaxation. They are generally (a) where different portions of the property lie in different jurisdictions, or (b) when some portion of the property is at the time incapable of partition, or (c) when the property from its nature is importable, or (d) When property is held jointly with strangers who cannot be joined as parties to a general suit for partition, or (e) where cotenants, by mutual agreement, decide to make partition of a part of the joint property retaining the rest in common."</u>
29. In the instant case, none of the above situations arose. So, there is no reason to deviate from the proposition of law settled by this Division.
30. Now the remaining point whether the High Court Division is justified in setting-aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court below without adverting the finding of same regarding the disputed auction sale which is a pure question of fact.
31. The appellate court below upon evidences on record arrived at a conclusive finding that the plaintiffs/ respondents is not able to prove their claim regarding auction sale as such the alleged auction sale is not proved. For proper understanding the findings of the appellate court below on this point is reproduced below:
"বাদী/রেসপনডেন্ট পরে দাখিলী প্রদর্শনী-৪ পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, উক্ত মোকদ্দমায় ২৫ টাকা ও ১২ আনা ৫ পাই জমার জমিতে ডিক্রী হইয়াছে এবং খতিয়ান নম্বর নাই। কিন্ত প্রদর্শনী-১, সি.এস. ৫৫৯নং খতিয়ান পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, উক্ত খতিয়ানের খাজনা ৬৪/- টাকা । ইহাতে উক্ত খাজনার মোকদ্মায় এবং ডিক্রী মামলার নিলামে সি.এস. ৫৫৯ নং খতিয়ানের ৬৪/- টাকা খাজনার জমি নিলাম হয় নাই । বরং ২৫/- টাকা ১২ আনা ৬ পাই খাজনায় অন্য খতিয়ানের বা খেবটের জমি নিলাম হইয়াছে। বাদী/ রেসপন্ডেন্ট পক্ষে প্রদর্শনী-১৫ এবং ১৫ (ক) পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, সাবেক ৪১০নং খেটের ওসত নিম হাওলার জমি নিলাম হইয়াছে, যাহার খাজনা ৫১।।/ আনা। কিন্ত সি.এস. ৫৫৯নং খতিয়ান পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, উক্ত খতিয়ানের জমি ক্যা ওসত নিম হাওলা নহে।"
32. It appears from the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division that the High Court Division without assigning any independent findings and without adverting the findings of fact arrived at by the appellate court below make the Rule absolute as a revisional court simply holding that:
The contesting defendants raised a dispute regarding auction sale of the suit property in Rent Suit No.229 of 1948 and Rent Decree Execution Case No.226 of 1949 and stated that the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 was not sold in auction. It has been clearly stated that the land in Sabek Khabot No.410 has been subsequently recorded in C.S. Khatian No.559 and the land of said Khabot No.410 corresponding to C.S. Khatian No.559 was sold in auction."
<u>33. The claim of the plaintiffs/respondents regarding auction sale is purely a question of fact. It is a settled proposition of law that the revisional court cannot interfere with the findings of facts arrived by the appellate court below, if the findings are not perverse or beyond the scope of law.</u>
34. Plaintiffs/respondents claimed that their predecessor purchased the suit land through auction. The plaintiffs filed the suit for partition of C.S. Khatian No.559 and claimed that the land mentioned in C.S. Khatian No,559 and Khabot Khatian No.410 are same and on perusal on exhib-it-06 i.e. sale certificate of land in Rent Suit no. 229 of 1948 it appears that the same do not contain any C.S. Khatian number, rather contain only Khabot Khatian No.410, so it was the duty of the plaintiffs/respondents to establish such claim through relay of the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 with that of Khabot Khatian No.410 by appointing a survey knowing advocate commissioner. But on perusal of record it appears that the plaintiffs/ respondents did not take any such initiatives to establish their claim. Moreover, on perusal of exhibit-06 it appears that Arshed Ali purchased 7 acres of land in that auction. Again, exhibit-06 stated that Arshed Ali purchased the land corresponding to Khabot Khatian No.410 which is under annual rent of 51 taka 9 annas. On perusal of exhibit-1 i.e. C.S. Khatian No it appears that the entire 7 acres of land of that khatian is under annual rent of 64 taka. It is to be mentioned here that if the land of Khabot Khatian No.410 and C.S. Khatian No.559 are same then the annual rent of two khatians should be the same, but in reality the annual rent of both the khatians are not same. Thus, from the above discussions it appears to us that the plaintiff failed to prove that their predecessor purchased the land of C.S. Khatian No.559 through auction, as such the claim of auction purchase of the land of C.S. Khatian No. 559 by the plaintiffs is not proved.
35. From the aforementioned discussions it appears to us that the High Court Division as a revisional court did not utter a single word to controvert the findings of the appellate court below, which is a final court of facts regarding the defect of party, botch-pot as well as alleged auction purchase.
<u>36. This Division in the case of Fakhruddin Mia and Ors. vs. Mohammad Khodabaskh Sheikh, reported in 29 DLR (AD) 268, held:</u>
<u>"The finding of fact whether concur-rent or not, arrived at by the lower appellate court is bindings on the High Court, both as second appellate court and a revisional court, except in certain well-defined exceptional circumstances."</u>
37. Thus, from the above discussions and the principle enunciated in the above cited cases, the conclusive findings of the appellate court below which is a final court of fact regarding defect of parties, hotchpot as well as alleged auction sale are based on evidences on record as such those findings of the same are immune from interference by the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction, but the High Court Division without assigning any independent findings and without adverting those findings of the appellate court below erroneously passed the impugned judgment and order which calls interference by this Division.
38. Under the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions made herein-above, we are inclined to allow the appeal.
39. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
40. The judgment and order dated 06.04.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5187 of 2004 is hereby set-aside and decree dated 15.08.2004 in Title Appeal No.99 of 2001 passed by the Additional District Judge, Barguna, is restored.
41. No order as to costs.
End.
