case_source: (From the judgment- and order dated 13.01.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 71 of 2002 With Civil Revision No. 87 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Krishna Debnath J. That these two civil appeals arise out of leave granted by this court in two civil petitions for Leave to Appeal Nos. 717 and 718 of 2009 are directed against the judgment and order dated the 13th day of January, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.71 of 2002 with Civil Revision No.87 of 2002 discharging both the Rules thereby affirming those dated 21.10.2001 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.36 of 1999 heard analogously with Title Appeal No.35 of 1999 allowing both the appeals decreeing Title Suit No 67 of 1995 setting aside those dated 30.11.1998 passed by the Assistant Judge, Beani Bazar, Sylhet decreeing Title Suit No.67 of 1995 and dismissing Title Suit No.64 of 1995.
2. The facts involved in the case no 67 of 1995, in short are that the suit land originally belonged to Gajendra Kumar Chattarjee; that Gajendra Kumar while in possession intended to sell the same and entered into an agreement with the present proforma respondent no 2, Liakot Ali and Panaullah on 13.09.1963 at an consideration money of Tk.1000.00; that Gajendra received tk.800 from the purchasers and inducted them into possession; that on 09.03.1965 after getting the balance amount of tk. 200 the aforesaid Gajendra executed the sale deed in favour of Panaullah and Liakot Ali ; that therefore a dispute arose between the Panaullah and Liakot regarding the purchased land and Panaullah instituted Title suit no 312 of 1967 against the said Liakot and ultimately the suit was decreed on 23.01.1968 on the basis of a solenama, the present pro-forma respondent no 2 Liakot got the 2nd scheduled land in his share and had been owning and possessing the same; that original owner Gajendra filed Title suit No 386 of 1967 for permanent injunction against Panaullah and Liakot which was ultimately withdrawn by the plaintiff, Gajendra and in that suit Gajendra admitted his earlier sale in favour of Panaullah and Liakot; that the proforma respondent No 2 Liakot had been possessing the 2nd scheduled land of the plaint by constructing house at S.A. Plot No 171 and cultivating paddy on S.A. plot no 125 and had been paying rent regularly and also mutated his name in the record of right in Mutation Case No. 43 of 1968-69; that thereafter the aforesaid Liakot went to Dinajpur for some purposes and had been possessing the suit land through his maternal uncle one Nasiruddin, a retired police officer; that thereafter, Liakot became a member of the local Union Parishad at Dinajpur and had been living there permanently; that at the instance of certain local interested persons the local Vested Property Authority claiming the suit land and some other lands as Vested and Non-resident Property started VP Case no 22 of 1978-79 and served notice upon Liakot and present respondent no 1 Mostafa Ahmed directing them to hand over possession of the same; that on behalf of Liakot, his uncle Nasiruddin filed written objection and Mostafa Ahmed also filed a separate written objection and after hearing VP Case No 22 of 1978-79 was dropped; that in that case Mostafa Ahmed the respondent No 1 filed papers before the Court with Firisti along with aforesaid Nasiruddin the representative of Liakot Ali; that the present proforma respondent no 2 Liakot Ali sold the 2nd scheduled land of the plaint to proforma respondent Nos. 3-7 and one lqbal Hussain and others who purchased 1.33 acres of land out of 1.41 acres through different registered sale deeds dated 12.06.1989 and 18.06.1989 respectively at Tk 4,40,000.00.Thereafter defendant Nos. 2-6 along with lqbal Hussain and others constructed dwelling house and by digging pond and filling earth possessed the same. Thereafter, the said lqbal Hussain and others transferred their shares to Mostafa Shahriar through different sale deeds dated 05.10.1989 and 08.11.1989 respectively and delivered possession to him and since then the petitioner and others have been possessing the 2nd scheduled land. In the month of June, 1989 one Nizamuddin, a relative of Liakot Ali came to know that the respondent no 1, Mostafa Ahmed mutated 2nd scheduled land in his name and accordingly, on enquiry, he further came to know that he has created a forged deed dated 20.04.1983 by way of false personation. On 17.06.1989 the said Nizamuddin filed a complaint before the District Anti-Corruption Department, Sylhet against Mostafa Ahmed. Thereafter, on 08.08.1989 after obtaining the certified copy of the deed dated 20.04.1983 Liakot Ali came to know about the existence of that bainapatra dated 18.10.1973 which was also forged deed and never been executed by Liakot Ali and as such, the plain-tiff filed the suit for declaration that the bainapatra dated 18.10.1973 and the deed of sale dated 20.04.1983 are forged and collusive papers, hence the plaintiffs instituted the suit.
3. The defendant No. 1 contested the case by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Gajendra Kumar who executed a bainapatra on 13.09.1963 in favour of one Liakot Ali, son of Rafique Uddin of Khidirpur and Panaullah and he received tk. 800 out of total consideration of tk. 1000 and inducted them into possession; that thereafter, getting the remaining amount of tk. 200 the aforesaid Gajendra executed a sale deed on 09.03.1965 in favour of both Liakot and Panaullah: that Panaullah filed Title suit No. 312 of 1967 for partition in the Court of subordinate judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet and on the basis of solenama the suit was decreed; that as per terms of solenama Panaullah got 42 decimals towards the western side of plot no 171 and 54 decimals towards the southernside of plot no 125 that thereafter, Panaullah and Liakot mutated their names in the record of right vide Mutation Case No. 42 of 1968-69; that Panaullah transferred his share in favour of one Rabeya Khatun, wife of Shoikot Ali by registered deed dated 13.04.1968; that Rabeya Khatun by two registered deed dated 05.12.1972 and 15.12.1972 respectively transferred the same in favour of present defendant no 1 Mostafa Ahmed and inducted him into possession; that after the purchase from Rabeya the owner of other portion namely Liakot Ali intended to transfer his land and the defendant No.1 in order to purchase the same entered into an agreement for sale with Liakot Ali on 18.10.1973 and consideration money was fixed at Tk. 12000.00 and tk. 6000 was paid on that date and defendant no. 1 was inducted into possession of the land; that in spite of repeated requests Liakot Ali delayed the execution of the kabala on different pleas and ultimately on 20.04.1983 after getting the remaining tk. 6000 executed and registered the sale deed in favour of the defendant No. 1 and he has been possessing the suit land as before; that the defendant No. 1 on 31.08.1971 received a notice from the vested property authority directing him to hand over the possession of the land in favour of the government claiming the same as vested and non-resident property; that the defendant No. 1 instituted title suit no 226 of 1982 in the court of subordinate judge 2nd court. Sylhet for a declaration that the land is not a vested and nonresident property and also for a declaration that the plaintiff is the owner in possession of the same on the basis of purchase; that he also filed title suit no 202 of 1984 in the same court for permanent injunction restraining the government from interfering with the plaintiffs' possession and the same was decreed on 25.02.1985; that the government did not prefer any appeal against that decree; that title suit no 226 of 1982 was also decreed on 28.11.1987 declaring the plaintiffs' title and possession over the land mentioned in the plaint; that from the date of bainapatra dated 18.10 1973 the defendant no.1 has been possessing the suit land by constructing house and paying rent regularly; that the defendant no 1 mortgaged entire land of plot no 171 with the local Sonali Bank in the year 1986 and transferred entire land of plot no.125 to Musammat Kamrunnessa Khatun, Badrun Lashker, Luthfur Rahman Chowdhury, Abdus Samad and Abdus Sajjad who mutated their names in the record of right and have been possessing their and by constructing building thereon; that Liakot Ali after his sale left the locality and at present, there is no Liakot Ali at the locality which is evident from the local voter list: that the plaintiffs in order to grab the suit land created some forged deeds presenting a false person as Liakot Ali before the Sub-Registrar: that the plaintiffs have no title and possession over the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. That in title suit no 64 of 1995 the present respondent no 1 Mostafa Ahmed as the plaintiff stated everything in support of his claim which he stated by filing written statement in Title suit no 67 of 1995. He also stated that the present appellant Mostafa Shahriar in collusion with his alleged nephew defendant No. 1 Shahed Ahmed Chowdhury created a forged deed dated 10.11.1991 alleged to have been executed and registered by plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed in favour of defendant No. 1 Shahed Ahmed and his son has been shown as an attesting witness though he never executed and registered any deed in favour of Shahed Ahmed Chowdhury that he and his son were not present at Sylhet on that date; that the defendant in order to grab the land of the plaintiff created the aforesaid false deed; that on 10.07.1994 when the plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed was in Dhaka, the defendants Shahriar and Shahed with the help of their party men forcibly entered into the house of the plaintiff Mostafa Ahmed and dispossessed him from the house and also from the land; that on return to Sylhet when he asked the defendants about the reason they disclosed that on the basis of purchase they took possession of the same: that after enquiry on 08.08.1994 and after obtaining the certified copy he came to know that defendant No. 1 in collusion with defendant No. 2 created a forged deed dated 10.11.1991 in respect of 60 decimals of land of plot no 171; that on the basis of so-called deed dated 10.11.1991 the defendants have not acquired any title or possession and for declaration of the aforesaid deed as forged and recovery of khas possession after evicting defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from the suit land of the suit he instituted T.S. No 64 of 1995.
5. That the present appellant Mostafa Shahriar as defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing written statement and stated everything which he stated in his plaint of T.S. No. 67 of 1995. He also stated that since their purchase from the Liakot Ali in the year 1989 he and his other sharers have been possessing the land by con-structing house, they also dug a pond and connected their land with electric and gas line, that the so called dispossession of the plaintiff on 10.07.1994 from the suit land is absolutely a false story; that the plaintiff of T.S. No. 64 of 1995 had no title or possession over the suit land: that defendant No 2 is not his nephew and he has no connection with him and he had no knowledge about the so called deed dated 10.11.1991 and as such T.S. No. 64 of 1995 against him is liable to be dismissed with cost.
6. The trial court after analogous trial decreed the Title Suit No. 67 of 1995 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 64 of 1995 on 30.11.1998.
7. That being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree respondent No. 1 filed title appeal Nos. 35 of 1999 and 36 of 1999 and the court of appeal below allowed the appeals by his judgment and decree dated 21.10.2001.
8. That being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree this appellant filed Civil Revision Nos.71 of 2002 and 87 of 2002 which were heard analogously by a single judge of the High Court Division who by his judgment and order dated 13.01.2009 discharged the rule.
9. That being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order in Civil Revision No. 71 of 2002 with Civil Revision No.87 of 2002 this appellant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 717 of 2009 and 718 of 2009 before this Court and after hearing the parties this Court considered submissions of the learned advocates and leave was granted to consider the additional grounds.
10. Mr. Fida M. Kamal learned Senior Advocate with Mr. Zuhurul Islam Mukul, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants in both the appeals submit that Liakot Ali himself as plaintiff No. 1 and along with purchasers from him having instituted the suit and deposed twice as P.W-2 to prove in support of his case and his identity having not being challenged and defendants in his suit having not been able to prove that he is not the real Liakot. Mr. Kamal further submits that in support of his claim Mostafa Ahmed (respondent) having stated that his vendor Liakot Ali left for Chittagong Hill Tracts and he is already dead and Liakot Ali present in Court is not the real person and the trial court having disbelieved his claim and having held that he has not been able to prove the said facts. Lastly, he submits that the Vested Property Authority issued a notice on 31.08.1978 in VP Case No. 22 of 1978-79 claiming the entire land as vested property (possessed by Liakot and Panaullah) and after their representation and production of the necessary papers on 27,09.1987 the said notice having been withdrawn. the Title Suit No. 226 of 1982 filed on 12.07.1982 by respondent Mostafa Ahmed challenging the notice dated 31.08.1978 without impleading Liakot Ali as a party is malafide to show himself as the sole owner of the entire property and the court of appeal below committed an error in not considering the aforesaid facts, in decreeing the instant suit and the High Court Division also committed error in affirming the same.
11. On the other hand Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate with Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents of both the appeals submit that the appellant Mostafa Shahriar in no way acquire his title through the disputed deeds upon 1.33 acres of land from Liakot Ali, the identity of the produced Liakot Ali is being disputed. Mr. Ali submits on the contrary Panaullah, one of the admitted owners of the suit land has been examined in the Court and proved the transfer in favour of respondent No. 1 Mostafa Ahmed. Lastly, he supports the judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as the judgment and order of the Court of Appeal and prays for dismissal of the appeals.
12. We have heard the learned Advocates of both sides and have considered their sub-missions, perused the records and others.
<u>13. Firstly, it appears that Liakot Ali as plaintiff No. 1 along with purchasers instituted the suit and deposed twice as P.W-2 to prove his case. His identity was not challenged by the defendants at that time. Secondly, Respondent Mostafa as defendant stated that, his vendor Liakot Ali left for Chittagong Hill Tracts and he has already died and Liakot Ali present in the Court is not the real person, trial court dis-believed his claim with cogent reasons. but, the Court of Appeal below without reversing the said findings with its own finding referring the materials on record mechanically and whimsically allowed the appeal and thereby committed serious error as revisional Court in allowing the appeals and the High Court Division com-mitted an error in failing to thresh out the said mistake of affirming the judgment of the Court of appeal below. Thirdly, it appears that the Vested Property Authority issued notice on 31.08.1978 in VP Case No. 22 of 1978-79 claiming the entire land as vested property, but, after production of the necessary papers by the appellants that notice withdrawn. However, the Court of Appeal did not consider these aspects of the case rather, the High Court Division also committed error in failing to find out the said error of the Court of appeal below and thereby committed error in affirming the decision of the Court of appeals Lastly, it appears that the plaintiff appellant filed his suit for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession, but the Court of appeal below decreed the suit in favour of respondent without arriving at any finding regarding his possession followed by dispossession of the suit land and the High Court Division erred in affirming such an erroneous judgment and decree.</u>
14. Regard being had, we are, therefore, of the view that, the High Court Division upon an erroneous view discharged the Rules and affirmed the judgment and order passed by the Court of appeal below which, according to law is liable to be interfered by this Division.

15. In the result, both the appeals are allowed. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and the Court of appeal below are hereby set aside.
16. The Trial Court's judgment is restored.
End.

full_judgment:
Borhanuddin J. This civil appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and decree dated 02.05.2010 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 459 of 2000 allowing the same. 

2. Facts relevant are that the predecessor-in-interest of present respondent nos. 1(a)- 1(h) and respondent nos. 2 and 3 as plain-tiffs instituted Partition Suit No.57 of 1994 in thy Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2na Court Bogra, impleading the petitioners herein alongwith the predecessor of present respondent nos.4(a)-4(f) and respondent nos.5-85 as defendants claiming saham of 1.48 1/6 acres of land out of the suit land measuring 13.35 acres, contending interalia, that the suit jote comprising 13.35 acres of land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.10 of Mouza Khamarkandi under Police Station-Bogra, District-Bogra, originally belonged to Azim Uddin Mollah, Abdul Mollah and Sabu Mollah in equal share; During ejmali possession said Azim Uddin Mollah and Abdul Mollah transferred their shares to the extent of two third measuring 11 bighas and 17 kathas infavour of Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah both sons of C.S. recorded tenant Azim Uddin Mollah by registered deed dated 09.06.1917 on condition that they would pay vendor's debt . of Tk.450/- to the ex-landlord; Since the sale was a conditional one, the vendors retained possession of the land; The said sale deed was never acted upon for non-payment of the debt to the ex-landlord in compliance with the condition stipulated in the deed; Azim Uddin Mollah died leaving three sons namely Asmat, Jasmat and Najem alongwith two daughters solebi and Sawabi; Sabu Mollah died leaving three sons namely Korban, Muslim and Moyez; Jasmat died leaving full brother Asmat; Said Abdul Mollah died leaving wife Amiron and three sons namely Kashem, defendant no.1 Chand, defendant no.2 Farid and 3 daughters namely Shukimon, defendant no.3 Rupban and Janina; Amiron died leaving two sons Ayetullah and defendant no.2 Farid and daughter defendant no.3 Rupban; Asmat Ullah died leaving two sons namely olam and Nasir and two daughters Toiron and Gendi; Najem died leaving a son plaintiff no.1 Jashim and daughter Lalbibi; Sawabi died leaving a son defendant no,6 Kuranu; Nasir died leaving a son plaintiff no.2 Khairuzzaman Mollah and daughter plaintiff no.3 Shahera; Golan died leaving wife defendant no,7 Kochimon and two daughters namely Jahanara, Jobeda and two sisters Gendi and Toiron; Salebi died leaving two sons Md. Nabir Uddin and Kalim Uddin, defendant nos.10 and 11 respectively; Korban died leaving three sons namely Buhl, Riaz and Kawser; Said Riaz died leaving four sons namely Md. Biraz Uddin, Md. Azizer Rahman, Md. Hafizar Rahman and Md. Abdur Rahman, defen-dant nos.13-16 respectively; Kawser died leaving only daughter defendant no.17 Mosammat Asma and brother Bulu; Moyez died leaving wife Fuljan, a son defendant no. 18 Md. Mojam Uddin and two daughters Most. Kallaton Nesa and Most. Potol Bibi; Fuljan died leaving husband defendant no.10 Md. Nabir Uddin, a son Mojam Uddin and three daughters Kallaton, Potol and Golapi, defendant nos.19-21 respectively; Moslem died leaving a son Samsul and three daughters Borki Bibi, Bull and Momijan, defendant nos. 22-25 respectively; Kashem died leaving a son Futu Mollah, defendant no.26 and three daughters Sonaban Bibi, Fatema Bibi and Rahima Bibi, defendant nos.27-29 respectively; Shukimon died leaving four sons namely Kazem, Sukra, Azo and Kachua alongwith one daughter Atopjan; Said Kazem died leaving defen-dant no.30 Kodban and Atopjan died leaving a daughter defendant no.31 Sharifon and three brothers Sukra, Azo and Kachua; Said Sukra died leaving wife defendant no.32 Hamidon and three sons namely Md. All Fakir, Md. Hachen Fakir and Md. Hamid Fakir alongwith daughter Shurjoban, defendant nos.33-36 respectively; Azo died leaving a son Yousuf Ali and two daughters Momena and Ayjon, defendant nos.37-39 respectively; Jarina died leaving two sons Rabia and Bacha; Said Bacha died leaving wife defendant no. 40 Achiron and brother Rabia; Said Rabia died leaving wife defendant no.41 Maim n, and five sons namely Abul Hossain, Gaffer, Hobibar, Sekander and Nur Hossain and three daughters Asarban, Nurbanu and Asma Khatun, defendant nos.42-49. respectively. Toiron died leaving five sons namely Asgar, Ahab, Dhalu, Bulu and Tutu and two daughters' Jarina and .lamina, defendant nos.50-56 respectively; Gendi died leaving a son defendant no.57 Dilbor and a daughter defendant no.58 Sahera; Kachu died leaving wife Kanchi and two sons Sobhan, Montu alongwith daughter Mariam, defendant nos.59-62 respectively; Defendant nos.1-62 are the co-sharers by inheritance to the suit jote and defendant nos.63-66 are the co-sharers by purchase to the suit jote; The plaintiffs are in ejmali possession; The plaintiffs demanded partition of the suit land from defendant no.26 on 15.06.1992 but he denied; Hence, the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos.1-1(Uma), 2, 4, 12., 26, 15, 16, 18, 23, 27 and 29 filed separate written statements supporting case of the plaintiffs. 

4. The defendant nos.67 and 68 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. 

5. The case of the defendant nos. 67 and 68 are that the suit jote appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.10 originally belonged to Abdul Azim Mollah, Abdul Mollah and Sabu Mollah; During ejmali possession Azim Mollah and Abdul Mollah transferred their share to the extent of 11 bighas and 17 kathas in the year 1917 to Asmat and Jasmat but the C.S. record was not prepared accordingly; Azim Mollah, Abdul Mollah, Sabu. Mollah, Asmat and Jasmat transferred 22 bighas and 6.75 kathas of land to Shushila Shundari Gbosh, predecessor of the defendants, vide registered deed no.11.2 dated 05.01.1923 prior to the C.S. operation but C.S. record was prepared and published wrongly in the name of Azim Mollah, Abdul Mollah and Sabo Mollah; Though C.S. record was published wrongly but Shushila Sundari Ghosh possessed the purchased land through borgadars; Abdul Pramanik transferred 1.17 acres of land to Rajani Kanta Ghosh, husband of Shushila Sundari vide registered kabala dated 18.12.1928; Both Shushila Sundari and Rajanii. Kanta Ghush gave barga of the suit land infavour of Abdul Pramanik for 7 years by barga deed dated 02.04.1929; Shushila settled .55 acre of land to different persons and the rest to the extent of 10.59 acres was recoraed in the M.R.R. Khatain in her name Rajani Kanta died prior to publication of M.R.R. Khatian; Shushila Sundari died leaving two daughters Radharani and Raj lakshmi, defendant nos.67 and 68 respectively; During the war of liberation Shushila Sundari and her successors engaged Chand Miah son of Abdul Ariz as bargadar in respect of their share and left for India; On their return after liberation when they demanded usufructs from Chand Miah, he denied to give the same and then they filed Title Suit No. 2 of 1974 against Chand Miah which was decreed on compromise in their favour; Rajlakshmi transferred .24 acre of land by registered deed dated 25.06.1989 infavour of defendant no.22 son of defendant no.2; Rajlakshmi also transferred some lands to different persons; After transfer, the defendants retained possession to the extent of 7.43 acres of land; The defendants filed Case No.3713192 under Section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against defendant no.26 and others which was disposed of in their favour on compromise; Plaintiffs are not entitled to get any saham/relief in the suit and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

6. During trial, the plaintiff examined three witnesses and the contesting defendants examined four witnesses and both the parties produced relevant documents which were marked as exhibits. 

7. After hearing the parties and perusing the evidence on record, the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 28.02.2000.

8. Being aggrieved, the plaintiffs i.e. respondent nos.l-3 herein as appellants filed First Appeal No.459 of 2000 before the High Court Division. Upon hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record, a Division Bench of the High Court Division allowed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 02.05,2010 and decreed the suit giving saham to the plaintiffs as prayed for. 

9. Having aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division, the defendant-respondents as petitioner nos.1- 3 preferred civil petition for leave to appeal invoking Article 103 of the Constitution and obtained leave on 14.06.2012.
 
10. Consequently, instant civil appeal arose. 

11. Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division committed an error by not considering that Azim, Abdul, Sabu alongwith Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah executed registered deed dated 05.01.1923 infavour of Shushila Sundari Ghosh, mother of the defendant-appellants, which shows that Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah, purchaser of the land vide registered deed dated 09.06.1917, had been the owner and possessor of the land purchased and which also proves that the registered deed dated 09.06.1917 was duly executed. He also submits that the plaintiffs failed to prove their claim that the debt due to ex-landlord to the extent of Tk.450/- was not paid; He again submits that the document being ancient one clearly establish right, title, interest and possession of the defendant-appellants and their predecessor. He further submits that the defendant-appellants by adducing evidence proved that the respondent-plaintiff's predecessors cultivated the land as bargadar of Shushila Sundari and that the M.R.R. Khatian was prepared duly in the name of defendants' predecessor i.e. Shushila as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the defendant-appellants relayed the land through Advocate Commissioner which is apparent from Advocate Commissioner's report as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. He lastly submits that the High Court Division wrongly shifted the onus of proof of payment of debt to the ex-landlord by the vendees of kabala dated 09.06.1917 on the defendant-appellants though in view of the kabala dated 05.01.1923 the onus was squarely falls upon the respondent-plaintiffs to prove the non-payment of the dues of ex-landlord by the vendees and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. 

12. On the other hand Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent nos.1(a)- 1(h), 2-3 submits that the deed dated 09.06.1917 executed by Md. Azim Mollah and Md. Abdul Mollah infavour of Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah was a conditional sale and the condition not being complied with, it was not acted upon and accordingly C.S. Khalian was prepared in the name of original owners but the trial court erroneously shifted the onus upon the plaintiffs as such the impugned judgment and decree shall sustain. He also submits that C.S. Khatian has presumption of its correctness which is suit rebatable by proper evidence but no evidence was adduced by the contesting defendants to discharge their onus which lawfully lies on them and the trial court failed to appreciate the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs and thus erroneously holding title and possession of the defendants. He again submits that Khatian has no presumptive value as such the impugned judgment and decree shall sustain and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He lastly submits that the plaintiffs categorically stated in the plaint that: 
“নালিশী উক্ত সম্পত্তিতে উক্ত সুশীলা সুন্দরীর কোন প্রকার স্বত্ব দখল অধিকার ইত্যাদি কিছুই নাই এবং কোন দিনই ছিলনা । ৬৭/৬৮নং পক্ষভুক্ত বিবাদীর মৌরস সুশীলা সুন্দরী দাসী এবং তৃদীয় স্বামী রজনী কান্ত ঘোষ জীবদ্দশায় সুদের ব্যবসা করিত। বিভিন্ন ব্যক্তি বরাবরে টাকা পয়সা ধার দিত এবং তাহা -------------------------- বগুড়া সদর থানাধীন পার বগুড়া সাকিনে রামলাল দাস নামীয় তাহাদের একজন নিকট আত্মীয় ছিল। সে বগুড়া সদর সাব-রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে দলিল লেখক মোহরার হিসাবে কাজকর্ম করিত। তাহার সহযোগিতায় উক্ত ৬৭/৬৮নং বিবাদীর মৌরসদ্বয় উক্ত সাদা স্ট্যাম্পে সহিযুক্ত কাগজদ্বারা জালিয়াতিমূলে বহু মূল্যবান দলিলপত্রাদি সৃষ্টি করিয়া বহু নিরীহ মানুষকে ভিটেমাটি ছাড়া করিয়াছে এবং পথে বসাইয়াছে মর্মে প্রকাশ পাইতেছে। ৬৭/৬৮নং সরল নিরীহ অজ্ঞ অশিক্ষিত মৌরসগণকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে উৎখাত করার অপচেষ্টায় ও উদ্দেশ্যে উক্তরূপ কোন কাগজাত সৃষ্টি করিয়া থাকিতে পারে এবং তন্মুলে বিগত revisional settlement জরিপকালে জরিপ কর্মচারীগণকে বাধ্য করিয়া তাহাদের নামে ১৫নং ভুয়া এম.আর.আর. খতিয়ান প্রস্তুত করাইয়া তাহা গোপেনে রাখিয়াছে।”

13. But the trial court without taking into consideration of the averments of the plaint and evidence thereof dismissed the suit erroneously and as such the impugned judgment and decree shall sustain. 

14. Heard the learned Advocate for the respective parties and gone through the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court as well as by the High Court Division and evidences annexed in the paper book and additional paper book. 

15. it appears that the trial court dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their claim that the condition attached to the kabala dated 09.06.1917 was not complied with by the vendees of the kabala; The kabala dated 05.01.1923 (exhibit-'l ha') shows that Abdul, Azim, Sabu, Asmat and Jasmat together sold 22 bighas and 6.75 kathas of land to Shushila Sundari and thus the CS. recorded tenants Abdul, Azim and Sabu admitted the title of Asmat and Jasmat and therefore the plaintiffs cannot deny the title of the defendants who are the heirs of Shushila Sundari; The kabala dated 09.07.1923 (exhibit- ‘ga,') proves that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs cultivated the suit land as bargadar of Shushila Sundari and thus they admitted the title of the defendant's predecessor-in-interest. Relevant portion of the judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is quoted herein as under: 
“বিবাদীপক্ষের দাখিলী ০৯/০৭/১৯২৩ তারিখের
কবলা দলিল প্রদঃ “গ” ও ০২/০৪/১৯২৯ তারিখের
কবুলিয়ত প্রদঃ “ঙ' হইতে দেখা যায় যে, সুশিলার
স্বতু স্বীকার করিয়া বাদীদের মৌরশগণ নাঃ জোতের
জমি af করিয়াছেন। তাহা ছাড়া বিবাদীপক্ষের
দাখিলী ১৮/০৬/১৯৮০ তারিখের কবলা প্রদঃ 'প' ও
১৮/০৬/১৯৮০ তারিখের অপর কবলা পদঃ “ফ' হইতে দেখা যায় যে, সুশিলার ওয়ারিশদের নিকট হইতে ৬৯নং বিবাদী সম্পত্তি খরিদ করিয়াছেন। তাহা ছাড়া নাঃ সম্পত্তির এম.আর.আর. খতিয়ান ৬৭/৬৮নং বিবাদীদের পূর্ববর্তীদের নাম প্রস্তুত হয়। বিবাদীপক্ষের ডি-ডবি-উ-২ মোঃ মজিবর রহমান, ডি-ডবি-উ-৩ ওছমান আলী ফকির, ডিডবি-উ-৪ ইউসুফ আলী সকলেই জবানবন্দিতে বিবাদীদের স্বত্ব দখল সমর্থন করিয়াছেন। এমতাবস্থায়, ইং-০১/০৬/১৯১৭ ও ০৫/০১/১৯২৩ তারিখের কিংবা বিবাদীপক্ষের দাবীকৃত অন্যান্য কবলা দলিলেল কোন কার্যকারিতা হয় নাই মর্মে দাবী মোটেও প্রমানিত হয় নাই। উপরোক্ত ০৯/০৬/১৯১৭ ও ০৫/০১/১৯২৩, ১৮/১২/১৯২৮ তারিখের কবলামূলে বাদীদের মৌরশগণ সি.এস. ১০নং খতিয়ানের সমুদয় সম্পত্তি হস্তান্তর করায় সি.এস. প্রজাদের ওয়ারিশ হিসাবে বাদীপক্ষের নাঃ জোত সম্পত্তিতে কোন স্বত্ব দখল বিদ্যমান নাই।
বিবাদীপক্ষ আদলতযোগে এ্যাডভোকেট কমিশনার দ্বারা ইং-০৫/০১/১৯২৩ তারিখের কবলাতুক্ত সম্পত্তি নাঃ তপসিল ভুক্ত সম্পত্তির সহিত সাদৃশ্য রহিয়াছে মর্মে রিপোর্ট প্রাপ্ত হন। উক্ত কমিশন রিপোর্ট যথাযথ হওয়ায় তাহা গ্রহণ করা হইয়াছে। বাদীপক্ষ উপরে উলি-খিত দলিলসমূহের বিরুদ্ধে মোকদ্দমা করেন নাই। উপরোক্ত আলোচনার প্রেক্ষিতে এই সিদ্ধান্তে আসি যে, বিবাদী পক্ষের দাবীকৃত ০১/০৬/১৯১৭, ০৫/০১/১৯২৩ ও অন্যন্য তারিখের দলিল এর প্রেক্ষিতে পরবর্তীতে এম.আর.আর. খতিয়ান প্রস্তুত হওয়ায় এ সকল দলিলসমূহ বাস্তবে কার্যকর হইয়াছে বিধায় বাদী পক্ষের দাবী প্রমানিত হয় নাই। আর তাই বাদী পক্ষ প্রার্থনা মতে কোন প্রতিকার পাইতে হকদার নয়। অত্র বিচার্য বিষয়সমূহ বাদী প্রতিকূলে বিবেচিত হইল। অতএব আদেশ হয় যে, অত্র মোকদ্দমাটি ৬৭/৬৮নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে দো-তরফা সূত্রে ও অন্যান্যদের (অন্যান্য বিবাদীদের) বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা সূত্রে বিনা খরচায় ডিসমিস হয় ।”

16. But the High Court Division allowed the first appeal and decreed the suit in preliminary form and thereby allotted shaham of 1.48 acres of land infavour of the plain-tiffs holding that: 
"Considering the evidence adduced by the defendant-respondents it does not appear that the consideration money for the deed dated 09.06.1917 i.e. exhibit 'Ica' was paid to the ex-landlord. It appears that trial court courageously fixed the onus of such proof on the plaintiff-appellants. The rebuttal onus always lies with the other side who wants to repudiates the presumption as the C.S. record of rights hold.   
Obviously under the aforesaid provision of law here in the present case the proof of payment of consideration money lies on the defendant-respondents who claim to pay the consideration money of the deed dated 09.06.1917.  It is to be noted that the defendant-respondents could not produce either oral or documentary evidence in sup-port of payment of the consideration money of the deed dated 09.07.1917- 
The observation of the lower court that the defendant-respondents could establish their title & possession to the suit jute thus stands on mere conjecture & surmise having no proof of evidence." (Sic) 

17. Admittedly, the original owners i.e. Aim Uddin Mollah and Abdul Mollah transferred 11 bighas and 17 kathas of land infavour of Asmat Ullah and Jasrnat ullah by registered deed dated 09.06.1917 (exhibit-la') with a condition that the vendees would pay Tk.450/- to the ex-landlord, a debt of the vendors. There is a dispute between the parties regarding the payment and non-payment of the said debt of Tk.450/-. 

18. Section 101 of the Evidence Act lays down that whoever desire any court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependant on the existence of fact which he asserts, must prove that those facts exist and Section 103 of the Act pro-vides that the burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided in any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on the particular person. 

19. In the plaint, the plaintiffs asserted that: 
“উক্তরূপভাবে কথিত বিক্রীত সম্পত্তিতে উক্ত দাতাঘ্বয় স্বতৃবান ও দখলিকার নিযুক্ত থাকা অবস্থায় পরবর্তীকালে উক্ত জমিদানের খণ নিজেরাই পরিশোধ করিয়া দায়মুক্ত হয় বটে । উক্তরূপ অবস্থায় কথিত আজিম ও আব্দুল দত্তা কথিত আছমত ও জসমত বরাবরে কথিত উক্ত বিগত ইং ০৮/০৬/১৯১৭ তারিখে সম্পাদিত ও ০৯/০৬/১৯১৭ তারিখে ৩৩৯৪ নম্বর রেজিষ্ট্রকৃত কবলা দলিলখানা তথ্যকীমূলক সৃষ্ট দলিল হইতেছে।”

20. As per the provisions of Evidence Act, the burden of proof regarding the subsequent payment of debts of the ex-landlord by the predecessor of the plaintiffs is lies upon the plaintiffs. Though PW-1 Md. Khayrat Jahan Mollah deposed in his examination-in-chief in support of his said claim but failed to adduce any corroborative evidence. The PW-2 and 3 also did not give any evidence in their respective testimony in this regard. So, such claim of plaintiffs is not proved by corroborative evidence. 

21. Again, defendants claimed that the original owners i.e. Azim Uddin Mollah, Abdul Mollah and Sena Mollah alongwith the purchaser of registered deed dated 09.06.1917 i.e. Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah jointly transferred 22 highs and 6.75 kathas of land infavour of Shushila Shundari Ghosh, predecessor of the defendant nos.67 and 68, vide registered deed dated 05.01.1923. They produced the original copy of deed no.112 dated 05.01.1923 which was marked as exhibit- 'Um'. On perusal of exhibit-‘kha' it appears that said registered deed is an original copy of more than 30 years old document which is sub-mitted in the court by the proper custodian of that deed. 

22. As per provisions of Section 90 of the Evidence Act there is a presumption infavour of a thirty years old original copy of a registered deed which is submitted in the court from proper custody. For proper appreciation Section 90 of the Evidence Act is reproduced below: 
"90. Presumption as to documents thirty years old: Where any document, purporting or proved to be thirty years old, is produced from any custody which the Court in the particular case considers proper, the Court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document, which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person, is in that person's handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, that it was duly executed and attested by the persons by whom it purports to be executed and attested.
  
23. From the provisions of above mentioned Section of the Evidence Act it appears that the exhibited copy of thirty years old registered document dated 05.01.1923 is being an original copy and produced before the court from proper custody as such the presumption infavour of deed no.112 dated 05.01.1923 is that the said deed is a genuine one. In such a situation the onus of proof of the allegation of the plaintiffs regarding lending money by taking signature in blank stamp and thereafter used the same to create forged document by the predecessor of the defendant nos.67 and 68 lies upon the plaintiffs. 

24. PW-1 though deposed that Shushila Sundari and Rajani Tanta were joteder and lend money by taking signature in blank stamp and thereafter used the same to create forged documents but failed to prove his contention by adducing evidence rather stated in his cross: 
“সুশীলা ও রজনীকান্ডের সুদের ব্যবসার কোন কাগজ দেখাতে পারব না। তাদেরকে আমি দেখি নাই । তাহাদের ব্যবসা বাণিজ্য বা চাষ বাস সম্পর্কে আমার ব্যাক্তিগত জ্ঞান নাই। টাকা ধার নেওয়ার কোন কাগজিক প্রমাণ নাই। সাদা স্ট্যান্ডে সহি নেওয়ার কথা মানুষের মুখে শুনেছি। সুশিলা ও রজনী কেমন ধরনের লোক ছিল আমার জানা নেই।”

25. Furthermore, PW-2 and PW-3 did not adduce any evidence to that effect. Thus, it appears that plaintiffs failed to prove such claim by corroborative evidence. 

26. Again, on perusal of registered deed dated 05.01.1923 (exhibit-Kha) it appears that Abdul, Azim, Sabu, Asmat and Jasmat together sold 22 bighas and 6.75 kathas of Land to Shush la SundAri And thus the original owner Abdul, Azim and Sabu admitted the title of Asmat and Jasmat and therefore the plaintiffs cannot deny the title of the defendants who are the heirs of Shushila Sundari. Moreover, registered deed dated 05.01.1923 executed infavour of Shushila Sundari by the vendors Azim, Abdul, Sabu alongwith Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah (purchaser of the land vide deed dated 09.06.1917) clearly proves that the registered deed dated 09.06.1917 was acted upon on payment of debt of the ex-landlord as per condition of the deed dated 09.06.19.17. Thus, the claim of the plaintiffs that the condition attached to the deed dated 09.06.1917 (exhibit-Ka) was not complied with lies upon the plaintiffs. But the High Court Division without considering legal and factual aspect of the suit arrived at an erroneous decision that the claim regarding noncompliance of the condition of paying debt of Tk.450/- is upon the defendants. 

27. From the discussions made above, we find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellants that the High Court Division committed an error of law by shifting the burden of proof upon the defendant-appellants. 

28. We have also perused the statements of the witnesses examined by the parties. PW-1 in his chief deposed that:

“শর্ত ছিল যে, জমিদারের রেহানী দেনা ৪৫০ টাকা পরিশোধ করিবে ও দাতাদের দায়মুক্ত করিবে । কিন্তু আসমত ও জসমত সেই দেনা পরিশোধ করে নাই।”

29, But failed to adduce any corroborative evidence in support of said deposition. So, it appears that plaintiffs have failed to prove the burden which was upon them. 

30. From the aforementioned discussions, we are of the view that since the suit land was purchased by Shushila Sundari before C.S. operation, the C.S. record should have been prepared in her name. Again, on perusal of exhibit-'neo' i.e. M.R.R. khatian no.15 it appears that said khaitian was prepared in the name of Shushila Sundari in continuation of kabala dated 09.06.1917 and 05.01.1923 which are marked as exhibit-la' and ‘kha' respectively, as such said M.R.R khatian was prepared correctly. From the contents of kabala dated 18.06.1080 (exhibit-'pa') and another kabala also dated 18.06.1980 (exhibit-' fa' it appears that defendant no.69 purchased portion of the suit land from the heirs of Shushila Sundari. Thus Trial Court justly arrived at a finding that plaintiffs have failed to prove their title in the suit land. 

31. Now let's discuss regarding possession. PW-2 Md. Nabir Uddin Akandh was the relative of the plaintiff but fated to assert that the plaintiffs possess the suit land. PW-3 Md. Tomir Uddin Pramanik, also the relative of the plaintiffs, deposed that: 
“নাঃ জমির দাগ, খতিয়ান, পরিমান ও চৌহদ্দি বলতে পারব না। কে কোন দাগে কতটুকু দখল করে বলতে পারব না। নাঃ গ্রামের কোন কোন জমি নিয়ে মামলা  হচ্ছে বলতে পারব না।---
বাদীরা কতটুকু জমি দখল করে বলতে পারব না”

32. From the above, it appears that the witnesses produced by the plaintiffs are not independent witnesses and their testimony does not prove possession of the plaintiffs. Furthermore, plaintiffs failed to produce any documentary evidences to prove their claim regarding possession. 

33. On the other hand, DW-1 deposed in his testimony in support of their claim of possession. DW-2, 3 and 4 deposed in support of possession of the predecessor of the defendants over the suit land. 

34. DW-2 Md. Mojibor Rahman deposed in his chief: 
“বাদী ও ৬৭-৬৮নং বিবাদীদের চিনি। ৬৮নং বিবাদী রাজলক্ষ্মীর নিকট হতে আমি ৭৬ শতক জমি ২ দলিলে খরিদ করি। উক্ত দলিল ২টি আদালতে আমি উক্ত খরিদা হমি ভোগ দখল করি। বাদী এবং অন্যান্য বিবাদী উক্ত জমি দখল করে না। রাজলক্ষ্মী অবশিষ্ট সম্পত্তি দখল করে ।”

35. DW-3 Osman Ali Fakir deposed that: 
“বাদী বিবাদীদের চিনি। মামলার জমিও চিনি। নালিশী জমির মাঠে কাজ-কাম করি এজন্য চিনি। নালিশা জমি রাধারাণী ও রাজলক্ষমী ভোগ দখল করেছে। তারা বর্গা দিয়ে দখল করেছে ও করে।

36. He denied the suggestion made by the plaintiffs that Radharani never possessed the suit land, 

37. DW-4 Md. Younus Ali Fakir deposed that: 
“আমি নালিশা জোট মধ্যে ৪০% ও ৮০% দুই খন্ড জমি গোপাল দাসের অধীনে বর্গা করি। গোপাল রাজলম্ষ্মীর ছেলে । সে বর্গা দখল দেয়।”

38. He denied the suggestion in his cross that the plaintiffs possessed the suit land. 

39. Plaintiffs could not shaken the witnesses of the defendants in cross examination. 

40. Kabala dated 09.07.1923 (exhibit-'ga') proves that the predecessor-in-inter-est of the plaintiffs cultivated the suit land as bargadar of Shushila Sundari i.e. the predecessor-in-interest of the defendants and thus they admitted possession of the defendant's predecessor-in-interest. Moreover, defendants filed rent receipts (exhibit-'n' and 1n-1') in support of their possession. 

41. From the discussions made above, we are of the view that the defendants have been able to prove their possession. 

42. It is to be noted that the view of the trial court regarding the credibility of the witnesses has a great weight and should not be lightly discarded inasmuch as trial court have the opportunity to evaluate the demeanour of the witnesses at the time of recording of evidences. 

43. In the case of State vs. M M Rafiqul Ryder, reported in 45 DLR (AD) (1993) 13, this Division observed: 
"It is well-settled that when a finding of fact is based upon the credibility of evidence involving the appreciation of the demeanour of witnesses, the view of the trial court is entitled to great weight and should not be lightly discarded." 

44. Cardinal principle in civil litigation is that plaintiffs have to prove their case and weakness of the defendants is not a ground to decree the suit. In ex-parte hearing plaintiffs also have to prove their case through proper evidences. 

45. in the present suit plaintiffs hopelessly failed to prove their title as well as possession over the suit land. Since the finding of the trial court is based on proper appreciation of evidence on record, thus the same should not be discarded lightly. 

46. From the above discussions and the principle enunciated in the cited case, we are of the view that the High Court Division failed to arrive at a correct decision appreciating facts and circumstances of the case as well as provisions of the Evidence Act which requires interference by this Division and as such we are inclined to allow this appeal. 

47. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. 

48. The impugned judgment and decree dated 02.05.2010 passed by the High Court Division is set-aside and the judgment and decree dated 28.02.2000 passe4 by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nu Court, Bogra, is hereby restored. 

49. No order as to costs. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 07.05.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.10268 of 2007)
full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman J. This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 07.05.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.10268 of 2007 making the Rule absolute and declaring the Memo No. ওঃপ্রঃ/গুঃশা৩/৪৫২(৩) dated 01.10.2007 in respect of the respondent No.1 herein as writ petitioner's property of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate bearing E.C. No.1690 is illegal, without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

2. Facts leading, to filing of this civil appeal, is abort, are that the writ petitioner filed the Writ Petition No.IO268 of 2007 before the High Court Division challenging the order dated 30.09.2007 passed under the signature of the writ respondent No.2 contained in Memo No. ওঃপ্রঃ/গুঃশা৩/৪৫২(৩) dated 01.10.2007 in respect of the property-Waqf Estate being E.C. No.1690 stating that the writ petitioner was the Mutwalli of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate being E. C. No.1690 and this Waqf was created by the Waqfnama executed by Azizur Rahman and the same was enrolled in the Office of the respondent No.l. The Waqf deed No. 5303 was executed on 22.03.1928 and since then the properties mentioned in the schedule of the Waqf deed is managed, possessed and controlled by Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate. There is another Waqf Estate in the locality known as Abdaul Gani Waqf Estate and the deed was executed on 22.03.1928 bearing deed No.1402 and its E.C. No.2059. On 18.5.2006, the respondent No.3 filed an application to respondent No.1 praying for exclusion of the property of schedule No.1 of Waqf Deed No.5303 being E.C. No.1690 of Azizur Rahman Waqf Estate and for inclusion of the same property in the Waqf deed No.1402 of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate being E.C. No.2059 in the schedule 11 of that Waqf Estate. Then the respondent No.1 through his Inspector of Chattogram Office issued a memo, dated 12.07.2006 directing the Mutwalli of Abdul Gani Waqf Estate to attend the Office of the Inspector of Chattogram and direction also was given to the writ petitioner to attend on 25.07.2006. Accordingly, the writ petitioner attended the Inspector's Office and also took part in the proceeding. The inquiry was held by the Inspector of Chattogram Office as per direction of the writ respondent No.1 under Memo dated 04.07.2006. Upon receiving the report of the Inspector, hearing was held in the Office of writ respondent No. 1. The writ petitioner produced the necessary documents and also submitted written arguments in support of his case. After hearing of the parties, the writ respondent No.2 in a lengthy order dated 30.09.2007 passed order for correction of schedule of Waqf document and the property in question was ordered to be treated as property of Waqf Estate bearing E.C. No. 2059. This order was passed by the writ respondent No.2 under section 49 of the Waqf Ordinance. Therefore, challenging the said order, the writ petitioner finding no other alternative efficacious remedy moved the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule Nisi. 

3. The writ-respondent Nos.1 and 3 contested the Rule Nisi by filing affidavit-in-opposition.

11. We will examine the materials on record as to whether judgment and order of High. Court Division is justified or erred which calls for interference by this Division.  

12. The origin of Waqf is to the direct prescriptions, of the Prophet (Sm) Ibn Omer as stated in the Jamaa ut Tirmizi that “Omer (R:)had acquired a piece of land in (the canton of) Khaibar, and proceeded to the Prophet (Sm) and sought his counsel, to make the most pious use of it, (where- upon) the Prophet (Sm) declared, ‘tie up’ the property (asl or corpus) and devote the usufruct to human beings, and it is not to be sold or made the subject of gift or inheritance; devote its produce to your children, your kindred, and the poor in the way of God. In accordance with this rule Omer dedicated the property, in question, and the Waqf contained in existence for several centuries until the land became wastage. (relied on Commentaries on Mbhommedan Law by Amir Ali Syed). 

13. According to Imam Abu Hanifa the meaning of Waqf is the detention of a specific thing in the ownership of Waqf and the devoting of its profit or products “in charity of poor or other good objects”. Imam Abu Yusuf said, “Waqf signifies the extinction of the Waqif’s ownership in the thing dedicated and detention of all thing in the implied ownership of the Almighty Allah, in such a manner that is profits may revert to or be applied ‘for the benefit of Mankind.’  

14. Three basic principles governed the Waqf: the trust was required to be irrevocable, perpetual, and inalienable. Once property was declared Waqf by its owner, the trust thereby created was irrevocable. It means (i) inalienable lands used for charitable purposes and (ii) pious endowments.  

15. The origin of Waqf can be traced to the impulse of Muslims to do charitable deeds i.e., to endow property ‘in the way of the Almighty Allah’. According to Section 2(1) of the Mussalman Waqf Validating Act, 1913 “Waqf’ means the permanent dedication by a person professing the Mussalman faith of any property for any purpose recognized by the Mussalman Law as religious, pious or charitable. According to section 6(10)of the Bengal Waaf Act, 1934 “Wagqf’ means the permanent dedication by a person professing Islam of any movable or immovable property for any purpose recognized by the Islamic Law as pious, religious or charitable and includes a Waqf of by user.  

16. The Waqf is irrevocable after possession is handed over to the Mutawalli. The Waqif divests himself of the ownership of the property and of everything in the nature of contract from the moment the waqf is created.  

17. In purely metaphorical sense the expression “ownership of God” is used but unlike Hindu Law, since conception of a personal God is not recognized, there is no ownership of God or no property belonged to God in the Jural sense, although the ownerships of the property becomes reverted in God because God is originally owner of all thing.  

18. From the recital of Waqf deed it appears that the object, for which the property in question has been dedicated, is charitable, pious or religious in nature and a portion of the usufructs should be used by the descendents. Therefore, the dedication was complete and it could not be divested for any other purposes. Therefore, when a property can be used only for religious or charitable purpose, it acquires a permanent character. The Waqf property vests in the implied ownership of the Almighty in the sense that nobody can claim ownership of it. Even in Wagqf al aulad, the property is dedicated to the Almighty and only the usufructs are used by the descendents. Once the property is given to Waqf, it remains for the Waqf forever. The property cannot be alienated or transferred nor is it subject to the rights of inheritance. It cannot be sold or given away to anybody except in accordance with law. The Islamic Law is a sacred Law, and, thus transaction, or obligation is measured by the standards of religious and moral rules. Those rules are developed through analogical reasoning by Muslim Jurists. When ownership of the Waqf property is relinquished by the Waqfi it cannot be acquired by any other person, rather, it is arrested or detained. In Section 56 of the Bangladesh Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 Mutawalli’s power of alienation of Waqf property has been restricted like section 53 of the Bengal Waqf Act, 1934, where the bar to transfer of immovable property of a Waqf was provided. 

19. Section 49 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 reads as follows: 
“Power to cause enrolment of waqf and to amend register 
49. The Administrator, on his own motion or on the petition of any person interested, verified in the manner referred to in sub section (8) of section 47, may direct a mutawalli to apply for the enrolment of a waqf or to supply any information regarding a waqf, or may himself collect such information, and may cause any waqf to be enrolled, or may at any time amend the register of Waqfs.” 

20. Which means that the Waqf Administrator may at any time amend the register of Waqfs and on perusal of the impugned order along with the judgment and order of the High Court Division it is ordinarily understood that the High Court Division committed error in not considering that the mandate of the section 49 of the Waqfs Ordinance which empowered the Waqf Administrator to correct the register of Waqfs.

20. Lands to be retained in the possession of rent-receivers, cultivating raiyats, cultivating under-raiyats and non-agricultural tenants- (5) (i) Nothing in sub-sections (1) (2) and (3) of the section shall apply- (b) ----------

আজিজর রহমান পিং মৃত আশরপ আলী-১ একটা কাহিং বেতন সাং-বাকলিয়া পাইবে ২য় মতোয়াল্লীর অবর্তমানে তাহার নিজ ওয়াকফ এষ্টেটে যে ব্যক্তি মতোয়াল্লী হইবে সেই ব্যক্তি এই ওয়াকফ এষ্টেইট এ ২য় মতোয়ারী পদে আপাট্য ক্রম থাকিবে, কারণ ২য় মতোয়াল্লী আমার বহু কালীনে কার্যকারক হয় সে ওয়াকফর সম্পত্তির জমি জমার অবস্থিত ও বিবরণ এবং সীমা পরিচয় মামলা মোকদ্দমার ইত্যাদির বিষয় অতি ভাল অবগত আছে তাহার তোলনায আমি কিছু জানি না বিশেষতঃ আমার অবর্তমানে ওয়াকফ শর্ত মতে স্ত্রী লোক ছাড়া পুরুষ মতোরাল্লী হইতে পারে আমার ওয়ারিশগণের মধ্যে এমন কেহ নাই। অহেতু ২য় মতোয়াল্লী বিশেষ দরকার লিং শ্রী আজিজুর রহমান পিং মৃত আশরাফ আলী । 

26. Azizur Rahman is also a deed writer of Waqf Nama of Abdul Gani.” 

27. In view of such law, it is apparent on the face of the record, that by dint of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the tenant of Waqf Estate cannot claim the ownership of a property as a tenant. 

28. Moreso, there is a legal bar to transfer of immovable property of a Waaf Estate by any of mutawalli under sections 56(1)(2)(3)(4) and (5) of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. 1 of 1962). It runs as follows:  
CHAPTER VI 
TRANSFER OF WAQF PROPER- TIES Bar to transfer of immovable property of a waqf 
56. (i)No transfer by a mutawalli of any immovable property of a waqf by way of sale, gift, mortgage or exchange, or by way of lease for a term exceeding 5 years shall be valid without the previous sanction of the Administrator: Provided that the sanction by the Administrator shall not validate any transfer which is contravention of any law for the time being in force or is otherwise invalid. 
(2) No Court shall grant permission to any Receiver appointed by the Court for the transfer of any waqf property unless the prior sanction of the Administrator has been obtained. 
(3) In the absence of the sanction required by sub-section (1), any transfer made by a mutawalli shall be declared void, if the Administrator, within 4 months of his coming to know of such transfer, or within 3 years from the date of such transfer, whichever is later, applies to the Civil court this behalf.  
(4) Where a mutawalli transfer a waqf property in contravention of sub section (1) and afterwards himself becomes the owner of the property, the mutawalli shall, on the direction of the Administrator, re convey the property to the waaf.  
(5) Any transfer made in contravention of the provisions of sub section (1) shall be deemed to be an act of malfeasance and breach of trust for the purpose of sub-section (1) of Section 32.  
57. A mutawalli or a Receiver may apply to the Administrator for sanction to transfer waqf property under sub section (1) of section 56, and the Administrator, after making such enquiry and giving notice to such persons in such manner as he thinks fit and hearing them, if they desire to be heard, may accord sanction to such transfer on such terms and conditions as he may, in his discretion, impose: Provided that where such transfer is to be made under an express power conferred by the waqf deed, the Administrator shall not refuse to accord sanction.  
Sub-registrar not to register deeds. 
17[57A.(1) Notwithstanding anything contained to the contrary in the Registration Act, 1908 (Act No. XVI of 1908), no Sub-Registrar shall register any deed of transfer of any immovable property belonging to a waqf, without the previous sanction of the Administrator or the Government, as the case may be. (2) If a Sub-Registrar, knowingly and intentionally, registers a deed in violation of the prohibition under sub-section (1), he shall be liable for commission of the offence of abetment of criminal breach of trust.” 

29. As long as the said decree having not been yet varied or altered, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not maintainable and cannot be sustained in law. 

30. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed. No order as to costs. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 09.02.2003 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.296 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman J. This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 09.02.2003 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No:296 of 1999 making the Rule absolute, and, thereby, setting aside the judgment and-decree dated 29.09.1998 passed by the District Judge, Cox's Bazar in Other Appeal No:59 of 1945 (heard analogously with other Appeal No.86 of 1995) dismissing the appeal, and, thereby, partly decreeing the suit by setting aside the judgment and decree dated 29.06.1995 passed by the Sub-Ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Cox's Bazar in Other Suit No.193 of 1994 decreeing the suit. 

2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No.14 of 1988 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now joint District Judge), Cox's Bazar against the defendants for declaration of title to the second schedule land, and, for declaration that Memo No.31-1/87/1983 dated 29.10.1987 issued by the signature of the defendant No.1 and Memo No.159/1/S.A. dated 28.01.1988 issued by the defendant No.2, are Void, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for other reliefs. The Other Suit No.14 of 1988 was transferred to the Court of Subordiante Judge, Court No.2, Cox's Bazar and re-numbered as Other Suit No.193 of 1994.  

3. The suit properties measuring 38.59 acres belonged to four brothers, namely, Purna Chandra Chowdhury, Rashik Chandra Chowdhury, Bama Charan Chowdhury and Sashi Kumer Chowdhury, and, the R.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared, and, finally published in their names, and, they were in possession. They verbally settled 28.9425 acres of land to their relation Sukumar Biswas @ Sukomoy Biswas, Sunil Bikash Sen, Mihir Kanti Das & Sachindra Nath Guha in the year 1940, and, the remaining ½th share measuring 9.6475 acres remained with the said original owners. The further case; is that, the names of the settlement holders Sukumar Biswas, @ Sukamoy Biswas, Sunil Bikash Sen, Mihir Xanti Das, and, Sachindra Nath Guha were recorded in the R.S. Khatian, and, while in possession, they transferred the suit land by 10 kabalas dated 22.04.1978, 03.04.1978 and 09.04.1978 measuring 9.88 acres in favour of the plaintiffs, but, the defendant Government forfeited the suit land belonging to the plaintiffs to the extent of 7.40 acres by issuing the alleged notices dated 27.01.1988 and 29.01.1987 respectively. Hence is the suit. Subsequently, defendant Not.5-11 by filing application got themselves added in the suit.  

4. The defendant Nos.1-4 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that, under the President Order No.96 of 1972, the owners Gouranga Prashad Chowdhury filed L.R. Statement of 6.87 acres of land, unil Bikash Sen 1.25, Sukumar Biswas @ Sukamoy Biswas 1.24 and Mihir Kanti Das 1.24, Sachindra Nath 1.24, Pranab Das 9.65 in all 21.29 acres, and, the remaining 2.41 acres were surrendered to the Government. The further case, is that, the Government forfeited 7.40 acres of land, and, the tenants surrendered 2.81 acres of land, and, thus, the said forfeited, 7.40 acres of land, and, surrendered 2.81 acres belonged to the Government, and, was recorded in the Khas khatiaa of the Government.  

5. The defendant Nos.5-11 also contested the suit by filing a separate written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alias, that, the suit is not maintainable, and, the suit has got no cause of actions. The suit land originally belonged to Purna Chandra Chowdhury, Bama Charan chowdhury, Rashik Chandra Chowdhury and, Shashi Kumar Chowdhury, and, R.S. Khatian No.451 was finally prepared in their names. Thereafter, Purna Chandra died, and his 4 anas share devolved upon his son Sateyndra Bijoy Roy Chowdhury, Rasik Chandra died, and whose shares devolved on his son Upendra, Lal, and, after his death, his son Gouranga Prashad Chowdhury. The defendants stated that, R.S. recorded tenant Barra Charan Chowdhury died, and his share devolved upon his 2 sons Surendra Bijoy Chy and Tejendra Lal Chowdhury, and R.S. tenant Shashi Kumar gifted away 2.89 acres of land to his son Dhirendra Roy Chowdhury and, his brother-in-law Pranab Das on 25.06.1967. The defendants stated that, Sateyndra Roy Chowdhury and Tejendra Lal Chowdhury sold away 7.00 acres of the suit schedule land, and, other land in favour of Pranab Das dated 25.06.1967. The defendants stated that, while Pranab Das has been holding possession of the suit land for more than statutory period of limitation, he sold away the suit land to the defendant Nos.6-8 and to the extent of 3.68 acres on 12.03.1986 and on 05.03.1986 to the defendant Nos.6-8 and to others to the extent of 3.63 acres and on 12:03.1986 to the defendant No.5 and others and on 10.03.1986 to the defendant Nos.9-11 and others to the extent of 3.66 acres. The defendants stated that, after having purchased the suit land, they have been holding peaceful possession of the suit land by paying regular rent thereof. The defendants alleged that, M.R.R. Khatian No.637 was prepared wrongly in the name of Sukumar Biswas and others. The defendants denied right, title, interest and possession of the Plaintiffs in the suit land and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.  

6. On conclusion of the trial, the Trial Court, considering the evidences and documents on record, decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 29.06.1995.  

7. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree of the Trial Court; the defendant Nos.1- 4 as appellants preferred Tile Appeal No.86 of 1995 and the defendant Nos.5-11 as appellants preferred Other Appeal No .59 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar, who, heard both the appeal analogously, and, on consideration of the evidence on record found that the notices issued by the defendant Nos.1 and 2 to the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land are void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The District Judge, however, found that, the plaintiffs did not acquire any title in the 2nd schedule of the suit land. Accordingly, by the judgment and decree dated 29.09.1998, the learned District Judge dismissed both the said appeal and thereby, setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit in part. 

8. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 29.09.1998 passed by the learned District Judge, Cox's Bazar, the plaintiffs-respondents as petitioners preferred Civil Revision No.296 of 1999 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule. 

9. In due course, a Single Bench of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 09.02.2003 and thereby set aside the judgment and decree dated 29.09.1998 passed by the District Judge; Cox's Bazar in Other Appeal No.59 bf 1995 and restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

10. Feeling aggrieved, by the impugned judgment and order dated 09.02.2003 passed the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.296 of 1999, the defendant Nos.1-4 as petitioners herein preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1183 of 2004 before this Division and obtained leave, which, gave rise to the instant appeal. 

11. Md. Md. Zahangir Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that, the Court of Appeal below having found that, the vendors of the plaintiffs submitted statement making incorrect declaration regarding quantum of land in their possession, the suit land was liable to be stand forfeited to the Government and the Trial Court relying on the proviso to Article 8 of P.O. 98 of 1972, which was omitted by Article 7 of P.6:138 of 1972 erroneously held that, the suit and is not liable to be forfeited. The Court of Appeal below rightly arrived at the conclusion that, the plaintiffs acquired no title on the basis of their purchase, but, the High court Division erred in law in failing to take into consideration the effect of omission of the proviso to Article 8 of P.0.98 of 1972. He further submits that, the High Court Division has reversed the judgment of the Appellate Court without adverting to the findings of the Court of Appeal below that, the vendors of the plaintiffs submitted statement making incorrect declaration regarding quantum of land in their possession, and thereby, committed an error of law, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside, and, as such, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed. 

12. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned, Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.1-6 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that, the plaintiffs having purchased the suit lands by registered instruments have acquired good title in the suit land, and the same is not liable to be forfeited under President's Order No.98 of 1972, and therefore, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He further submits that, the learned District Judge having found that, the impugned notices are illegal and without jurisdiction, it follows that the forfeiture of the suit land has not been Validity made, and, consequently, the acquisition of title in the land by the plaintiffs by registered instruments cannot be said to be invalid. He next submits that, the present suit relates to the declaration of title on 9.88 acres of land, which is much less than one hundred standard Bighas, and, the plaintiffs are not required to submits any statement in the prescribed form, and the lands held by the plaintiffs being not in excess of one hundred standard Bighas is not liable to be forfeited to the Government, and, so the omission of the proviso to, Article 8 of the President's Order No.98 of 1972 did not affect the title of the plaintiffs acquired by registered instruments as the land is much less than one hundred standard Bighas, and, therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division with regard to the plaintiffs' title to the suit land is sustainable in law. He finally submits that, the land being 9.88 acres not having been belonged to the previous owner after transfer to the plaintiff, the said lands not liable to be forfeited to the Government, and, as such, the High Court Division rightly passed the impugned judgment and order, and, therefore, he prays for dismissal the instant appeal. 

13. We have heard learned Deputy Attorney General for the appellants, and, the learned Senior Advocate for the respondent Nos.1-6. Perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected materials on record. 

14. Leave was granted to examine the submissions made by the learned Deputy Attorney General for the appellants are quoted below: 
"The learned Deputy Attorney General submits that the court of appeal below having found that the vendors of the plaintiffs submitted statement making incorrect declaration regarding quantum of land in their possession, the suit land was liable to be stand forfeited to the government and the trial court relying on the proviso to Article 8 of P.O. 98 of 1972 which was omitted by Article 7 of P.O. 138 of 1972 erroneously held that the suit land is not liable to be forfeited. The court of appeal below rightly arrived at the conclusion that the plaintiffs acquired no title on the basis of their purchase but the High Court Division erred in law in failing to take into consideration the effect of omission of the proviso to Article 8 of P.O. 98 of 1972. He next submits that the High Court Division has reversed the judgment of the appellate court without adverting to the findings of the court of appeal below that the vendors of the plaintiffs submitted statement making incorrect declaration regarding quantum of land in their possession and thereby committed an error of law." 

15. At this juncture, let us scrutinize whether these submissions are worthy of merit consideration. 

16. Both of the Trial Court as well as the Appellate Court, as the only court of facts, reached on concurrent findings that impugned memos as exhibited as nos. V and V(1)are bad for aunt of jurisdiction as such these are void and without lawful authority. These two memos was issued under Article 8 of the Bangladesh Land Holding (Limitation) Order, 1972 (PRESIDENT'S ORDER no. 98 of 1972), ceiling of land laws enforced in this land and the appellants-defendants forfeited the suit lands in favour of the Government by dint of these two memos. The plaintiffs acquired title on the basis of their purchases (exhibit no. 9 series) which are not controversial and the deeds are proved as valid. If so, then, we find no reasons as why the respondents-plain-tiffs would not get a declaration of title over the suit land as the same was not actually forfeited in the eye of. 

17. The Appellate Court's decision as to the dismissal of the suit as far as it concerns the declaration of title is bad in law as it finds that the impediment behind the unsuccessfulness of the suit i.e. the impugned memos, itself void and without lawful Authority. Because, as per the Article 8 of the PRESIDENT'S ORDER no. 98 of 1972 If any head of a family or body falls, without any reasonable cause, to submit the statement required under Article 7, within the time mentioned therein or willfully makes any omission from, or incorrect declaration in, the statement submitted by him under that Article, he shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand take, or with both and the land for which no statement has been submitted or which has been omitted from the statement or in respect of which the incorrect declaration has been made may be, forfeited to the Government. Here the key word is "may be", that moans it is not forfeited ipso facto, rather it is incumbent upon the discretion of the Government as to whether they forfeit it or not. In the present case, the Government decided to forfeit, how-ever, the instruments through which they forfeited the suit land were declared unlawful by the Appellate Court. 

18. In addition, we too concur with the findings of the High Court Division that before applying any of the provisions of President's Order No.98 of 1972 there must be a clean finding that the head of every family hold land in excess of hundred standard Bighas. In the present case we do not find any finding by either the trial court or by the final court of fact that the plaintiffs holding land more than hundred standard Bighas so that the provisions of president order No. 98 of 1972 may be invoked and the land holding by them in excess of hundred standard Bighas shall be forfeited. The suit land is measured as 9.88 Acres which is equivalent to 29.887 Bighas (1 Acre = 3.025 standard Bighs), that is well underneath the ceiling of 100 standard Bighas. 

19. Therefore, we are of the considered view that the arguments advanced for the appeal are less than are merit worthy. 

20. Before parting with the matters one thing caught our sight and that is the issue of awarding costs of the suit by all of the courts below i.e. Trial Court, the Appellate Court and the High Court Division. 

21. Section 35 of the Code of Civil procedure, 1908 is as follows: 
"35.(1) Subject to such conditions and limitations as may be prescribed, and to the provisions of any law for the time being in force, the costs of and incident to all suits shall be in the discretion of the Court, and the Court shall have full power to deter-mine by whom or out of what property and to what extent such costs are to be paid, and to give all necessary directions for the purposes aforesaid. The fact that the Court has no jurisdiction to try the suit shall be no bar to the exercise of such powers. 
(2) Where the Court directs that any costs shall not follow the event, the Court shall state its reasons in writing. 
(3) The Court may give interest on costs at any rate not exceeding six per cent, per annum, and such interest shall be added to the costs and shall be recoverable as such." 

22. From a plain and simple reading of the section it is evident that awarding costs is mandatory and the rule is that it shall follow the event that is the result, which means, the losing party shall bear the costs and where the Court directs that any costs shall not follow the event, the Court shall state its reasons in writing. As there is consequence of the rule, it is not directory rather Mandatory. 

23. In the case of Harendra Math Mukherji and Ors. vs. Bari Pada Mukherji and Ors. reported in AIR 1939 Cal 387 their lordships opined that "As regards the costs the accepted principle is that posts shall follow the event unless the successful party is guilty of misconduct or there is other good cause for depriving him of it." 

24. In this concern we can recollect the invaluable words of Justice V R Krishna Iyer of Indian Supreme Court articulated in the case of Kali Prasad Singh vs. Ram Prasad Singh and Ors. reported in AIR 1974 SC 14B as to that: 
The learned District Judge was, therefore, right and the learned Single Judge in the High Court was clerly wrong. The appeal succeeds. It is unfortunate that this litigation which has stood an exhausting length of 17 years with alternating fortunes finds the parties out of pocket to considerably more than perhaps the value of the properties themselves, but this sad note on litigation in India cannot deflect us from the rule that costs must follow the event. The appeal is allowed with costs. " 

25. However, in the present case, without assigning any reasons as required, the Trial Court in decreeing the suit "without any cost" surely fails to comply to with the mandatory provision. In this point the Appellate Court dictated that "Considering the circumstances of the suit there is no order as to costs. The par-ties will bear their own costs" and the High Court Division dictated in the same fashion-"In the facts of the case I do not make any order as to costs". In our opinion, the phrases used by the Appellate Court and the High Court Division "the circumstances of the suit" and "facts of the case" respectively connote no actual sense. It is not understandable what are the circumstances or facts of the case that provoked them as to not to comply with the mandatory rules. It is the lawful right of the winning party to a civil suit/case to be awarded the costs and court cannot whimsically deny them such rights especially, in our civil courts which are burdened with thousands of pending 'tests suit' or false cases. Applying this rule by all of the civil courts could afford a bit of breathing space for the overburdened civil courts as well as the actual litigant people. However, this Division possesses an cxtra-ordinary prerogative under Article 104 of the Constitution to do any-thing for complete justice. As both of the parties involved fought the legal battle dragging it upto the Apex Court, we think that both of the parties affected equally, consequently, in our opinion, no order as to cost will be justified. 

26. Accordingly, this appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. 

End.
